definition_zh: 有弹性的；受力后能恢复原状的；可变通、可伸缩的；橡皮筋；弹性织物
definition_en: able to return to its original shape after being stretched or pressed; able to change or be interpreted freely
core_image: 一根被拉到两倍长的橡皮筋，松手的一刻立刻弹回原来长度，表面还留着拉伸过的细纹
scene: 物理课上，老师把一根橡皮筋拉到极限再松手，全班看着它缩回原长。The elastic band snapped back to its original length the moment she released it.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项：材料受力变形后能恢复原来的形状；句意为她松手的那一刻，橡皮筋立刻弹回原长。图中可辨识物件：拉长的皮筋、两只手、刻度尺、记录本。

pos.zh: 有弹性的；能恢复原状的；可伸缩、可变通的
橡皮筋；松紧带；弹性织物

derivatives.zh: 无弹性的；不随价格变动的

senses.title: A material that springs back
senses.titleCN: 受力后弹回原状的材料
senses.definition: able to return to its original shape after being stretched, squeezed or bent
senses.definitionCN: 被拉伸、挤压或弯曲之后能够恢复原来形状的
senses.example: The elastic band snapped back to its original length.
senses.exampleCN: 橡皮筋弹回了原来的长度。
senses.why: The Greek word behind it described metal that could be beaten out and would spring back, so recovery of shape is the oldest layer.
senses.whyCN: 它背后的希腊词描述的是能被锤打延展、又会弹回的金属，因此「恢复形状」是最古老的一层。

senses.title: A stretchy loop or strip
senses.definition: a strip or loop of rubber or similar material, used to hold things together or keep clothing snug
senses.definitionCN: 橡胶或类似材料做成的条状或环状物，用来捆扎物品或让衣物贴身
senses.example: She bound the rolled posters with an elastic.
senses.exampleCN: 她用一根橡皮筋捆住卷好的海报。
senses.why: Once the adjective had named the material, the material itself took the same word as a noun.
senses.whyCN: 形容词先给这种材料命名，材料本身随后就用同一个词作名词。

senses.title: A light, springy movement
senses.definition: moving with a quick, springy ease, as if the body were made of rubber
senses.definitionCN: 动作轻快、带弹跳感，仿佛身体是橡胶做的
senses.example: He crossed the court with an elastic stride.
senses.exampleCN: 他以轻快而有弹性的步幅穿过球场。
senses.why: A body that recovers its shape quickly looks light, so the material property was lent to movement.
senses.whyCN: 能迅速恢复形状的身体看上去轻快，于是材料的属性被借去描述动作。

senses.title: A rule that can be stretched
senses.titleCN: 可变通、可宽泛解释的规则
senses.definition: able to be changed, widened or reinterpreted without losing its identity
senses.definitionCN: 可以被改动、放宽或重新解释而不失其本来性质的
senses.example: The deadline is elastic if the client adds more work.
senses.exampleCN: 如果客户增加工作，截止期是可以变通的。
senses.why: Something that stretches and returns keeps its identity, which is exactly what a flexible rule does.
senses.whyCN: 能拉伸又复原的东西保持同一身份，可变通的规则正是如此。

senses.title: Demand that moves with price
senses.titleCN: 随价格明显变动的需求
senses.definition: in economics, changing by a larger proportion than the price change that caused it
senses.definitionCN: 在经济学中，变动幅度大于引起它的价格变动幅度的
senses.example: Luxury goods often show elastic demand.
senses.exampleCN: 奢侈品往往呈现弹性需求。
senses.why: Economists borrowed the material word for a quantity that stretches when price pulls it.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家借这个材料词，指被价格一拉就会伸缩的数量。

senses.title: A collision that keeps its energy
senses.definition: in physics, describing a collision in which the total kinetic energy is conserved
senses.definitionCN: 在物理学中，描述总动能保持不变的碰撞
senses.example: Billiard balls make an almost elastic collision.
senses.exampleCN: 台球之间的碰撞近乎弹性碰撞。
senses.why: The bodies deform and spring back, so little kinetic energy leaves as heat.
senses.whyCN: 物体先变形再弹回，很少有动能以热的形式散失。

senses.title: The point where springing back stops
senses.definition: the greatest stress a material can take and still return to its original shape
senses.definitionCN: 材料能承受而仍可恢复原状的最大应力
senses.example: Bend the rod past its elastic limit and it stays bent.
senses.exampleCN: 把杆弯过弹性极限，它就保持弯曲。
senses.why: The word marks the boundary of its own promise: beyond that point the material no longer springs back.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标出自身承诺的边界：越过那一点，材料就不再弹回。

senses.title: A clause that can expand
senses.titleCN: 可扩张解释的宪法条款
senses.definition: in American law, a clause worded broadly enough to let Congress use powers not listed
senses.definitionCN: 美国法律中措辞宽泛、允许国会行使未列明权力的条款
senses.example: The elastic clause let Congress regulate new technologies.
senses.exampleCN: 弹性条款让国会得以监管新技术。
senses.why: A clause written in general words can be stretched to cover cases its authors never named.
senses.whyCN: 用宽泛措辞写成的条款能被拉伸，覆盖起草者从未点名的情形。

senses.title: Computing power that grows on demand
senses.definition: in computing, resources that can be added or released quickly as the workload changes
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机领域，能随工作负载迅速增加或释放的资源
senses.example: Elastic computing lets the site absorb a sudden rush of visitors.
senses.exampleCN: 弹性计算让网站承受突然涌入的访问者。
senses.why: Cloud capacity stretches like rubber and contracts again when the load falls.
senses.whyCN: 云端容量像橡皮一样被拉长，负载下降时又缩回去。

intro.en: Elastic reached English through French and New Latin from Greek elastos, a word for something ductile or beaten out. The usual link to elaunein 'to drive, beat out' is generally accepted, but the exact semantic step is source uncertain.
intro.cn: elastic 经法语与新拉丁语进入英语，源头是希腊语 elastos，指可延展、可锤打成形的物件。把它与 elaunein「驱赶、打出」相联是一般认为的说法，但确切的语义环节来源不确定。

items.en: Greek elastos described something ductile, especially metal that could be hammered into shape and would spring back.
items.cn: 希腊语 elastos 指可延展的，尤指能被锤打成形又会弹回的金属。

items.en: The common derivation takes elastos from elaunein 'to drive, beat out'; how driving metal became springing back is source uncertain.
items.cn: 常见的推源把 elastos 追溯到 elaunein「驱赶、打出」；从锤打金属到弹回原状之间的语义过渡来源不确定。

items.en: Sixteenth- and seventeenth-century writers on mechanics formed Latin elasticus for the power of a body to restore its shape.
items.cn: 十六、十七世纪研究力学的作者造出新拉丁语 elasticus，用来指物体恢复形状的能力。

items.en: French élastique carried the word into educated English in the seventeenth century, first as a property of springs and gases.
items.cn: 法语 élastique 在十七世纪把这个词带进英语书面语，最初指弹簧与气体的性质。

items.en: Hooke's experiments on springs fixed the adjective in physics, and the phrase elastic limit followed as the boundary of the property.
items.cn: 胡克对弹簧的实验使这个形容词在物理学中定型，弹性极限一说随后出现，用来标出这种性质的边界。

items.en: In the nineteenth and twentieth centuries the word was lent to demand in economics, to broadly worded legal clauses and to computing capacity.
items.cn: 十九与二十世纪，这个词又被借去指经济学的需求、措辞宽泛的法律条款以及计算容量。

note.en: The first group shares the root or the shape of elastic; the second group names neighbouring ideas.
note.cn: 第一组与本词同根或形近；第二组是意思相邻的其他说法。

entries.definition: The noun for the power to spring back; the property itself rather than the material.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指弹回原状的能力，说的是性质而非材料。

entries.definition: Made with elastic threads woven in, said of a waistband or cuff.
entries.definitionCN: 指织入弹性纤维的，用于腰带或袖口。

entries.definition: A rubber-like polymer that stretches and returns; the ending names a class of materials.
entries.definitionCN: 类橡胶的聚合物，能拉伸并回弹；词尾表示一类材料。

entries.definition: Not springing back; in economics, demand that barely moves when price changes.
entries.definitionCN: 不会弹回的；经济学中指价格变动而需求几乎不变。

entries.definition: To give a fabric or material the power to stretch and recover.
entries.definitionCN: 使织物或材料获得伸缩与回弹的能力。

entries.definition: Able to bend easily; the general capacity to bend, without the promise of springing back.
entries.definitionCN: 容易弯曲的；泛指能弯，并不保证弹回。

entries.definition: Able to recover quickly after being compressed or hit, and by extension after hardship.
entries.definitionCN: 受压或受击后能迅速恢复的，引申指遭遇困难后复原。

entries.definition: The everyday word for a material that can be pulled out a long way.
entries.definitionCN: 口语说法，指能被拉得很长的材料。

entries.definition: Bouncy under the foot or hand, like a well-made mattress.
entries.definitionCN: 踩上去或按下去有弹跳感，像好床垫那样。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Greek source, the physics term and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的希腊语来源、物理术语与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Greek elastos named metal that could be hammered and would spring back, and that is the physical core of the word.
normal.cn: 希腊语 elastos 指能锤打成形而弹回的金属，这正是这个词的物理内核。

normal.en: The family runs elastic, elasticity, elasticated, elastomer and inelastic.
normal.cn: 同族词有 elastic、elasticity、elasticated、elastomer 与 inelastic。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: elastic band, elastic waistband, elastic collision, elastic limit.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出用法：橡皮筋、松紧腰带、弹性碰撞、弹性极限。

normal.en: In economics elastic demand stretches when price moves, and inelastic demand barely budges.
normal.cn: 经济学里，弹性需求随价格变动而伸缩，无弹性需求几乎不动。

normal.en: Cloud engineers speak of elastic capacity that grows with traffic and shrinks when the rush ends.
normal.cn: 云端工程师说的弹性容量，会随流量增长，也会在高峰过后收缩。

abstract.en: An elastic rule is one that bends under pressure and returns to its shape when the pressure passes.
abstract.cn: 弹性规则受压时弯曲，压力过去后恢复原样。

abstract.en: The band can be stretched for hours, but only up to a point; every material has its limit.
abstract.cn: 皮筋能被拉很久，却只到某一点为止；凡材料都有极限。

abstract.en: Springing back is not the same as never bending; it is bending and then coming home.
abstract.cn: 弹回并不等于从不弯曲，而是弯过之后回到原处。

examples.en: The elastic waistband keeps the trousers snug without a belt.
examples.cn: 松紧腰带不用皮带也能让裤子贴身。

examples.en: Demand for holiday flights is highly elastic in the weeks before departure.
examples.cn: 起飞前几周，假日航班的机票需求极具弹性。

examples.en: A stretched spring stores energy, and an elastic collision gives it back.
examples.cn: 拉伸的弹簧储存能量，弹性碰撞又把能量还回来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「伊拉丝提克」——一拉就回弹的丝，松手立刻缩回原长：有弹性的

root: 希腊语 elastos「可延展的、会弹回的」← 一般认为与 elaunein「驱赶、打出」相关；经新拉丁语 elasticus 与法语 élastique 进入英语，十七世纪成为物理术语，后扩展到需求、条款与计算容量。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one piece of rubber: the material that springs back, the band itself, the springy body, the stretchable rule, responsive demand, a conserving collision, the limit of the property, an expanding clause and scalable computing.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟着同一块橡胶：会弹回的材料、皮筋本身、轻快的身体、可伸缩的规则、随价变动的需求、守能的碰撞、性质的极限、可扩张的条款与可伸缩的计算。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a band pulled to twice its length snaps back the instant the hand lets go.
core.cn: 核心意象：拉到两倍长的皮筋，在手松开的一瞬弹回原长。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL AND ITS LIMIT: the spring that returns, and the point beyond which it cannot.
branches.cn: 材料与极限：会回弹的弹簧，以及它再也回不去的那一点。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: the loop itself, sold by the packet and used to hold papers or a waistband.
branches.cn: 物件本身：成包出售的皮筋，用来捆纸或收腰。

branches.en: THE BODY: a stride that looks light because the flesh recovers as fast as rubber.
branches.cn: 身体：因为肌肉像橡胶一样恢复得快，步态看上去轻快。

branches.en: THE STRETCHABLE RULE: a deadline or a clause that yields under pressure and still holds together.
branches.cn: 可伸缩的规则：受压时让步、却仍自成一体的截止期或条款。

branches.en: THE RESPONSIVE SYSTEM: demand, a collision and cloud capacity that give back exactly what was put in.
branches.cn: 会响应的系统：需求、碰撞与云端容量，投入多少就还回多少。

intro.en: Elastic is built on a Greek adjective and Latin endings; the core is not a Latin root, so the Latin list holds only the endings and the New Latin form.
intro.cn: elastic 由希腊语形容词与拉丁语词尾构成；核心并非拉丁词根，故拉丁词条只收词尾与新拉丁语形式。

latinIntro.en: The Latin material here is the New Latin adjective elasticus and the suffixes that build its family.
latinIntro.cn: 这里的拉丁语成分是新拉丁语形容词 elasticus，以及构成其同族词的词尾。

items.structure: Greek elastos through New Latin elasticus
items.example: The adjective names the property before the object.
items.exampleCN: 形容词先给性质命名，物件随后。

items.example: The word was first used of metal, not rubber.
items.exampleCN: 这个词最初用于金属，而非橡胶。

items.example: The verb supplied the image of metal driven into shape.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供金属被打成形的意象。

items.example: Mechanics writers coined it from the Greek adjective.
items.exampleCN: 力学作者由希腊语形容词造出此形。

items.example: The ending makes a property into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾把性质变成形容词。

items.example: The suffix turns the adjective into the name of the property.
items.exampleCN: 词尾把形容词变成性质的名称。

items.example: The noun is the measurable property in physics.
items.exampleCN: 名词是物理学中可测量的性质。

items.example: The negating prefix marks the limit of the family.
items.exampleCN: 否定前缀标出这一族词的边界。

items.example: The second element comes from a Greek word for part.
items.exampleCN: 第二个成分来自希腊语中表示部分词。

latinEntries.structure: Greek elastos (driven, ductile) + Latin -icus; New Latin elasticus
latinEntries.example: New Latin elasticus is the adjective English borrowed through French.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 新拉丁语 elasticus 是英语经法语借入的那个形容词。

latinEntries.example: Latin -icus builds adjectives such as publicus and rusticus.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 -icus 构成 publicus、rusticus 这类形容词。

latinEntries.example: Latin -itas builds nouns such as veritas, truth.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 -itas 构成 veritas（真理）这类名词。

latinEntries.structure: Latin negative prefix in-, assimilated to il-, im- and ir-
latinEntries.example: It negates elastic to give inelastic, as it negates many Latin adjectives.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它否定 elastic，构成 inelastic（无弹性的），正如它否定许多拉丁形容词那样。

definition_zh: 灵活性；柔韧性；可变通性；身体的活动度；可调整的余地
definition_en: the ability to bend, change or be changed without breaking; the room a body, plan or system has to adjust
core_image: 舞者把一条腿抬到耳侧，关节与肌肉都还留着一寸余地，放下时也毫无阻滞
scene: 排练室里，舞者把腿抬到耳侧，又缓缓放下，关节没有一丝滞涩。Years of stretching gave the dancer a flexibility that let her hold the pose without strain.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项：身体关节与肌肉能被弯曲、拉伸而不受伤的活动余地；句意为多年拉伸让舞者获得柔韧度，能毫不费力地保持这个姿势。图中可辨识物件：把杆、地胶、镜子、抬起的腿。

pos.zh: 灵活性；柔韧性；可变通性（不可数）

senses.title: The body's room to move
senses.definition: the range within which joints and muscles can bend and stretch without injury
senses.definitionCN: 关节与肌肉能被弯曲、拉伸而不受伤的幅度
senses.example: Daily stretching slowly improved her flexibility.
senses.exampleCN: 每天的拉伸慢慢提高了她的柔韧度。
senses.why: A body that bends far without tearing has more room before it reaches its limit, and room is what the word names.
senses.whyCN: 身体能弯得远而不撕裂，说明在到达极限之前还有余地，而这个词命名的正是余地。

senses.title: A material that bends without breaking
senses.definition: the property of a material that lets it bend under force without cracking
senses.definitionCN: 材料受力时能弯曲而不裂断的性质
senses.example: The flexibility of the rubber tube lets it follow the pipe's curve.
senses.exampleCN: 橡胶管的柔性使它顺着管道的弯走。
senses.why: Elasticity is the power to spring back; flexibility is only the power to bend, and a bent metal rod may stay bent.
senses.whyCN: 弹性是弹回原状的能力，柔性只是能弯的能力；弯过的金属杆可能就一直弯着。

senses.title: A plan that can be redrawn
senses.definition: the quality of a plan or arrangement that can be changed when circumstances change
senses.definitionCN: 计划或安排能在情况变化时被改动的性质
senses.example: The schedule's flexibility saved the trip when the flight was cancelled.
senses.exampleCN: 航班取消时，日程的弹性救了这次旅行。
senses.why: A plan with spare room can absorb an interruption without being abandoned, which is the practical value of bending.
senses.whyCN: 留有余地的计划能吸收一次中断而不必作废，这就是「能弯」的实际价值。

senses.title: Working hours that can shift
senses.definition: the arrangement that lets employees choose or shift their working hours
senses.definitionCN: 允许雇员选择或挪动工作时间的安排
senses.example: The firm offers flexibility over start and finish times.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司允许员工弹性安排上下班时间。
senses.why: Once the word described bodies and plans, employers applied it to the timetable, the part of work easiest to bend.
senses.whyCN: 这个词先描述身体与计划，雇主随后把它用到时间表上，因为那是工作里最容易弯的部分。

senses.title: A system that can be reshaped
senses.definition: the capacity of a system, design or piece of software to be modified or extended
senses.definitionCN: 系统、设计或软件能被修改、扩展的能力
senses.example: The software's flexibility allows each school to build its own forms.
senses.exampleCN: 这套软件的灵活性让每所学校都能自建表单。
senses.why: A system built from separate parts can be rearranged, so the word moves from the body to the structure.
senses.whyCN: 由独立部件搭成的系统可以重新排列，于是这个词从身体移到了结构上。

senses.title: Room to give in a bargain
senses.definition: the willingness or scope to adjust a position in a negotiation
senses.definitionCN: 在谈判中调整立场、作出让步的意愿或空间
senses.example: Both sides showed flexibility on the payment terms.
senses.exampleCN: 双方在付款条件上都表现出了灵活性。
senses.why: A negotiator who can move without losing the whole deal is bending while keeping the shape of the agreement.
senses.whyCN: 谈判者能在不失去整笔交易的情况下移动立场，就是弯着却保持协议的形状。

senses.title: A mind that can switch
senses.definition: the ability to change habits of thought and see a problem from another side
senses.definitionCN: 改变思维习惯、从另一面看问题的能力
senses.example: Cognitive flexibility helps children move from one task to another.
senses.exampleCN: 认知灵活性帮助孩子从一项任务转到另一项。
senses.why: Thinking that cannot bend gets stuck on the first frame it meets, so the physical word became a mental one.
senses.whyCN: 不会弯的思维会卡在它遇到的第一个框架上，于是这个物理词变成了心理词。

senses.title: Prices and wages that can move
senses.definition: in economics, the ease with which prices or wages adjust to changes in supply and demand
senses.definitionCN: 在经济学中，价格或工资随供求变化而调整的容易程度
senses.example: Wage flexibility is central to this labour-market reform.
senses.exampleCN: 工资的灵活性是这项劳动力市场改革的核心。
senses.why: A price that can move finds a buyer instead of leaving goods unsold, so economists call that room flexibility.
senses.whyCN: 能变动的价格能找到买主，而不至于让货物滞销，经济学家就把这种余地叫作灵活性。

senses.title: Loose order in a sentence
senses.definition: in linguistics, the freedom a language allows in arranging words without changing the meaning
senses.definitionCN: 在语言学中，一种语言在不改变意义的前提下自由排列词语的程度
senses.example: Latin's flexibility of word order comes from its case endings.
senses.exampleCN: 拉丁语语序的自由来自它的格词尾。
senses.why: When endings mark who does what, the words can move, and the grammar itself is described as bending.
senses.whyCN: 当词尾标明谁做什么，词就能移动，语法本身也就被形容为可弯。

intro.en: Flexibility comes from Latin flexibilis 'that can be bent', built on flectere 'to bend', with the noun ending -itas. The deeper link to a root meaning 'to plait' is generally accepted, though the exact path is source uncertain.
intro.cn: flexibility 来自拉丁语 flexibilis「可弯曲的」，由 flectere「弯曲」加名词词尾 -itas 构成。把它上溯到意为「编、折」的词根是一般认为的说法，确切路径来源不确定。

items.en: Flectere meant to bend, turn or curve, and it supplied the verb at the centre of the whole family.
items.cn: flectere 意为弯曲、转动或使成弧线，为整个词族提供了核心动词。

items.en: The adjective flexibilis, 'that can be bent', joined the verb to the suffix -bilis, which marks what is possible.
items.cn: 形容词 flexibilis 意为「可弯曲的」，把动词与表示「能够」的词尾 -bilis 结合。

items.en: The suffix -itas turned the adjective into a noun naming a quality, the step that gives English its -ity.
items.cn: -itas 把形容词变成指称性质的名词，这一步后来给了英语 -ity 的词尾。

items.en: French flexibilité carried the noun into English in the seventeenth century, first in descriptions of bodies and materials.
items.cn: 法语 flexibilité 在十七世纪把这个名词带进英语，最初用于描述身体与材料。

items.en: Etymologists generally connect flectere with a root meaning to plait or fold; whether the bending image began with weaving is source uncertain.
items.cn: 词源学者一般认为 flectere 与意为「编、折」的词根相关；弯曲的意象是否起于编织，来源不确定。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word was applied to working hours, labour markets and software, wherever a fixed shape had to give.
items.cn: 二十世纪，这个词被用到工时、劳动力市场与软件上，凡固定形状必须让步之处都能用它。

note.en: The first group shares the bending root; the second group names ideas that overlap without being identical.
note.cn: 第一组共享「弯」这个词根；第二组是部分重叠但并不等同的说法。

entries.definition: The adjective: able to bend or adapt.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词：能弯曲或能变通的。

entries.definition: The adverb: in a way that adjusts rather than insists.
entries.definitionCN: 副词：以调整而非坚持的方式。

entries.definition: Not able or willing to bend, in body, rule or temper.
entries.definitionCN: 身体、规则或性情上不能或不愿弯曲的。

entries.definition: To bend a joint or a muscle; also a flexible cable.
entries.definitionCN: 弯曲关节或肌肉；也指柔性电缆。

entries.definition: A working system in which starting and finishing times can vary.
entries.definitionCN: 上下班时间可浮动的工时制度。

entries.definition: The power to spring back to the original shape; flexibility only needs to bend.
entries.definitionCN: 弹回原状的能力；而柔性只要求能弯。

entries.definition: Smooth, easy bending of the body, with no sense of force.
entries.definitionCN: 身体弯曲得平滑轻松，不带用力的感觉。

entries.definition: The capacity to change oneself to fit a new situation.
entries.definitionCN: 改变自身以适应新处境的能力。

entries.definition: The power to recover after strain or hardship, closer to elasticity than to bending.
entries.definitionCN: 受压迫或挫折后恢复的力量，更接近弹性而非柔性。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Latin verb, the real family and the fixed phrases of work and training.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁动词、同族词，以及训练与工作场景里的固定说法。

normal.en: Latin flectere meant to bend, and every word in the family keeps that image.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 flectere 意为弯曲，这一族里的每个词都保留着这个意象。

normal.en: The family runs flexible, flexibly, flexibility, inflexible and flex.
normal.cn: 同族词有 flexible、flexibly、flexibility、inflexible 与 flex。

normal.en: Trainers speak of flexibility training, and offices speak of workplace flexibility.
normal.cn: 教练说柔韧训练，办公室说工作安排的灵活性。

normal.en: Economists contrast wage flexibility with wage rigidity, two ends of one scale.
normal.cn: 经济学家把工资灵活与工资刚性对举，那是同一标尺的两端。

normal.en: A language with case endings can afford flexibility of word order.
normal.cn: 有格词尾的语言才敢让语序自由。

abstract.en: Flexibility is the spare room that keeps a thing from snapping when life pushes.
abstract.cn: 灵活性是那点余地，让东西在生活推挤时不至于折断。

abstract.en: A body that can bend far has learned where its edge is, and stops just short.
abstract.cn: 能弯得远的身体知道自己的边在哪里，并且总停在边上一点。

abstract.en: The opposite of flexibility is not strength but brittleness.
abstract.cn: 灵活的反面不是坚强，而是脆。

examples.en: Yoga builds flexibility in the hips and shoulders.
examples.cn: 瑜伽增强髋部与肩部的柔韧性。

examples.en: The team's flexibility let it re-plan the study after the equipment failed.
examples.cn: 团队的灵活性使他们能在设备故障后重新规划研究。

examples.en: Too much flexibility in the rule can also mean too little protection.
examples.cn: 规则过于灵活，也可能意味着保护不足。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「弗莱克西比利提」——像弹簧一样能屈能伸的比利提：灵活性

root: 拉丁语 flectere「弯曲」→ flexibilis「可弯曲的」→ 名词词尾 -itas；经法语 flexibilité 进入英语。深层词根一般认为与「编、折」有关，确切路径来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one bending motion: the body's range, a material that bends, a plan that can be redrawn, movable working hours, a reshapeable system, room in a bargain, a mind that switches, prices that float and free word order.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟着同一个弯曲动作：身体的活动幅度、能弯的材料、可重画的计划、可挪动的工时、可改造的系统、谈判的余地、能转换的头脑、可浮动的价格与自由的语序。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a leg lifted to the ear, still an inch short of its limit, then lowered without a catch.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条腿抬到耳侧，离极限还差一寸，放下时也没有卡顿。

branches.en: THE BODY AND THE MATERIAL: room to bend, measured in joints and in rubber.
branches.cn: 身体与材料：以关节、也以橡胶来度量的可弯余地。

branches.en: THE MOVABLE SCHEDULE: a plan and a working day that can shift without collapse.
branches.cn: 可挪动的日程：能改变而不致崩溃的计划与工作日。

branches.en: THE RESHAPEABLE STRUCTURE: software modules and sentence order that can be rearranged.
branches.cn: 可重排的结构：能重新组合的软件模块与句子语序。

branches.en: THE ROOM IN A BARGAIN: a position that moves while the agreement holds.
branches.cn: 谈判的余地：立场在移动，协议却仍成立。

branches.en: THE MIND AND THE MARKET: thought that switches frames, prices that find a buyer.
branches.cn: 头脑与市场：能换框架的思维，能找到买主的价格。

intro.en: Flexibility is a Latin adjective plus a Latin noun ending, and the family is built with the verb flectere.
intro.cn: flexibility 由一个拉丁形容词加一个拉丁名词词尾构成，同族词都建在动词 flectere 上。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is flectere and its adjective flexibilis, with the endings -bilis and -itas.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语成分是 flectere 及其形容词 flexibilis，以及 -bilis 与 -itas 两个词尾。

items.example: The noun names a quality, not a thing.
items.exampleCN: 名词命名的是性质，不是物件。

items.example: The verb is the centre of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整个词族的中心。

items.example: The suffix marks what is possible.
items.exampleCN: 词尾表示「能够」。

items.example: It builds adjectives of possibility.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示可能性的形容词。

items.example: It turns adjectives into names of qualities.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词变成性质的名称。

items.example: English took the adjective before the noun.
items.exampleCN: 英语先取形容词，后取名词。

items.example: The prefix marks the closed end of the scale.
items.exampleCN: 前缀标出这根标尺封闭的一端。

items.example: The short verb now leads a gym instruction.
items.exampleCN: 短动词如今是健身房的口令。

items.example: The compound names the arrangement, not the act.
items.exampleCN: 复合词命名的是制度，不是动作。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb flectere (flect-, flexum; to bend)
latinEntries.example: Latin flectere means to bend, and its participle flexus gives flex.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 flectere 意为弯曲，其分词 flexus 给出英语 flex。

latinEntries.example: Latin flexibilis means that can be bent.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 flexibilis 意为「可被弯曲的」。

latinEntries.example: Latin -bilis builds adjectives such as amabilis, lovable.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 -bilis 构成 amabilis（可爱的）这类形容词。

latinEntries.example: It builds flexibilitas, the Latin noun for flexibility.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它构成 flexibilitas，即表示「柔韧」的拉丁名词。

definition_zh: 刚性；僵直；死板；严格不变的性质
definition_en: the quality of being stiff, unbending or unable to change; resistance to deformation or adaptation
core_image: 一根钢梁在重压下弯了不到一毫米，卸去载荷后仍然笔直如初
scene: 桥梁检测时，工程师在钢梁上逐级加载，仪表指针几乎不动。The rigidity of the steel beam kept the bridge deck from sagging under the load.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项：材料抵抗弯曲与变形的能力；句意为钢梁的刚性使桥面在载荷下没有下沉。图中可辨识物件：钢梁、千分表、加载砝码、桥面。

pos.zh: 刚性；僵直；死板；不可变性（不可数）

senses.title: A material that will not bend
senses.definition: the property of a solid that resists bending or deformation under force
senses.definitionCN: 固体在外力下抵抗弯曲与变形的性质
senses.example: The rigidity of the alloy kept the blade from warping.
senses.exampleCN: 这种合金的刚性使叶片不会变形。
senses.why: A material that holds its shape under load is the oldest sense, because rigidity was first seen in beams and bones.
senses.whyCN: 受载仍保持形状是这个词最古老的一层，因为刚性最早见于梁木与骨骼。

senses.title: A frame that will not sag
senses.definition: the stiffness of a structure or frame that keeps it from sagging or twisting
senses.definitionCN: 结构或框架的刚度，使其不致下沉或扭转
senses.example: The rigidity of the frame comes from triangular bracing.
senses.exampleCN: 框架的刚性来自三角形支撑。
senses.why: A frame is rigid when its parts cannot slide past one another, and bracing is how builders remove that freedom.
senses.whyCN: 构件的各部分不能相互滑动时，框架才算刚，而支撑正是建造者拿走那种自由的手段。

senses.title: A body that will not loosen
senses.definition: stiffness of the limbs or muscles that makes movement slow and awkward
senses.definitionCN: 四肢或肌肉发僵，使动作迟缓笨拙的状态
senses.example: Rigidity in his shoulders made the swimmer slow to turn.
senses.exampleCN: 肩部的僵直让这名游泳者转身很慢。
senses.why: Warm muscle bends and lengthens; cold or tense muscle holds its length, and that held length is rigidity.
senses.whyCN: 温暖的肌肉能弯能伸，寒冷或紧张的肌肉则保持原长，这种被固定住的长度就是僵直。

senses.title: A sign in medicine
senses.definition: in medicine, a fixed resistance of muscles to passive movement, often a sign of nerve disease
senses.definitionCN: 在医学中，肌肉对被动活动呈现固定阻力，常为神经疾病的体征
senses.example: Muscle rigidity is common in Parkinson's disease.
senses.exampleCN: 肌肉僵直在帕金森病中很常见。
senses.why: When the nervous system keeps a muscle switched on, the limb feels like a locked hinge, and clinicians call it rigidity.
senses.whyCN: 当神经系统让肌肉持续紧张，肢体就像被锁住的铰链，临床医生称这种状态为僵直。

senses.title: A mind that will not move
senses.definition: an unwillingness or inability to change habits of thought or accept another view
senses.definitionCN: 不愿或不能改变思维习惯、接受另一种看法的状态
senses.example: Her rigidity about routines made any change distressing.
senses.exampleCN: 她对固定流程的执着让任何改变都令人难受。
senses.why: Thinking that will not bend repeats the same answer, and the physical word for unbending serves the mental case.
senses.whyCN: 不会弯的思维重复同一个答案，那个表示「不弯」的物理词就用到了心理情形上。

senses.title: A rule applied without slack
senses.definition: the quality of a rule or official practice that allows no discretion or exception
senses.definitionCN: 规则或官方做法不留裁量空间、不容例外的性质
senses.example: The rigidity of the rule left the clerk no discretion.
senses.exampleCN: 规则的僵硬让那名职员毫无裁量权。
senses.why: A rule written so tightly that no case can bend it turns a guard against exceptions, and that is what the word criticises.
senses.whyCN: 写得紧到任何个案都弯不动的规则，会把守则变成拒绝例外的关卡，这正是这个词所批评的。

senses.title: Wages that will not fall
senses.definition: in economics, the failure of prices or wages to adjust when supply and demand change
senses.definitionCN: 在经济学中，价格或工资在供求变化时无法调整的现象
senses.example: Wage rigidity keeps unemployment high after a shock.
senses.exampleCN: 工资刚性使冲击之后的失业率居高不下。
senses.why: A wage that cannot move down is a price stuck at one level, and economists describe that stuckness as rigidity.
senses.whyCN: 降不下去的工资是卡在一个水平上的价格，经济学家把这种卡住的状态称为刚性。

senses.title: A shape that cannot deform
senses.definition: in geometry and mechanics, the property of a body whose distances and angles do not change under movement
senses.definitionCN: 在几何与力学中，物体在运动时距离与角度都不改变的性质
senses.example: The rigidity of a body in geometry means its distances never change under rotation.
senses.exampleCN: 几何中物体的刚性意味着旋转时距离永不改变。
senses.why: If every pair of points keeps its distance, the body can only turn and slide, never distort, and that is the strict mathematical sense.
senses.whyCN: 若每一对点的距离都保持不变，物体就只能转动和平移，绝不会扭曲，这是严格的数学含义。

senses.title: A hierarchy that blocks movement
senses.definition: the inflexibility of an institution or social order that prevents people or ideas from moving
senses.definitionCN: 机构或社会秩序不容人或观念流动的僵化状态
senses.example: The rigidity of the old hierarchy blocked promotion.
senses.exampleCN: 旧有层级的僵化堵住了晋升之路。
senses.why: A ladder whose rungs cannot be reached is rigid in the social sense, and the word carries the same image of a fixed frame.
senses.whyCN: 一架横档够不着的梯子在社会的意义上就是僵硬的，这个词仍带着固定框架的同一意象。

intro.en: Rigidity comes from Latin rigiditas, built on rigidus 'stiff' and rigere 'to be stiff or numb'. Beyond Latin the reconstruction is source uncertain, so the deeper root is usually left open.
intro.cn: rigidity 来自拉丁语 rigiditas，由 rigidus「僵硬的」与 rigere「发僵、变硬」构成。越过拉丁语之后属于重构，来源不确定，因此更深的词根通常不作定论。

items.en: Rigere meant to be stiff, numb or fixed, said of a limb that will not move and of a body stiffened by cold.
items.cn: rigere 意为发僵、麻木、固定不动，用于不会活动的肢体，也用于被寒冷冻僵的身体。

items.en: The adjective rigidus described anything stiff, hard or unbending, from a beam to a person's manner.
items.cn: 形容词 rigidus 描述一切僵硬、坚硬、不肯弯的东西，从梁木到人的态度。

items.en: Rigor named the stiffness itself, and in English it kept the senses of strictness and of a chill running through the body.
items.cn: rigor 指僵硬本身，进入英语后保留了「严格」与「寒战穿身」两种意思。

items.en: Rigiditas turned the adjective into a noun of quality, the form that passed through French into English.
items.cn: rigiditas 把形容词变成表示性质的名词，这一形式经法语进入英语。

items.en: English rigidity appears in the seventeenth century, first in descriptions of bodies and mechanical parts.
items.cn: 英语中的 rigidity 出现于十七世纪，最初用于描述物体与机械部件。

items.en: In the nineteenth and twentieth centuries the word was applied to muscle signs, to rigid prices and wages, and to institutional inflexibility.
items.cn: 十九与二十世纪，这个词被用到肌肉体征、价格与工资刚性，以及制度的僵化上。

note.en: The first group shares the stiff root or merely looks like it; the second group names related qualities.
note.cn: 第一组与本词同根或只是形近；第二组是意思相关的其他性质。

entries.definition: The adjective: stiff, unbending, strictly fixed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词：僵硬的、不肯弯的、严格固定的。

entries.definition: The adverb: in a stiff or unyielding manner.
entries.definitionCN: 副词：以僵硬或不妥协的方式。

entries.definition: To make or become stiff, literally or in habit.
entries.definitionCN: 使变硬、变僵，可用于实物，也可用于习惯。

entries.definition: Strictness, or a sudden chill; the noun behind the adjective rigorous.
entries.definitionCN: 严格，或突然的寒战；形容词「严谨的」背后的名词。

entries.definition: Strict and thorough, from the same stiffness but turned into method.
entries.definitionCN: 严格而周密的，同出「僵」这一层，但转成了方法上的严谨。

entries.definition: Cold in temperature or in manner; it only looks close, since its root means cold.
entries.definitionCN: 温度低或态度冷淡；只是形近，其词根意为寒冷。

entries.definition: The everyday word for the bodily or material quality.
entries.definitionCN: 口语中最常用的说法，指身体或材料的僵、硬。

entries.definition: Unwillingness to bend, closer to the mental and institutional senses.
entries.definitionCN: 不愿弯曲，更贴近心理与制度层面的意思。

entries.definition: Resistance to scratching or pressing, a material property that is not the same as stiffness.
entries.definitionCN: 抗刮擦或抗压的能力，与刚性并非同一性质。

entries.definition: Steadiness under pressure, often a virtue rather than a fault.
entries.definitionCN: 受压时的稳定，常是优点而非缺陷。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Latin verb, the real family and the fixed phrases of engineering and economics.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁动词、同族词，以及工程与经济学里的固定说法。

normal.en: Latin rigere meant to be stiff or numb, and rigidity is that state turned into a noun.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 rigere 意为发僵、麻木，rigidity 就是把这种状态变成名词。

normal.en: The family runs rigid, rigidly, rigidify, rigidity and rigor.
normal.cn: 同族词有 rigid、rigidly、rigidify、rigidity 与 rigor。

normal.en: Engineers test structural rigidity; doctors note muscle rigidity; economists warn of wage rigidity.
normal.cn: 工程师测结构刚性，医生记肌肉僵直，经济学家警告工资刚性。

normal.en: A rigid body in geometry keeps every distance fixed while it turns.
normal.cn: 几何中的刚体在转动时保持所有距离不变。

normal.en: Rigidity is measured against flexibility: the same scale, two ends.
normal.cn: 刚性是相对柔性来度量的：同一根标尺，两个端点。

abstract.en: A beam that will not bend carries more, but it also breaks instead of yielding.
abstract.cn: 不肯弯的梁能承更多重量，但宁可断裂也不让步。

abstract.en: A rule with no slack protects nobody in the end, because every real case needs an exception.
abstract.cn: 不留余地的规则最终保护不了谁，因为每个真实个案都需要例外。

abstract.en: The stiffest mind is not the strongest; it is the one with the fewest ways out.
abstract.cn: 最僵硬的头脑不是最强的，而是出口最少的。

examples.en: The rigidity of the ceramic keeps the cutting edge sharp.
examples.cn: 陶瓷的刚性使刀刃保持锋利。

examples.en: Rigidity in the labour market can prolong a recession.
examples.cn: 劳动力市场的刚性会拖长衰退。

examples.en: The instructor noticed rigidity in the beginner's hips.
examples.cn: 教练注意到初学者髋部的僵紧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「瑞吉迪提」——像冻住的铁棍，怎么掰也掰不弯：刚性

root: 拉丁语 rigere「发僵、变硬」→ rigidus「僵硬的」→ rigiditas「僵硬的性质」；经法语进入英语。更深词根属重构，来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one unbending beam: the stiffness of a material, of a frame, of a limb, the medical sign, the closed mind, the rule without slack, the wage that will not fall, the shape that cannot deform and the hierarchy that blocks movement.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟着一根不肯弯的梁：材料的刚性、构架的刚性、肢体的僵直、医学体征、封闭的头脑、不留余地的规则、降不下来的工资、不能变形的形体，以及卡住流动的层级。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a steel beam bends less than a millimetre under load and returns to dead straight.
core.cn: 核心意象：钢梁在载荷下弯不到一毫米，卸力后笔直如初。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL AND THE FRAME: a solid that will not bend and a structure that will not sag.
branches.cn: 材料与构架：不肯弯的固体，不会下沉的结构。

branches.en: THE BODY: stiff shoulders, and the clinical sign of a muscle that stays switched on.
branches.cn: 身体：僵住的肩，以及肌肉持续紧张这一临床体征。

branches.en: THE CLOSED MIND: thought that repeats its first answer and cannot turn.
branches.cn: 封闭的头脑：重复第一个答案、转不过弯的思维。

branches.en: THE FROZEN ORDER: a rule without discretion and a ladder with unreachable rungs.
branches.cn: 冻结的秩序：不留裁量权的规则，与横档够不着的阶梯。

branches.en: THE FIXED NUMBER: a wage that will not fall and a body whose distances never change.
branches.cn: 固定不变的数量：降不下来的工资，与距离永不改变的形体。

intro.en: Rigidity is a Latin adjective and noun ending over the verb rigere; unlike elastic, it has a genuine Latin root chain.
intro.cn: rigidity 是拉丁形容词与名词词尾叠加在动词 rigere 上；与 elastic 不同，它有一条真实的拉丁词根链。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer runs rigere, rigidus, -idus, rigor and -itas.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语成分包括 rigere、rigidus、-idus、rigor 与 -itas。

items.example: The noun is the abstract quality behind every concrete use.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是各具体用法背后的抽象性质。

items.example: The verb describes the state, not the act of making.
items.exampleCN: 动词描述状态，而非使之变硬的动作。

items.example: The adjective covers beams and manners alike.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词同时覆盖梁木与态度。

items.example: It builds adjectives of condition.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示状态形容词。

items.example: The noun kept a medical chill as well as a moral strictness.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词既保留医学上的寒战，也保留道德上的严格。

items.example: The suffix makes the adjective into an abstract noun.
items.exampleCN: 词尾把形容词变成抽象名词。

items.example: English took the adjective first.
items.exampleCN: 英语先取形容词。

items.example: The verb names a change of state.
items.exampleCN: 动词命名状态的变化。

items.example: The same root turns into method rather than matter.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根转向方法，而非物质。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb rigere (rig-; to be stiff)
latinEntries.example: Latin rigere means to be stiff, and its stem gives rigidus.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 rigere 意为发僵，其词干给出 rigidus。

latinEntries.example: Latin rigidus means stiff or hard.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 rigidus 意为僵硬的、硬的。

latinEntries.example: Latin -idus builds adjectives such as fluidus, flowing.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 -idus 构成 fluidus（流动的）这类形容词。

latinEntries.example: It builds rigiditas, the Latin noun behind rigidity.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它构成 rigiditas，即 rigidity 背后的拉丁名词。

definition_zh: 科学；一门学科；系统的知识体系；科研活动；理科课程
definition_en: organized knowledge gained by observation and experiment; a branch of such knowledge, or the activity that produces it
core_image: 实验台上摊着记录本、滴管与标尺，每个数字都被写得足以让别人重做一遍
scene: 实验室里，学生把同一组步骤写进记录本，标明温度与用量，好让别人照做。Science advances only when results can be checked by someone else.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项：以观察与实验建立可检验知识的系统活动；句意为只有当结果能被他人核验时，科学才向前推进。图中可辨识物件：记录本、滴管、温度计、标尺。

pos.zh: 科学；学科；知识体系（作不可数名词指活动或总体，作可数名词指一门学科）

senses.title: Knowledge built by testing
senses.definition: the systematic study of the physical and natural world through observation and experiment
senses.definitionCN: 通过观察与实验对物质与自然世界进行的系统研究
senses.example: Modern science rests on observation and experiment.
senses.exampleCN: 现代科学建立在观察与实验之上。
senses.why: Latin scientia meant knowledge of any kind; what narrowed it was the demand that claims be tested against the world.
senses.whyCN: 那个拉丁名词本指任何知识；把它收窄的，是「主张必须接受世界检验」这一要求。

senses.title: One branch of the study
senses.definition: a particular branch of this study, such as chemistry, physics or biology
senses.definitionCN: 这一研究的某个具体分支，如化学、物理或生物学
senses.example: Chemistry is a science with its own language.
senses.exampleCN: 化学是一门有自己的语言的学科。
senses.why: Once the whole had a name, each division needed the same name with a different modifier.
senses.whyCN: 整体有了名字之后，每个分支就用同一个名字加上不同的限定语。

senses.title: The knowledge already gathered
senses.definition: the body of knowledge that research has produced and that later work builds on
senses.definitionCN: 研究产生、并为后续工作所依托的知识总体
senses.example: The science of genetics has grown faster than its ethics.
senses.exampleCN: 遗传学的知识增长得比它的伦理讨论更快。
senses.why: A discipline is both an activity and a store; the word names the store whenever people speak of what is known.
senses.whyCN: 一门学科既是活动也是仓库；当人们谈「已知的东西」，这个词指的就是仓库。

senses.title: Research as a working life
senses.definition: the profession or daily activity of carrying out research
senses.definitionCN: 从事研究的职业或日常活动
senses.example: She has spent thirty years in science.
senses.exampleCN: 她在科研领域干了三十年。
senses.why: When the word names a career, it points to the people and hours behind the results.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词指一种职业时，它指向成果背后的人与工时。

senses.title: A subject at school
senses.definition: the school subject that teaches the methods and facts of natural science
senses.definitionCN: 在学校教授自然科学方法与事实的科目
senses.example: Science is timetabled for three hours a week.
senses.exampleCN: 科学课每周排三小时。
senses.why: Schools took the grand word and made it a timetable slot, because the method had to be taught before it could be used.
senses.whyCN: 学校把这个大词变成了课程表上的一格，因为方法必须先教才能用。

senses.title: Any systematic discipline
senses.definition: a systematically organized field of study, even when its subject is not nature
senses.definitionCN: 系统化组织起来的学问领域，即使研究对象并非自然
senses.example: Library science is a science of collections, not of nature.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆学是关于藏书体系的学问，而非关于自然。
senses.why: The pattern of defined terms and testable rules can be copied to libraries, so the name travelled beyond nature.
senses.whyCN: 定义术语与可检验规则这套做法能搬到图书馆，于是这个名字走出了自然领域。

senses.title: A skill reduced to rules
senses.definition: a skill or craft understood as a set of principles rather than an instinct
senses.definitionCN: 把一门手艺理解为一套原则，而非单凭直觉
senses.example: Baking bread is a science as much as an art.
senses.exampleCN: 烤面包既是一门艺术，也是一门学问。
senses.why: A craft becomes a science when its tacit steps are written down and made repeatable.
senses.whyCN: 当一门手艺中只可意会的步骤被写下来、变得可重复，它就成了一门学问。

senses.title: Methodical exactness
senses.definition: careful, systematic procedure rather than guesswork
senses.definitionCN: 谨慎而有系统的程序，而非凭猜测行事
senses.example: He tuned the engine with more science than instinct.
senses.exampleCN: 他调发动机靠的是条理，而不是直觉。
senses.why: If a thing is done with science, it is done by measure and check, which is the everyday adverb-like use of the noun.
senses.whyCN: 若一件事「带着科学」去做，就是按度量与核对去做，这是这个名词近乎副词化的日常用法。

senses.title: The enterprise and its people
senses.definition: the institutions, funding and community that together produce scientific knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 共同产出科学知识的机构、经费与人群
senses.example: Science has not yet settled the question.
senses.exampleCN: 科学界尚未解决这个问题。
senses.why: Results depend on journals, laboratories and money, so the word came to name the whole enterprise, not only its content.
senses.whyCN: 成果依赖期刊、实验室与经费，因此这个词也指整个事业，而不只是它的内容。

intro.en: Science comes from Latin scientia 'knowledge', from sciens, the present participle of scire 'to know'. English took it through Old French in the fourteenth century, and the modern narrowing to natural science belongs to the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries.
intro.cn: science 来自拉丁语 scientia「知识」，源自动词 scire「知道」的现在分词 sciens。英语经古法语在十四世纪引入；现代把它收窄为自然科学，则是十八、十九世纪的事。

items.en: Scire meant to know or to know how, and it stood apart from noscere, which meant to come to know a person or thing.
items.cn: scire 意为知道、懂得如何做，与 noscere（逐渐认识某人或某物）分工不同。

items.en: Scientia was simply knowledge or understanding, with no restriction to experiment or to nature.
items.cn: scientia 就是知识或理解，并不限于实验，也不限于自然。

items.en: The participle sciens 'knowing' supplied the shape of the noun, and the same stem produced conscious and conscience.
items.cn: 分词 sciens「知道的」提供了名词的词形，同一词干还产生了 conscious 与 conscience。

items.en: Etymologists generally trace scire to a root meaning to cut or split, the image being a distinction drawn between things; the exact step is source uncertain.
items.cn: 词源学者一般把 scire 上溯到意为「切、分」的词根，意象是在事物之间划出区分；确切一步来源不确定。

items.en: Old French science carried the word into English in the fourteenth century, where it still meant knowledge in general.
items.cn: 古法语 science 在十四世纪把词带入英语，当时仍泛指知识。

items.en: From the eighteenth century, science was increasingly reserved for tested knowledge of nature, and Whewell's coinage scientist in 1833 marked the new profession.
items.cn: 从十八世纪起，science 越来越多地专指关于自然、经得起检验的知识；惠威尔一八三三年造出 scientist，标出这一新职业。

note.en: The first group shares the knowing root or looks close; the second group names neighbouring ideas.
note.cn: 第一组同出「知道」这个词根或形近；第二组是意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The adjective for what follows scientific method.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指遵循科学方法的。

entries.definition: The person who does the work; coined in 1833 on the model of artist.
entries.definitionCN: 从事这项工作的人；一八三三年仿「艺术家」一词造出。

entries.definition: The adverb for doing something by tested method.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，指以经检验的方法去做。

entries.definition: Knowledge shared with oneself, literally knowing together; moral sense, not research.
entries.definitionCN: 字面为「与自己共知」，指道德意识，与科研无关。

entries.definition: Awake and aware, from the same knowing verb with a different prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 清醒有知觉的，同一动词加不同前缀。

entries.definition: Knowing everything, a theological word built on the same stem.
entries.definitionCN: 无所不知，同一词干构成的神学词。

entries.definition: The general word for what is known, without the demand for testing.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指已知之物的通用词，不含检验要求。

entries.definition: An organized field with its own methods and boundaries.
entries.definitionCN: 有自身方法与边界的有组织领域。

entries.definition: The activity of looking for new findings, closer to the work than to the body of knowledge.
entries.definitionCN: 寻找新发现的活动，更贴近工作而非知识总体。

entries.definition: A question-driven search for truth, without the institutional weight of science.
entries.definitionCN: 以问题驱动的求真过程，没有科学那种制度分量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Latin knowing verb, the real family and the fixed phrases of research policy.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁语「知道」动词、同族词，以及科研政策中的固定说法。

normal.en: Latin scire meant to know, and scientia was simply knowledge before experiment narrowed it.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 scire 意为知道，scientia 本只是知识，后来才被实验收窄。

normal.en: The family runs science, scientific, scientifically, scientist and scientism.
normal.cn: 同族词有 science、scientific、scientifically、scientist 与 scientism。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: basic science, applied science, science education, science policy.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出领域：基础科学、应用科学、科学教育、科学政策。

normal.en: Conscience and conscious share the same knowing stem with a different prefix.
normal.cn: conscience 与 conscious 用同一词干，只是前缀不同。

normal.en: Whewell coined scientist in 1833, on the pattern of artist, because the old phrase man of science was clumsy.
normal.cn: 惠威尔一八三三年仿 artist 造出 scientist，因为旧说法「科学人」太笨重。

abstract.en: Science is a habit of asking what would prove this wrong, not a pile of settled answers.
abstract.cn: 科学是追问「什么能证明这错了」的习惯，而不是一堆定论。

abstract.en: A result that no one else can repeat is a story, not yet a science.
abstract.cn: 无人能重复的结果只是一个故事，还算不上科学。

abstract.en: The word began as knowledge in general and learned to distrust itself.
abstract.cn: 这个词从泛指知识开始，后来学会了不轻信自己。

examples.en: Science grew out of natural philosophy once measurement became routine.
examples.cn: 当测量成为常规，科学便从自然哲学中长了出来。

examples.en: The science of materials gave the bridge its lighter deck.
examples.cn: 材料科学让这座桥有了更轻的桥面。

examples.en: She teaches science to children who have never used a microscope.
examples.cn: 她给从未用过显微镜的孩子上科学课。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「赛恩斯」——一场不断比赛、不断被推翻的求知活动：科学

root: 拉丁语 scire「知道」→ sciens「知道的」→ scientia「知识」；经古法语进入英语。深层词根一般认为意为「切、分」，确切一步来源不确定；十九世纪起专指经检验的自然知识。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one tested claim: the systematic study of nature, a branch of it, the knowledge gathered, research as a job, a school subject, any systematic discipline, a craft written into rules, methodical exactness, and the enterprise itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟着一个可检验的主张：对自然的系统研究、其中一门分支、积累起来的知识、作为职业的科研、学校科目、任何系统化学问、被写成规则的手艺、有条理的精确，以及整个事业。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bench notebook records temperature and dose well enough for a stranger to repeat the run.
core.cn: 核心意象：实验台上的记录本写清温度与用量，陌生人也能照着重做一遍。

branches.en: THE ACTIVITY AND THE STORE: the testing of claims and the knowledge that survives it.
branches.cn: 活动与仓库：对主张的检验，以及通过检验留存下来的知识。

branches.en: THE DIVISIONS: chemistry as a branch, science as a slot on a school timetable.
branches.cn: 分支：作为一门学科的化学，以及课程表上的一格科学课。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE AND THE INSTITUTIONS: careers in the lab, journals and funding behind the results.
branches.cn: 人与机构：实验室里的职业，以及成果背后的期刊与经费。

branches.en: THE COPIED PATTERN: libraries organized like a science, a craft written into repeatable rules.
branches.cn: 被搬用的范式：按科学方式组织的图书馆，与被写成可重复规则的手艺。

branches.en: THE HABIT OF MEASURE: tuning an engine by reading and checking rather than guessing.
branches.cn: 度量的习惯：靠读数与核对而不是靠猜来调发动机。

intro.en: Science has a genuine Latin root chain, and the same stem also built conscience, conscious and omniscient.
intro.cn: science 有一条真实的拉丁词根链，同一词干还构成了 conscience、conscious 与 omniscient。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is scire, sciens and scientia, with the noun ending -entia and the adjective ending -ficus in the modern coinage scientific.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语成分是 scire、sciens 与 scientia，以及名词词尾 -entia 与现代造词 scientific 中的形容词词尾 -ficus。

items.example: The English word still carries the older sense in phrases like a science of the mind.
items.exampleCN: 英语中「心灵的学问」一类说法仍保留较老的意思。

items.example: The verb is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整个词族的根。

items.example: The participle supplies the shape of the noun.
items.exampleCN: 分词提供了名词的词形。

items.example: Latin made the noun without any experimental limit.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语造出这个名词时并无实验的限制。

items.example: It builds abstract nouns from participles.
items.exampleCN: 它由分词构成抽象名词。

items.example: Scientific uses it in the sense of knowledge-making.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词用它表示「产生知识」。

items.example: The adjective arrived before the modern narrowing was complete.
items.exampleCN: 形容词在现代收窄完成之前就已出现。

items.example: It turned the field into a profession in 1833.
items.exampleCN: 一八三三年它把这个领域变成一种职业。

items.example: The prefix shifts knowledge inward, to morals.
items.exampleCN: 前缀把知识转向内部，指向道德。

items.example: The theological compound shows how far the stem reaches.
items.exampleCN: 这个神学复合词显示词干延伸之远。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb scire (sci-, scitum; to know)
latinEntries.example: Latin scire means to know, and its participle gives sciens.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 scire 意为知道，其分词给出 sciens。

latinEntries.example: Latin scientia means knowledge, the direct source of science.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 scientia 意为知识，是 science 的直接来源。

latinEntries.example: Latin -ia builds nouns such as memoria, memory.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 -ia 构成 memoria（记忆）这类名词。

latinEntries.example: New Latin scientificus is the adjective behind scientific.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 新拉丁语 scientificus 是 scientific 背后的形容词。

definition_zh: 科学家；从事系统研究的科研人员；某一科学分支的专家
definition_en: a person who studies the natural world by observation and experiment, or who works professionally in a branch of science
core_image: 凌晨的实验室里，一个人反复核对同一组读数，把可疑的异常一一圈出
scene: 深夜的实验室里，一个人反复核对同一组读数，把可疑的异常圈出来。The scientist repeated the run three times before trusting the number.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项：以系统研究自然为职业的人；句意为这位科研人员把同一轮实验做了三次，才肯相信那个数字。图中可辨识物件：白大褂、记录本、仪器屏幕、红笔圈注。

collocations.zh: 火箭专家（常喻极聪明的人）

senses.title: A professional researcher of nature
senses.titleCN: 以研究自然为职业的人
senses.definition: a person whose paid work is to study the natural world through observation and experiment
senses.definitionCN: 以观察与实验研究自然世界、并以此为职业的人
senses.example: The scientist repeated the run three times before trusting the number.
senses.exampleCN: 这位科研人员把同一轮实验做了三次，才肯相信那个数字。
senses.why: The word was coined to name a profession, so the working life is its first and central sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本是为命名一种职业而造，因此以此谋生的工作就是它最核心的一层。

senses.title: The person at the bench
senses.definition: someone who carries out experiments with instruments and samples in a laboratory
senses.definitionCN: 在实验室里用仪器与样品做实验的人
senses.example: The scientist pipetted the samples herself rather than leave it to a machine.
senses.exampleCN: 这位科研人员亲自移液取样，没有交给机器。
senses.why: Before the word existed, the work was called natural philosophy; after it, the hands at the bench had a name.
senses.whyCN: 这个词出现前，这份工作叫自然哲学；有了它之后，实验台前那双手才有个称呼。

senses.title: A specialist named by a field
senses.definition: a specialist in one branch, usually named by putting the branch before the word
senses.definitionCN: 某一分支的专家，通常把分支名放在这个词前面
senses.example: A materials scientist designed the lighter alloy.
senses.exampleCN: 一位材料科学家设计了更轻的合金。
senses.why: Once a general name for the worker exists, compounds can point to the bench or the field the worker belongs to.
senses.whyCN: 劳动者有了通名之后，复合词就能指明他所属的领域或实验台。

senses.title: A worker in any scientific field
senses.titleCN: 任何科学领域的工作者
senses.definition: a person who applies scientific method in a field such as computing, psychology or linguistics
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机、心理学或语言学等领域应用科学方法的人
senses.example: A computer scientist proved the bound with a short proof.
senses.exampleCN: 一位计算机科学家用一个简短证明定出了那个上界。
senses.why: The method travelled into computing and the social sciences, and the job title travelled with it.
senses.whyCN: 这套方法走进了计算机与社会科学，职位名称也跟着走。

senses.title: An amateur who collects data
senses.titleCN: 参与采集数据的业余研究者
senses.definition: a member of the public who gathers observations for a real study, usually called a citizen scientist
senses.definitionCN: 为真实研究采集观察资料、通常称为公民科学家的公众成员
senses.example: The scientist leading the bird count trained volunteers in the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 主持鸟类统计的那位研究人员在山谷里培训志愿者。
senses.why: Large studies need eyes everywhere, so the name widened to include trained helpers who are not paid researchers.
senses.whyCN: 大型研究需要到处都有眼睛，于是这个名称扩展到受训的帮手，即使他们不是受薪研究者。

senses.title: An expert who advises government
senses.definition: a researcher employed or consulted by a public body to give technical advice
senses.definitionCN: 受公共机构雇用或咨询、提供技术意见的研究者
senses.example: The government scientist warned that the river would rise again.
senses.exampleCN: 那位政府科研人员警告河水还会再涨。
senses.why: A government needs technical answers it cannot get from the bench, so it keeps its own researchers.
senses.whyCN: 政府需要实验台给不出的技术答案，于是养着自己的研究人员。

senses.title: A very clever person, in an idiom
senses.definition: in the fixed phrase rocket scientist, used ironically for a person of great or (in the negative) limited intelligence
senses.definitionCN: 在固定说法「火箭专家」中，用来反讽极聪明或（加否定时）极不聪明的人
senses.example: It does not take a scientist to see that the plan will fail.
senses.exampleCN: 看出这个计划要失败，并不需要什么专家。
senses.why: The hardest technical field became the yardstick for cleverness, and the phrase now works both ways.
senses.whyCN: 最难的技术领域成了聪明的标尺，这个说法于是正反两用。

senses.title: A researcher inside a company
senses.definition: a researcher employed by industry to develop products or processes
senses.definitionCN: 受雇于企业、开发产品或工艺的研究者
senses.example: A scientist at the plant found a cheaper way to coat the glass.
senses.exampleCN: 厂里的一位研究人员找到了更便宜的玻璃镀膜方法。
senses.why: Industry hired the same trained people for product work, and the title moved from campus to plant.
senses.whyCN: 企业雇用同样受过训练的人做产品，这个头衔就从校园走到了工厂。

senses.title: The figure in stories
senses.definition: the stock character of a researcher in fiction, often drawn as brilliant, obsessive or reckless
senses.definitionCN: 虚构作品中常见的科研人员形象，常被画成聪明、执拗或不顾后果
senses.example: The scientist in the novel refuses to publish and hides the result.
senses.exampleCN: 小说里那位科学家拒绝发表，把结果藏了起来。
senses.why: Fiction needs a figure to stand for curiosity without limits, and the word supplied that costume.
senses.whyCN: 虚构作品需要一个代表无边界好奇心的形象，这个词提供了那身行头。

intro.en: Scientist is an English coinage of 1833: scientia with the agent ending -ist. William Whewell proposed it because man of science was clumsy, and the word was mocked before it became ordinary.
intro.cn: scientist 是英语在一八三三年的新造词，由 scientia 加表示从业者的词尾 -ist 构成。惠威尔提出它，是因为「科学人」这一说法太笨重；在普遍使用之前，它一度受到嘲笑。

items.en: Scientia meant knowledge in general, and it supplied the first half of the new English word.
items.cn: scientia 泛指知识，为新英语词提供前半部分。

items.en: The ending came through Latin -ista from Greek -istes, naming a person who practises an art or a field.
items.cn: 这个表示从业者的词尾经拉丁语 -ista 来自希腊语 -istes，指从事某门技艺或领域的人。

items.en: Whewell proposed scientist in a review of Somerville's survey of physical science, wanting a word parallel to artist.
items.cn: 惠威尔在评论萨默维尔那部物理科学综述时提出 scientist，想要一个与 artist 平行的词。

items.en: The new word was resented by some scholars because it sounded like a mere trade label; the objection is well recorded.
items.cn: 一些学者不喜欢这个新词，因为它听起来只是一个行业标签；这一反对意见记录充分。

items.en: In the later nineteenth century the word settled into use as laboratories, chairs and doctorates made research a career.
items.cn: 十九世纪后期，随着实验室、教席与博士学位使研究成为职业，这个词才稳定下来。

items.en: The twentieth century built compounds such as computer scientist, and the twenty-first added citizen scientist for trained volunteers.
items.cn: 二十世纪造出计算机科学家一类复合词，二十一世纪又加上公民科学家，指受过训练的志愿者。

note.en: The first group shares the science stem or looks close; the second group names neighbouring roles.
note.cn: 第一组共享「科学」词干或形近；第二组是意思相邻的职位。

entries.definition: The field itself, from which the person noun was cut.
entries.definitionCN: 领域本身，表示人的名词正是由它截取而来。

entries.definition: The adjective for method or content that follows testing.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指遵循检验的方法或内容。

entries.definition: The adverb for doing something by tested method.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，指以经检验的方法去做。

entries.definition: An excessive claim that science can answer every question; a criticism, not a job.
entries.definitionCN: 指科学能回答一切问题的过头主张；是批评用语，并非职业。

entries.definition: The adjective for that overreaching attitude.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指那种越界态度的。

entries.definition: The broad word for anyone who looks for new findings, in any field.
entries.definitionCN: 广义说法，指任何领域寻找新发现的人。

entries.definition: A learned person in the humanities as much as the sciences.
entries.definitionCN: 博学之人，人文与科学领域都可用。

entries.definition: The person who runs the trial, with less weight on training or title.
entries.definitionCN: 实际做试验的人，对训练与头衔的强调更少。

entries.definition: A researcher who leads a study, or an official who inquiries into events.
entries.definitionCN: 领导一项研究的研究者，或查证事件的官方人员。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the 1833 coinage, the real family and the fixed phrases of fields and jobs.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用一八三三年的造词事实、真实同族词，以及领域与职位里的固定说法。

normal.en: The word is dated: Whewell put scientist into print in 1833, beside artist as a parallel.
normal.cn: 这个词有明确年代：惠威尔一八三三年把 scientist 写进文章，与 artist 平行。

normal.en: The family runs science, scientific, scientifically, scientist and scientism.
normal.cn: 同族词有 science、scientific、scientifically、scientist 与 scientism。

normal.en: Field names go in front: materials scientist, computer scientist, social scientist.
normal.cn: 领域名放在前面：材料科学家、计算机科学家、社会科学家。

normal.en: Citizen scientist names a trained volunteer who collects real observations.
normal.cn: 公民科学家指采集真实观察资料、受过训练的志愿者。

normal.en: Rocket scientist is an idiom for a very clever person, and in the negative for the opposite.
normal.cn: 火箭专家是形容极聪明者的习语，加否定则指反面。

abstract.en: A scientist is someone who would rather be wrong in a way that can be checked than right in a way that cannot.
abstract.cn: 科学家宁愿以可被核对的方式错，也不愿以无法核对的方式对。

abstract.en: The title is a job description, not a badge of wisdom.
abstract.cn: 这个头衔是职位说明，不是智慧的徽章。

abstract.en: What makes the figure trustworthy is the notebook, not the white coat.
abstract.cn: 让这个形象可信的是记录本，而不是白大褂。

examples.en: A scientist must report the conditions that would have made the result fail.
examples.cn: 科学家必须报告哪些条件会让结果站不住。

examples.en: The scientist spent the morning calibrating the balance.
examples.cn: 这位科研人员花了一上午校准天平。

examples.en: No scientist would call one successful run a settled law.
examples.cn: 没有哪位科学家会把一次成功的实验称作定论。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「赛恩提斯特」——整天在实验室里追着数据问为什么的人：科学家

root: 拉丁语 scientia「知识」+ 表示从业者的词尾 -ist；惠威尔一八三三年仿 artist 造出，最初遭讥，后随实验室职业化而定型。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one white coat: the professional researcher, the hands at the bench, the field-named specialist, the method carrier in any discipline, the citizen volunteer, the government adviser, the clever figure in an idiom, the industrial researcher and the character in fiction.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟着一件白大褂：职业研究者、实验台前的那双手、以领域命名的专家、把方法带到任何学科的人、公民志愿者、政府顾问、习语里的聪明人、企业研究者与虚构人物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: at three in the morning someone checks the same readings again and circles what does not fit.
core.cn: 核心意象：凌晨三点，有人把同一组读数再核一遍，把对不上的地方圈出来。

branches.en: THE PROFESSION AND ITS BRANCHES: a paid researcher, and a specialist named by the field in front.
branches.cn: 职业与分支：受薪研究者，以及把领域名放在前面的专家。

branches.en: THE HANDS: pipetting at a university bench or coating glass in a plant.
branches.cn: 那双手：在大学实验台移液，或在工厂给玻璃镀膜。

branches.en: THE SPREADING METHOD: computer scientists, and trained volunteers counting birds.
branches.cn: 扩散的方法：计算机科学家，以及数鸟的受训志愿者。

branches.en: THE PUBLIC FACE: an adviser warning a government, and the clever figure of an idiom.
branches.cn: 公众面孔：向政府发出警告的顾问，与习语里的聪明人。

branches.en: THE STORY FIGURE: the obsessive researcher whom fiction dresses in a white coat.
branches.cn: 故事人物：虚构作品给它穿上白大褂的执拗研究者。

intro.en: Scientist joins a Latin knowledge noun to a Greek-derived agent ending; it is a modern English compound, not a Latin word.
intro.cn: scientist 把拉丁语的知识名词与源自希腊语的从业者词尾接在一起；它是现代英语的复合词，不是拉丁语词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is scientia and the borrowed ending -ista, with sciens behind the noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语成分是 scientia 与借入的词尾 -ista，名词背后还有分词 sciens。

items.example: The word was proposed, not inherited.
items.exampleCN: 这个词是被人提出的，不是承袭来的。

items.example: It gave the first half of the coinage.
items.exampleCN: 它提供了新造词的前半部分。

items.example: The verb sits at the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整个词族的根。

items.example: It made artist, scientist and many trade names.
items.exampleCN: 它造出了艺术家、科学家与许多行业名称。

items.example: The English ending is the working shape of the suffix.
items.exampleCN: 英语词尾是该后缀在实际使用中的形态。

items.example: The adjective marks method rather than the person.
items.exampleCN: 形容词标的是方法，不是人。

items.example: The suffix turns a field into a disputed ideology.
items.exampleCN: 词尾把领域变成有争议的意识形态。

items.example: The compound marks the unpaid end of the scale.
items.exampleCN: 复合词标出这根标尺上不受薪的一端。

items.meaning: an idiom for a clever person
items.example: The phrase works by irony as well as praise.
items.exampleCN: 这个说法既能反讽，也能称赞。

latinEntries.example: The noun supplies the first half of scientist.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 这个名词提供 scientist 的前半部分。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb scire (sci-, scitum; to know)
latinEntries.example: The verb is the oldest element behind science.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 这个动词是 science 背后最古老的成分。

latinEntries.example: The coinage scientist used the -ista ending already present in artist.
latinEntries.exampleCN: scientist 的造词沿用了 artist 中已有的 -ista 词尾。

latinEntries.example: It builds scientificus, making or producing knowledge.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它构成 scientificus，意为「造成知识的」。

definition_zh: 调查者；查证人员；科研项目负责人；侦探；审查者
definition_en: a person who carries out a systematic inquiry into an event, a claim or a research question
core_image: 火烧过的仓库里，一个人蹲着给每块残片编号，用粉笔画出可能的起火点
scene: 火灾过后，调查员在仓库废墟里给每块残片编号，标出最可能的起火位置。The investigator marked each fragment before moving it.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项：对事件进行系统查证的人；句意为这位调查者在搬动之前先给每块残片做标记。图中可辨识物件：编号纸牌、粉笔圈、烧焦的梁、相机。

collocations.zh: 项目负责人；首席研究员

senses.title: The person who inquires into an event
senses.definition: a person appointed to find out how an accident, fire or crime happened
senses.definitionCN: 受命查明事故、火灾或犯罪经过的人
senses.example: The investigator marked each fragment before moving it.
senses.exampleCN: 这位调查者在搬动之前先给每块残片做标记。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to track footprints, so the first figure is someone following a trace to its source.
senses.whyCN: 那个拉丁动词本指循着脚印追踪，因此这个词最初指顺着痕迹找到源头的人。

senses.title: The lead researcher of a study
senses.definition: the researcher who takes official responsibility for the design and conduct of a study
senses.definitionCN: 对一项研究的设计与实施负正式责任的研究者
senses.example: The investigator enrolled forty patients in the trial.
senses.exampleCN: 这位项目负责人把四十名患者纳入试验。
senses.why: A study needs one name answerable for its conduct, so research borrowed the word for a systematic inquiry.
senses.whyCN: 一项研究需要一个为实施负责的名字，于是科研借用了这个表示系统查证的词。

senses.title: A police detective
senses.definition: a police officer whose work is to solve crimes by gathering and testing evidence
senses.definitionCN: 以收集并检验证据来破案的警官
senses.example: The investigator interviewed the night porter twice.
senses.exampleCN: 这名警探两次询问了夜班门房。
senses.why: Detection is inquiry with powers of arrest, and the older word for inquiry fitted the new office.
senses.whyCN: 侦查是带有逮捕权的查证，那个表示查证的旧词正好配这个新职位。

senses.title: A private detective
senses.definition: a person hired privately to gather information, often for a client in a dispute
senses.definitionCN: 受私人雇用收集信息的人，常为纠纷中的一方服务
senses.example: A private investigator traced the missing payment.
senses.exampleCN: 一名私人侦探追查了那笔失踪的付款。
senses.why: When the state will not inquire, a client can pay someone to do it, and the same title follows the money.
senses.whyCN: 当官方不肯查时，当事人可以出钱请人查，同一个头衔就跟着钱走。

senses.title: A regulator who checks compliance
senses.definition: an official who examines whether a company or public body has followed the rules
senses.definitionCN: 审查公司或公共机构是否守规的官员
senses.example: The investigator found that the waste had been buried illegally.
senses.exampleCN: 这位审查人员发现废料被非法掩埋。
senses.why: Regulation is inquiry into compliance, and the officer needs the same patience with documents.
senses.whyCN: 监管就是查是否守规，而这位官员同样需要对文件有耐心。

senses.title: The physician running a trial
senses.definition: a clinician responsible for testing a treatment on participants under a protocol
senses.definitionCN: 按试验方案在参与者身上检验治疗方法的临床医生
senses.example: The investigator stopped the trial when the side effects appeared.
senses.exampleCN: 副作用出现时，这位研究者中止了试验。
senses.why: A trial has a protocol, a sponsor and one responsible doctor, and that doctor carries the title.
senses.whyCN: 试验有方案、有申办方，还有一位负责医生，那位医生就带着这个头衔。

senses.title: A reporter who digs
senses.definition: a journalist who searches documents and interviews to expose a hidden matter
senses.definitionCN: 通过查文件、访证人以揭露隐情的记者
senses.example: The investigator spent a year on the land records.
senses.exampleCN: 这位调查记者在土地档案上花了一年。
senses.why: Journalism adopted the word once reporting began to follow documents the way a detective follows traces.
senses.whyCN: 当报道开始像侦探循迹那样追查文件，新闻业就采用了这个词。

senses.title: The forensic specialist
senses.definition: a specialist who examines physical traces for legal purposes
senses.definitionCN: 为法律目的检验物证的专家
senses.example: The investigator matched the tyre mark to a van.
senses.exampleCN: 这位法医调查员把轮胎印与一辆货车对上了。
senses.why: A trace on the ground is literally a footprint, and the Latin root of the word means exactly that.
senses.whyCN: 地上的痕迹字面上就是脚印，而这个词的拉丁词根正是指脚印。

senses.title: Anyone who examines a question closely
senses.definition: a person who studies a question carefully, even without official authority
senses.definitionCN: 即使没有官方授权、也仔细研究某个问题的人
senses.example: A careful investigator of the manuscripts dates them by their ink.
senses.exampleCN: 一位细究手稿的人按墨迹给它们断代。
senses.why: The word keeps its general sense of following a trace, which any careful reader can do.
senses.whyCN: 这个词保留了「循迹」的一般含义，任何细心的读者都能做这件事。

intro.en: Investigator comes from Latin investigare 'to search into', built on vestigare 'to track' and vestigium 'footprint'. English took the word in the sixteenth century, and its police and research senses came later.
intro.cn: investigator 来自拉丁语 investigare「查究」，由 vestigare「追踪」与 vestigium「脚印」构成。英语在十六世纪引入该词，警务与科研两种用法则是后来才有的。

items.en: Vestigium meant a footprint or a trace left on the ground, the same noun that gives English vestige.
items.cn: vestigium 指地上的脚印或痕迹，英语 vestige 正出自同一名词。

items.en: Vestigare meant to follow a track, to trace out a path by the marks left behind.
items.cn: vestigare 意为循着踪迹走，凭留下的印记找出一条路径。

items.en: Adding in- turned tracking into searching into a matter, and the verb came to mean inquire thoroughly.
items.cn: 加上 in- 之后，循迹变成深入一件事内部去查，动词于是意为彻底查究。

items.en: The agent noun named the person who does the searching; English borrowed the pattern rather than the exact form.
items.cn: 表示施事的名词指进行查究的人；英语借的是这一构词方式，而非完全相同的词形。

items.en: Investigate and investigator entered English in the sixteenth century, first in learned and legal writing.
items.cn: investigate 与 investigator 在十六世纪进入英语，最初见于学术与法律文字。

items.en: The nineteenth century gave the word to detectives, and the twentieth gave it to the doctor who runs a trial.
items.cn: 十九世纪把这个词给了侦探，二十世纪又给了主持试验的医生。

note.en: The first group shares the footprint root or merely looks like it; the second group names related roles.
note.cn: 第一组共享「脚印」词根或只是形近；第二组是相关职位。

entries.definition: The verb: to search into a matter by following evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 动词：顺着证据查究一件事。

entries.definition: The inquiry itself, with its documents and interviews.
entries.definitionCN: 查究过程本身，连同文件与询问。

entries.definition: The adjective for reporting or work that digs into evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指深挖证据的报道或工作。

entries.definition: A small remaining trace of something gone; literally a footprint left behind.
entries.definitionCN: 某物消失后留下的小痕迹；字面就是留下的脚印。

entries.definition: To put money or effort in; from a Latin verb meaning to clothe, not to track.
entries.definitionCN: 投入金钱或精力；出自意为「穿衣」的拉丁动词，与追踪无关。

entries.definition: Anyone who looks for new findings, with less official weight.
entries.definitionCN: 寻找新发现的人，官方色彩更淡。

entries.definition: A police or private officer who solves crimes; the everyday word for the police sense.
entries.definitionCN: 侦破案件的警探或私家侦探；警务义上的日常说法。

entries.definition: An official who checks that rules are met, closer to the regulatory sense.
entries.definitionCN: 检查规则是否被遵守的官员，更贴近监管义。

entries.definition: A person who tests or questions something closely, often in an exam or audit.
entries.definitionCN: 仔细查验或提问的人，常用于考试或审计。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the footprint root, the real family and the fixed titles of research and policing.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用「脚印」词根、真实同族词，以及科研与警务中的固定头衔。

normal.en: Latin vestigium meant footprint, so the investigator is the one who follows the marks on the ground.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 vestigium 意为脚印，调查者就是顺着地上印记走的人。

normal.en: The family runs investigate, investigation, investigator, investigative and vestige.
normal.cn: 同族词有 investigate、investigation、investigator、investigative 与 vestige。

normal.en: Research has a principal investigator, policing has a lead investigator, and both answer for the inquiry.
normal.cn: 科研有项目负责人，警务有主办调查员，两者都为查证负责。

normal.en: A fire investigator starts where the burn is deepest and works outward.
normal.cn: 火灾调查员从烧得最深的地方开始，再向外推。

normal.en: The private investigator is the same job bought with a client's money.
normal.cn: 私人侦探是同一份工作，只是由当事人出钱买下。

abstract.en: To investigate is to refuse the first explanation until the traces agree with it.
abstract.cn: 调查就是拒绝第一个解释，直到痕迹与它吻合。

abstract.en: An investigator is judged by what was written down, not by what was suspected.
abstract.cn: 调查者的分量取决于记录了什么，而不是怀疑了什么。

abstract.en: Every inquiry begins with something left behind, and that is why the root means footprint.
abstract.cn: 每次查究都从某个留下的东西开始，这正是词根意为脚印的原因。

examples.en: The investigator sealed the room before collecting the samples.
examples.cn: 调查人员在采集样品前封住了房间。

examples.en: As principal investigator she signed the protocol on behalf of the team.
examples.cn: 作为项目负责人，她代表团队签署了试验方案。

examples.en: The investigator's report named three failures in the safety system.
examples.cn: 调查者的报告点出安全体系中的三处失效。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「因维斯蒂给特」——顺着脚印一路追进去的人：调查者

root: 拉丁语 vestigium「脚印」→ vestigare「循迹」→ investigare「查究」→ investigator「查究者」；英语十六世纪引入，十九世纪起用于侦探，二十世纪起用于科研负责人。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one set of footprints: the official inquiry, the study leader, the detective, the private eye, the compliance officer, the trial doctor, the digging reporter, the forensic specialist and any careful examiner.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟着同一串脚印：官方查证、研究负责人、警探、私家侦探、合规审查员、试验医生、深挖的记者、法医专家，以及任何细究问题的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: in a burnt warehouse a figure numbers every fragment and chalk-marks the likely origin.
core.cn: 核心意象：烧毁的仓库里，一个人给每块残片编号，用粉笔标出可能的起火点。

branches.en: THE TRACE: an official reading the marks of a fire, a forensic specialist reading a tyre print.
branches.cn: 痕迹：读火灾印记的官方人员，读轮胎印的法医专家。

branches.en: THE STUDY: the name on the protocol, and the doctor who stops a trial when harm appears.
branches.cn: 研究：方案上署名的负责人，以及见伤害就中止试验的医生。

branches.en: THE DETECTIVE: public inquiry with powers of arrest, private inquiry bought by a client.
branches.cn: 侦探：带逮捕权的公开查证，与当事人出钱买的私人查证。

branches.en: THE CHECKER: an officer testing compliance, a reporter testing a public story.
branches.cn: 查核者：检验是否守规的官员，检验公开说法的记者。

branches.en: THE CAREFUL READER: anyone who follows a trace through documents and dates them.
branches.cn: 细心的读者：任何顺着痕迹查文件、为它们断代的人。

intro.en: Investigator is a Latin verb plus a Latin agent noun ending; the root image is a footprint on the ground.
intro.cn: investigator 由一个拉丁动词加一个拉丁施事名词词尾构成，词根意象是地上的脚印。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer runs vestigium, vestigare, investigare and the agent ending -ator.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语成分包括 vestigium、vestigare、investigare 与施事词尾 -ator。

items.meaning: one who searches into a matter
items.example: The agent noun makes the inquiry a person.
items.exampleCN: 施事名词把查究变成一个人。

items.example: The concrete image stayed in English as vestige.
items.exampleCN: 这个具体意象在英语里留下了表示残迹的那个词。

items.example: The verb describes movement along marks, not speculation.
items.exampleCN: 动词描述沿印记移动，而非凭空推测。

items.example: The prefix turns tracking into an inquiry.
items.exampleCN: 前缀把循迹变成查究。

items.example: It is the same prefix seen in invade and intend.
items.exampleCN: 同一前缀也见于「侵入」与「打算」两个词。

items.example: It builds investigator, creator and narrator.
items.exampleCN: 它构成调查者、创造者与叙述者。

items.example: English keeps the verb beside the person noun.
items.exampleCN: 英语动词与人名词并存。

items.example: The abstract noun names the process.
items.exampleCN: 抽象名词命名过程。

items.example: The noun kept the literal footprint image.
items.exampleCN: 该名词保留了字面的脚印意象。

items.meaning: to put money or effort in
items.example: It clothes rather than tracks, and only looks related.
items.exampleCN: 它意为穿衣而非追踪，只是看起来相关。

latinEntries.example: Latin vestigium means footprint, the trace one follows.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 vestigium 意为脚印，即可供追踪的痕迹。

latinEntries.example: Latin vestigare means to follow a trace, to track.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 vestigare 意为循迹追踪。

latinEntries.example: Latin investigare means to track into, to search out.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 investigare 意为循迹而入，即查究。

latinEntries.example: Latin -ator builds nouns such as imperator, commander.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 -ator 构成 imperator（统帅）这类名词。

definition_zh: 假设；提出假说；假定（以便检验或推理）
definition_en: to propose a tentative explanation that can be tested, or to assume something for the sake of argument
core_image: 白板中央写着一个尚未验证的猜测，旁边画出一条通向可测结果的箭头
scene: 讨论会上，研究者在白板中央写下一条还没验证的解释，再画出检验它的步骤。They hypothesize that the mould grows faster in damp air.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项：提出一个尚待检验的解释；句意为他们假定霉菌在潮湿空气中长得更快。图中可辨识物件：白板、箭头、问号、记录贴。

pos.zh: 假设；提出假说；假定（可及物或接从句）

senses.title: To propose a testable explanation
senses.definition: to put forward an explanation that further observation or experiment can support or contradict
senses.definitionCN: 提出一种能由后续观察或实验支持或否定的解释
senses.example: They hypothesize that the mould grows faster in damp air.
senses.exampleCN: 他们假定霉菌在潮湿空气中长得更快。
senses.why: A hypothesis is a placing under, a foundation laid down so that a test can stand on it, which is why the verb needs something checkable.
senses.whyCN: 假说字面上是垫在下面的基座，先铺好基础，检验才能站上去，因此这个动词要求的正是可被检验的内容。

senses.title: To assume for an argument
senses.definition: to take something as true temporarily in order to work out what would follow
senses.definitionCN: 为推出后续结论而暂时把某事当作真的
senses.example: Let us hypothesize a world without friction and see what fails.
senses.exampleCN: 让我们假定一个没有摩擦的世界，看看什么会失灵。
senses.why: In a proof or a debate, a supposition is a working floor rather than a claim about reality.
senses.whyCN: 在证明或辩论里，假定只是临时地板，并非关于现实的主张。

senses.title: To guess without much evidence
senses.definition: to offer a guess about a cause or a possibility, often in ordinary conversation
senses.definitionCN: 对成因或可能性给出猜测，常用于日常谈话
senses.example: He hypothesized about the noise but never checked the roof.
senses.exampleCN: 他对那阵响声作了猜测，却从没上屋顶查看。
senses.why: The scientific word keeps a weaker everyday use, where the guess is not yet tied to a test.
senses.whyCN: 这个科学词保留了较弱的日常用法，此时猜测尚未与检验挂钩。

senses.title: To predict a specific outcome
senses.definition: to state in advance what a model or theory implies should happen in a given case
senses.definitionCN: 预先说明模型或理论在特定情形下应当产生什么结果
senses.example: The team hypothesized a rise of two degrees and set the sensor to catch it.
senses.exampleCN: 团队预测会上升两度，并设好传感器去捕捉它。
senses.why: Once a model is written, its next case is a prediction, and the verb marks the step from model to expected number.
senses.whyCN: 模型写成之后，下一个情形就是预测，这个动词标出从模型到预期数字的一步。

senses.title: To state a statistical relation
senses.titleCN: 在统计中假定某种关系
senses.definition: to frame a relation between variables as a hypothesis to be tested against data
senses.definitionCN: 把变量之间的关系表述成待用数据检验的假说
senses.example: We hypothesize a link between sleep and recall.
senses.exampleCN: 我们假定睡眠与回忆之间存在联系。
senses.why: Statistics needs a statement precise enough to be rejected, and the verb supplies that statement.
senses.whyCN: 统计学需要一个精确到能被否定的陈述，这个动词提供的就是那个陈述。

senses.title: To reconstruct a possible past
senses.definition: to propose what may have happened in the past from the traces that remain
senses.definitionCN: 根据残留痕迹提出过去可能发生了什么
senses.example: Historians hypothesize a trading post beneath the car park.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学者假定停车场下面曾有一个贸易站。
senses.why: When no document survives, the past can only be rebuilt as supposition, and the word fits that limit.
senses.whyCN: 没有文件留存时，过去只能作为假定重建，这个词正好承认这一限制。

senses.title: To posit something unseen
senses.definition: to propose the existence of an entity that has not yet been detected, because a theory requires it
senses.definitionCN: 因理论需要而提出某物的存在，尽管尚未探测到
senses.example: Physicists hypothesized a particle that no detector had yet found.
senses.exampleCN: 物理学家假定了一种尚无探测器找到的粒子。
senses.why: A theory can demand a missing piece, and naming it in advance is how the search is organised.
senses.whyCN: 理论可能需要一块缺失的拼图，提前给它命名正是组织搜寻的方式。

senses.title: To ask learners to predict
senses.definition: in teaching, to ask students to state what they expect before they observe or test
senses.definitionCN: 在教学中让学生先说出预期，再去观察或检验
senses.example: The teacher asked the class to hypothesize before adding the acid.
senses.exampleCN: 老师让全班在加酸之前先作假设。
senses.why: A prediction made before the demonstration gives the learner a stake in the result.
senses.whyCN: 在演示之前先作预测，能让学习者与结果产生切身关系。

senses.title: To form a working guess in practice
senses.titleCN: 在实践中先立一个可用的猜测
senses.definition: to adopt a provisional explanation while solving a practical problem, ready to drop it if it fails
senses.definitionCN: 在解决实际问题时先采用一个临时解释，一旦失败就放弃
senses.example: The mechanic hypothesized a blocked filter and tested it first.
senses.exampleCN: 修车工先假定滤芯堵塞，并优先验证这一点。
senses.why: A working guess saves time by directing the next test, even before any formal study exists.
senses.whyCN: 可用的猜测通过指明下一步测试来省时间，即使还没有正式研究。

intro.en: Hypothesize is an English verb built on hypothesis, from Greek hypothesis 'a placing under, a foundation'. The Greeks used it for a geometric base, and the modern sense of a testable supposition grew from that.
intro.cn: hypothesize 是在名词 hypothesis 上加动词词尾构成的英语动词；hypothesis 来自希腊语，意为「垫在下面、基座」。希腊人用它指几何中的基础，现代「可检验的假定」这一义正是从那里长出来的。

items.en: The prefix meant under or beneath, the same element that gives hypodermic and a hypothesis laid under a claim.
items.cn: 这个前缀意为在下面，与「皮下」一词同源；假说就是垫在主张下面的东西。

items.en: Thesis meant a placing or setting down, from tithenai 'to put', the verb behind theme and thesis.
items.cn: thesis 意为放置、放下，出自 tithenai「放」，也是 theme 与 thesis 的词根。

items.en: In geometry a hypothesis was the base or assumption on which a proof stood; in ordinary speech it was a supposition.
items.cn: 在几何里，假说是证明所站立的基座或前提；在日常说法里，它是一个假定。

items.en: Latin took hypothesis as a term of logic, and English borrowed it in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 拉丁语把假说作为逻辑术语接收，英语在十六世纪将其借入。

items.en: English formed hypothesize on the noun with the productive ending -ize; the verb is recorded from the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 英语用能产的词尾 -ize 在名词上造出这个动词，十七世纪已有记录。

items.en: In the nineteenth and twentieth centuries the verb settled into the method of stating a testable prediction before measuring.
items.cn: 十九与二十世纪，这个动词固定为「先陈述可检验的预测、再测量」的方法步骤。

note.en: The first group shares the hypothesis stem, with one false friend; the second group names weaker or stronger ways of positing.
note.cn: 第一组共享「假说」词干，其中有一个假朋友；第二组是程度不同的设定方式。
