entries.definition: The noun: a testable explanation, plural hypotheses with the Greek -es ending.
entries.definitionCN: 名词：可检验的解释，复数保留希腊式词尾。

entries.definition: The adjective: supposed rather than established.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词：属于假定而非已确立的。

entries.definition: The adverb: in a supposed case, not in fact.
entries.definitionCN: 副词：在假定情形下，而非事实中。

entries.definition: To pledge property as security; from a Greek word for a pledge, not a supposition.
entries.definitionCN: 以财产作抵押担保；出自希腊语中表示抵押的词，与假定无关。

entries.definition: A person who proposes hypotheses, a rare but regular agent noun.
entries.definitionCN: 提出假说的人，罕见但合乎构词规则。

entries.definition: To reason from incomplete evidence, with less commitment to testing.
entries.definitionCN: 凭不完整证据推理，对检验的承诺更弱。

entries.definition: To take something as a starting principle without deriving it.
entries.definitionCN: 把某事当作出发点，而不加推导。

entries.definition: To form an opinion on thin evidence; the noun is commoner than the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 凭薄弱证据形成看法；名词比动词更常用。

entries.definition: The everyday word for taking something as true for now.
entries.definitionCN: 日常说法，指暂时把某事当作真的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Greek 'placing under', the real family and the fixed frames of research writing.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用希腊语「垫在下面」这一构词意象、真实同族词，以及科研写作里的固定框架。

normal.en: Greek hypothesis was a base laid under a proof, and a testable guess is still a floor to stand on.
normal.cn: 希腊语中的假说是铺在证明下面的基座，可检验的猜测至今仍是站立的地板。

normal.en: The family runs hypothesis, hypothesize, hypothetical, hypothetically and hypothesizer.
normal.cn: 同族词有 hypothesis、hypothesize、hypothetical、hypothetically 与 hypothesizer。

normal.en: Research writing fixes the frame: hypothesize that, hypothesize a relationship, test a hypothesized link.
normal.cn: 科研写作有固定框架：假定……、假定某种关系、检验假定的联系。

normal.en: The plural of the noun is hypotheses, keeping the Greek ending.
normal.cn: 名词复数是 hypotheses，保留了希腊语词尾。

normal.en: Hypothecate looks identical in front but means to pledge property, not to suppose.
normal.cn: hypothecate 前半截相同，意思却是抵押财产，而非假定。

abstract.en: To hypothesize is to build a floor you are willing to remove.
abstract.cn: 提出假说，就是搭一层你愿意拆掉的地板。

abstract.en: A guess becomes a hypothesis only when it says what would count against it.
abstract.cn: 猜测只有在说清什么能反驳它时，才成为假说。

abstract.en: The sentence that can be tested is worth more than the sentence that sounds certain.
abstract.cn: 能被检验的句子，比听起来肯定的句子更有价值。

examples.en: The team hypothesized that the two groups would differ by one grade.
examples.cn: 团队假定两组会相差一个等级。

examples.en: It is easy to hypothesize a cause and hard to rule one out.
examples.cn: 假定一个成因很容易，排除一个却很难。

examples.en: She hypothesized a second pathway before the first was mapped.
examples.cn: 在第一条路径被画出之前，她就假定存在第二条。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「海剖塞赛兹」——先抛出一个猜想，再剖开来看真假：假设

root: 希腊语 hypo「在下」+ thesis「放置」→ hypothesis「垫在下面的基座、假定」；英语加 -ize 造出动词。其后缀化的 -ize 来自希腊语构词习惯，经拉丁语与法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one laid-down foundation: a testable explanation, a temporary assumption, a loose guess, a predicted outcome, a statistical relation, a rebuilt past, an unseen entity, a classroom prediction and a working guess in a workshop.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟着一块铺下的基座：可检验的解释、临时的假定、随口猜测、预测结果、统计关系、重建的过去、看不见的实体、课堂上的预测，以及车间里的临时猜测。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a guess is written in the middle of the board with an arrow drawn to the test that could break it.
core.cn: 核心意象：白板中央写下一个猜测，旁边画一支指向能推翻它的检验的箭头。

branches.en: THE TESTABLE CLAIM: an explanation and a stated relation, both precise enough to fail.
branches.cn: 可检验的主张：一个解释与一个关系陈述，两者都精确到可以失败。

branches.en: THE SUPPOSITION: a floor for argument, or a guess not yet tied to any test.
branches.cn: 假定：或为推理铺地板，或只是尚未与检验挂钩的猜测。

branches.en: THE PREDICTION: a number expected from a model, or a class asked to commit before the demo.
branches.cn: 预测：模型给出的预期数字，或让全班在演示前先下注。

branches.en: THE UNSEEN: a past rebuilt from traces, an entity named before it is found.
branches.cn: 看不见的东西：由痕迹重建的过去，与被找到之前先命名的实体。

branches.en: THE WORKING GUESS: a provisional cause adopted to decide which test comes first.
branches.cn: 临时猜测：先采用一个成因，用来决定先做哪项测试。

intro.en: Hypothesize joins a Greek compound noun to the productive verb ending -ize; the pieces are hypo, thesis and tithenai.
intro.cn: hypothesize 把希腊语复合名词与能产的动词词尾 -ize 接在一起，部件是 hypo、thesis 与 tithenai。

latinIntro.en: The word is Greek in origin and reached English through Latin; the Latin layer here is the borrowed noun hypothesis and the ending -izare.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词源自希腊语，经拉丁语进入英语；此处的拉丁语成分是借入的名词 hypothesis 与词尾 -izare。

items.example: The verb is English, the noun is Greek.
items.exampleCN: 动词是英语造的，名词来自希腊语。

items.example: It marks the base laid under a claim.
items.exampleCN: 它标出铺在主张下面的基座。

items.example: The noun names the act of putting something in place.
items.exampleCN: 名词命名把某物放到位的动作。

items.example: The verb is the far root of both thesis and theme.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是「放置」与「主题」两词的远根。

items.example: Geometry gave the word its first technical home.
items.exampleCN: 几何学给了这个词第一个专业归宿。

items.example: The ending turns nouns into verbs across English.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾在英语里把名词变成动词。

items.example: The adjective marks the status of the claim.
items.exampleCN: 形容词标出主张的地位。

items.example: The adverb sets the whole sentence in a supposition.
items.exampleCN: 副词把整句放进一个假定里。

items.example: It shares the prefix but not the supposition.
items.exampleCN: 它共享前缀，却没有「假定」之义。

latinEntries.structure: Greek hypothesis, from hypo- (under) + thesis (placing); borrowed into Latin
latinEntries.example: Latin took hypothesis from Greek with the meaning of a placed base.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语从希腊语借入 hypothesis，义为「垫在下面的基座」。

latinEntries.structure: Greek prefix hypo- (under), carried into Latin borrowings
latinEntries.example: Greek hypo- appears in Latin borrowings such as hypothesis.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 希腊语 hypo- 见于 hypothesis 这类拉丁借词。

latinEntries.structure: Medieval Latin verb ending -izare, from Greek -izein
latinEntries.example: Medieval Latin -izare builds verbs such as organizare.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 中世纪拉丁语 -izare 构成 organizare 这类动词。

latinEntries.structure: Greek thesis (a placing), from tithenai (to put)
latinEntries.example: Greek thesis means a placing, and Latin borrowed it unchanged.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 希腊语 thesis 意为放置，拉丁语原样借入。

definition_zh: 以原则为基础的；依据基本原则而非详尽细则运作的
definition_en: built on a small set of general principles rather than on detailed rules or listed cases
core_image: 一页只写三条原则的薄册子，旁边是一摞厚到压弯桌面的细则汇编
scene: 会议室里，委员会把厚厚一册细则推到一边，只在白板上留下三条原则。The principle-based charter left room for judgement in cases the drafters never imagined.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项：以若干基本原则为依据、而不依赖详尽条文的；句意为这份以原则为基础的章程，为起草者从未设想的情形留下了判断空间。图中可辨识物件：白板、三条短句、厚手册、被推开的文件夹。

pos.zh: 以原则为基础的；按原则而非细则运作的（多作定语，含连字符）

collocations.zh: 从基本原则出发的推理

derivatives.zh: 以细则为基础的（反义对照）

senses.title: Built on a few general principles
senses.titleCN: 建立在少数一般原则上的
senses.definition: designed so that a small set of general principles guides decisions instead of a long list of detailed rules
senses.definitionCN: 设计上让少数一般原则引导决定，而非依靠一长串细则
senses.example: The principle-based charter left room for judgement in cases the drafters never imagined.
senses.exampleCN: 这份以原则为基础的章程，为起草者从未设想的情形留下了判断空间。
senses.why: The compound names its own foundation: the principle is the base, and everything else is built upward from it.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词自己说明了地基：原则就是底座，其余都从它往上盖。

senses.title: Regulation that states outcomes
senses.definition: a regulatory style that states broad outcomes and lets firms decide how to reach them
senses.definitionCN: 一种监管风格，只规定宽泛的结果，让企业自行决定如何达到
senses.example: The regulator moved to a principle-based regime after the crisis.
senses.exampleCN: 危机之后，监管机构转向原则导向的制度。
senses.why: Detailed rules lag behind new products, so supervisors write principles broad enough to cover what they cannot yet name.
senses.whyCN: 详尽规则总落后于新产品，于是监管者写下足够宽的原则，覆盖他们尚不能命名的东西。

senses.title: Accounting guided by substance
senses.definition: an accounting system that sets broad principles and relies on professional judgement rather than exhaustive rules
senses.definitionCN: 只设宽泛原则、依赖专业判断而非穷尽规则的会计体系
senses.example: Principle-based accounting can record a lease that no rule anticipated.
senses.exampleCN: 原则导向的会计能记录规则未曾预料的租赁。
senses.why: A lease can be dressed to fit any rule, so standard setters describe the economic substance and leave the application to judgement.
senses.whyCN: 租赁可以被包装成符合任何规则的样子，因此准则制定者描述经济实质，把适用留给判断。

senses.title: Ethics founded on principles
senses.definition: an ethical method that derives judgements from general moral principles rather than from case lists
senses.definitionCN: 从一般道德原则推出判断、而非依赖案例清单的伦理方法
senses.example: A principle-based ethics asks what duty applies before asking what precedent fits.
senses.exampleCN: 以原则为根的伦理先问义务是什么，再问哪个先例适用。
senses.why: Case lists always meet a case they omit, while a principle can be applied to situations no author foresaw.
senses.whyCN: 案例清单总会遇到它漏掉的案例，而原则可以用于作者未曾预见的情形。

senses.title: Reasoning from first principles
senses.titleCN: 从基本原理出发的推理
senses.definition: a method of reasoning that starts from basic truths and builds conclusions step by step
senses.definitionCN: 从基本真出发、逐步建立结论的推理方法
senses.example: The engineer used principle-based reasoning to rebuild the pump from scratch.
senses.exampleCN: 这位工程师用从基本原理出发的推理，从头重建了水泵。
senses.why: Copying an existing design hides its assumptions; starting from principles exposes which parts are actually needed.
senses.whyCN: 照抄现成设计会掩盖其前提；从原理出发才能看出哪些部件真的必要。

senses.title: A curriculum built on big ideas
senses.definition: a course design that organizes teaching around a few central ideas instead of many isolated facts
senses.definitionCN: 围绕少数核心概念、而非大量孤立事实组织教学的课程设计
senses.example: The principle-based curriculum returns to the same idea in every unit.
senses.exampleCN: 以原则为纲的课程在每个单元都回到同一个核心概念。
senses.why: Facts are forgotten and principles are reused, so teachers build the year around what transfers.
senses.whyCN: 事实会被忘记，原则却能反复使用，因此教师围绕可迁移的东西安排全年。

senses.title: A design guided by stated principles
senses.titleCN: 按明示原则进行的设计
senses.definition: a design process in which a written set of principles decides trade-offs before specific choices are made
senses.definitionCN: 先由成文原则决定取舍、再作具体选择的设计过程
senses.example: The principle-based design kept the interface plain as features multiplied.
senses.exampleCN: 功能不断增加时，按原则进行的设计仍让界面保持朴素。
senses.why: When a new feature conflicts with an old one, a stated principle settles the argument without a meeting.
senses.whyCN: 当新功能与旧功能冲突时，一条明示原则不必开会就能裁决。

senses.title: Management by stated principles
senses.definition: a way of running an organization that trusts employees to apply stated principles rather than follow a manual
senses.definitionCN: 信任员工运用成文原则、而非照手册行事的管理方式
senses.example: A principle-based team decides locally and explains the decision afterwards.
senses.exampleCN: 以原则运作的团队就地决定，事后再解释理由。
senses.why: A manual cannot cover every situation a worker meets, so managers write principles and delegate the application.
senses.whyCN: 手册覆盖不了员工遇到的每种情况，于是管理者写下原则，把适用交给一线。

intro.en: Principle-based joins principle, from Latin principium 'beginning, foundation', to based, from Greek basis 'step, pedestal'. The hyphenated compound is a modern coinage of regulation, accounting and design writing.
intro.cn: principle-based 把 principle 与 based 接在一起：前者来自拉丁语 principium「开端、基础」，后者来自希腊语 basis「台阶、底座」。这个带连字符的复合词是监管、会计与设计写作中的现代造词。

items.en: Principium meant a beginning or first part, and from it came the English word for a rule that stands at the head of others.
items.cn: principium 意为开端或最初的部分，由此产生了英语中表示「统辖其余规则的那一条」的词。

items.en: Princeps 'first, chief' was built from primus 'first' and capere 'to take', literally the one who takes the first place.
items.cn: princeps「第一的、首领的」由 primus「第一」与 capere「抓取」构成，字面是占据首位者。

items.en: Both English words descend from the same family, but principle took the noun path and principal the adjective and office path; the split is well recorded.
items.cn: 两个英语词同出一族，但 principle 走名词一路，principal 走形容词与职位一路；这一分化记录充分。

items.en: Basis meant a step or pedestal, the thing a building or argument stands on; Latin took it as basis and English as base.
items.cn: basis 意为台阶或底座，是建筑或论证所立之物；拉丁语作 basis 接收，英语作 base。

items.en: English began writing principle-based as a hyphenated modifier in the later twentieth century, first in policy and standard-setting prose.
items.cn: 二十世纪后期，英语开始把这个词写成带连字符的定语，最早见于政策与准则制定文字。

items.en: The compound spread as the opposite of rules-based, a pairing that became standard in finance and regulation after the 1990s.
items.cn: 这个复合词作为 rules-based 的反面而传播，这一对举在二十世纪九十年代后成为金融与监管文字的标准搭配。

note.en: The first group shares one half of the compound or looks close; the second group names neighbouring approaches.
note.cn: 第一组共享复合词的一半或形近；第二组是相邻的做法。

entries.definition: A general rule or truth that other rules depend on.
entries.definitionCN: 其他规则所依赖的一般规则或真理。

entries.definition: A person or act that follows clear moral principles.
entries.definitionCN: 指人或行为遵循明确道德原则的。

entries.definition: Chief, or the head of a school; a different word despite the shared origin and sound.
entries.definitionCN: 首要的，或校长；虽同源同音，却是另一个词。

entries.definition: The foundation a thing rests on.
entries.definitionCN: 事物所依托的基础。

entries.definition: The lowest supporting part, or to found something on another.
entries.definitionCN: 最低的支撑部分，或把某物建立在另一物上。

entries.definition: Fundamental, forming the base of the rest.
entries.definitionCN: 基本的，构成其余部分的基础。

entries.definition: Built on detailed rules that try to list every case; the usual opposite.
entries.definitionCN: 建立在力图列举每种情况的细则之上；通常作为反面。

entries.definition: Guided by shared moral values rather than by procedure.
entries.definitionCN: 由共同价值而非程序引导的。

entries.definition: Guided by a theoretical model rather than by immediate data.
entries.definitionCN: 由理论模型而非眼前数据引导的。

entries.definition: The basic truths from which a subject is rebuilt.
entries.definitionCN: 用来重建一门学问的基本真理。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Latin first-place root, the basis image and the real contrast with rules-based writing.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用拉丁语「占首位」的词根、底座的意象，以及它与细则导向写作的真实对照。

normal.en: Principle came from the first place in a line, so a principle-based system is governed from the head, not the footnotes.
normal.cn: 原则一词本指队列之首，因此以原则为基础的系统由开头统辖，而非由脚注统辖。

normal.en: Based comes from a Greek pedestal, so the compound literally says what the pedestal is made of.
normal.cn: based 来自希腊语底座，这个复合词字面就说明了底座由什么制成。

normal.en: Principle and principal sound alike and share a root, but only principle names a rule.
normal.cn: principle 与 principal 同音同源，但只有前者指规则。

normal.en: Regulation, accounting and ethics all contrast principle-based with rules-based.
normal.cn: 监管、会计与伦理都把原则导向与细则导向对举。

normal.en: The phrase first-principles names the same idea in reasoning: start from the base, not from the finished model.
normal.cn: first-principles 在推理中表达同一想法：从底座出发，而非从成品模型出发。

abstract.en: A principle-based rule bends with the case; a rules-based one snaps when the case is new.
abstract.cn: 以原则为基础的规则随个案弯曲；细则导向的规则遇到新个案就折断。

abstract.en: Three principles on a whiteboard can outlast a shelf of manuals.
abstract.cn: 白板上的三条原则，可能比一整架手册活得更久。

abstract.en: The base is not the building, but nothing stands without it.
abstract.cn: 底座不是建筑本身，但没有它什么也立不住。

examples.en: A principle-based code tells staff why a decision is right, not only what to do.
examples.cn: 以原则为基础的守则告诉员工决定为何正确，而不只是该做什么。

examples.en: The bank adopted principle-based capital rules after the review.
examples.cn: 审查之后，这家银行采用了原则导向的资本规则。

examples.en: Her principle-based approach to hiring resisted the fashion of the year.
examples.cn: 她那种以原则为基础的招聘方式，抵制了当年的风气。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「普林西普-贝斯特」——先立几条普适原则，再把事情往上放：以原则为基础的

root: principle 来自拉丁语 principium「开端、基础」← princeps「占首位者」（primus + capere）；based 来自希腊语 basis「底座」经拉丁语进入英语。该复合词为二十世纪后期造词，常与 rules-based 对举。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one pedestal named principle: a general design, outcome-setting regulation, substance-led accounting, principle ethics, first-principles reasoning, a big-idea curriculum, principled design and management by stated principles.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着一块名为「原则」的底座：一般设计、只规定结果的监管、重实质的会计、以原则为根的伦理、从基本原理出发的推理、以大概念为纲的课程、按原则设计，以及按原则管理。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin charter with three principles sits beside a shelf of rules thick enough to bow the desk.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本只写三条原则的薄章程，旁边是一摞厚得压弯桌面的细则。

branches.en: THE GENERAL DESIGN AND ITS REGULATION: broad outcomes stated, application left open.
branches.cn: 总体设计与监管：只陈述宽泛结果，把适用留开。

branches.en: THE SUBSTANCE AND THE DERIVATION: accounting that follows economic reality, reasoning that starts from basics.
branches.cn: 实质与推导：跟随经济现实的会计，与从基本真出发的推理。

branches.en: THE TEACHING OF PRINCIPLES: ethics applied to new cases, a curriculum built on big ideas.
branches.cn: 原则的传授：用于新案例的伦理，与以大概念为纲的课程。

branches.en: THE DESIGN RULE: a written principle settling trade-offs before features multiply.
branches.cn: 设计规则：在功能增多之前，用成文原则裁决取舍。

branches.en: THE DELEGATED DECISION: staff apply the principle locally and explain afterwards.
branches.cn: 下放的判断：员工就地适用原则，事后说明理由。

intro.en: The compound joins a Latin principle to a Greek-derived base, and the hyphen marks it as a modifier rather than a sentence.
intro.cn: 这个复合词把拉丁语来源的 principle 与希腊语来源的 base 接在一起，连字符标明它作定语，而非独立成句。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is principium, princeps and primus, with capere behind princeps; basis is Greek, borrowed through Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语成分是 principium、princeps 与 primus，princeps 背后还有 capere；basis 是希腊语，经拉丁语借入。

items.example: The word keeps the image of a first place.
items.exampleCN: 这个词保留着「首位」的意象。

items.example: Latin made the abstract noun from the title of first place.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语由「首位」之名造出抽象名词。

items.example: Literally the one who takes the first place.
items.exampleCN: 字面是占据首位的人。

items.example: It also gives primary and prime.
items.exampleCN: 它也是「主要的」与「首要的」两词的来源。

items.example: The verb behind capture and receive.
items.exampleCN: 也是「捕获」与「接收」背后的动词。

items.example: A building or an argument stands on it.
items.exampleCN: 建筑或论证都立在它上面。

items.example: English uses it as noun and verb.
items.exampleCN: 英语中既可作名词也可作动词。

items.example: The suffix turns a noun into a modifier.
items.exampleCN: 这个构词成分把名词变成定语。

items.example: The hyphen keeps the two words one modifier.
items.exampleCN: 连字符把两个词合成一个定语。

items.example: It is the usual opposite in policy prose.
items.exampleCN: 在政策文字中常作反面对照。

latinEntries.example: Latin principium means beginning or foundation.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 principium 意为开端、基础。

latinEntries.example: Latin princeps literally means first taker, a leader.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 princeps 字面意为「首先拿取者」，即首领。

latinEntries.example: Latin primus means first and gives English primary.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 primus 意为第一，并给出英语 primary。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb capere (cap-, captum; to take)
latinEntries.example: Latin capere means to take, and its participle captus gives captive.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 capere 意为拿取，其分词 captus 给出 captive。

latinEntries.structure: Greek basis (step, pedestal), borrowed into Latin
latinEntries.example: Greek basis means a step or pedestal, the ground one stands on.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 希腊语 basis 意为台阶、底座，即站立的地基。

definition_zh: 科学定律；对自然现象中稳定关系的简洁陈述
definition_en: a concise statement, supported by repeated evidence, that describes a regular relationship in nature
core_image: 墙上挂着一块只写一条简洁等式的牌子，旁边贴满历年核对无误的数据表
scene: 物理教室的墙上挂着一块牌子，只写一条简洁的等式，旁边贴满历年核对过的数据。A scientific law describes what always happens under stated conditions, not why it happens.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项：经反复验证、描述自然中稳定关系的陈述；句意为科学定律说明在给定条件下总会发生什么，而不解释为何发生。图中可辨识物件：等式牌、数据表、图钉、坐标轴。

pos.zh: 科学定律；自然规律（可数）

collocations.zh: 违反科学定律（多作修辞）

collocations.phrase: a scientific law and a theory
collocations.zh: 科学定律与理论（常作对比）

senses.title: A statement of regularity
senses.definition: a concise statement that a certain relationship holds whenever the stated conditions are met
senses.definitionCN: 一条简洁陈述：只要满足所述条件，某种关系就成立
senses.example: A scientific law describes what always happens under stated conditions.
senses.exampleCN: 科学定律说明在给定条件下总会发生什么。
senses.why: The word law was borrowed from legal language for something laid down; here what is laid down is a regularity, not a command.
senses.whyCN: 「定律」一词借自法律语言，本指被立下的东西；在这里被立下的是一条稳定关系，而不是命令。

senses.title: A named law of physics
senses.definition: one of the named statements, such as Newton's laws of motion, that organise a branch of physics
senses.definitionCN: 组织某一物理分支的具名陈述，如牛顿运动定律
senses.example: Newton's scientific laws still hold for ordinary speeds.
senses.exampleCN: 牛顿的科学定律在寻常速度下依然成立。
senses.why: A name lets a whole pattern be cited in a sentence, which is why laws are named after their formulators.
senses.whyCN: 有了专名，一整套模式就能在一句话里被引用，因此定律常以提出者命名。

senses.title: The describing half of a pair
senses.definition: the part of knowledge that says what happens, as contrasted with a theory that says why
senses.definitionCN: 知识中说明「发生什么」的部分，与说明「为何发生」的理论相对
senses.example: A scientific law and a theory do different jobs and do not compete.
senses.exampleCN: 科学定律与理论各司其职，并不互相竞争。
senses.why: A statement of pattern and a statement of mechanism answer different questions, so the pair is not a ladder from weaker to stronger.
senses.whyCN: 对模式的陈述与对机制的陈述回答不同问题，因此这一对并不是由弱到强的阶梯。

senses.title: A quantitative empirical law
senses.definition: a law stating a measurable relation, often expressed as an equation, derived from experiment
senses.definitionCN: 陈述可测关系的定律，常写成等式，由实验得出
senses.example: Boyle's scientific law relates pressure and volume at fixed temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 玻意耳的科学定律描述定温下压强与体积的关系。
senses.why: Once a relation can be written as an equation, each new measurement can test it, and the law becomes a working tool.
senses.whyCN: 关系一旦能写成等式，每次新测量都能检验它，定律于是成为可用的工具。

senses.title: A law of conservation
senses.definition: a law stating that some quantity stays constant in a closed process, such as energy or momentum
senses.definitionCN: 陈述在封闭过程中某量保持不变的定律，如能量或动量
senses.example: The scientific law of conservation of energy survived every test.
senses.exampleCN: 能量守恒这条科学定律经受住了每一次检验。
senses.why: A conserved quantity is the strongest kind of regularity, because it says what cannot change rather than what usually does.
senses.whyCN: 守恒量是最强的一类稳定性，因为它说的是什么不能变，而不是通常怎样变。

senses.title: A law of nature, philosophically
senses.titleCN: 哲学意义上的自然规律
senses.definition: the idea that nature follows regularities that inquiry can discover, apart from any legislator
senses.definitionCN: 认为自然遵循可由探究发现的规律、且无需立法者的观念
senses.example: A scientific law of nature once implied a lawgiver, and the metaphor still troubles philosophers.
senses.exampleCN: 「自然规律」一说曾暗含立法者，这个比喻至今仍困扰哲学。
senses.why: The legal metaphor carried over: regularities were imagined as commands written into matter, and the image has never fully worn off.
senses.whyCN: 法律的比喻被继承了：稳定性被想象成写进物质的命令，这个意象从未完全褪去。

senses.title: A law in biology
senses.definition: a broad regularity in living systems, such as the patterns of inheritance, usually looser than a physical law
senses.definitionCN: 生命系统中的宽泛稳定性，如遗传模式，通常比物理定律宽松
senses.example: Mendel's scientific laws predict ratios rather than exact values.
senses.exampleCN: 孟德尔的科学定律预测比例，而非精确数值。
senses.why: Living systems carry variation, so biological laws tend to describe distributions, which is a weaker claim than a fixed equation.
senses.whyCN: 生命系统带有变异，因此生物定律多描述分布，这比固定等式是更弱的主张。

senses.title: A tendency in social science
senses.titleCN: 社会科学中的趋势陈述
senses.definition: an observed regularity in human affairs, stated as a tendency rather than an invariable rule
senses.definitionCN: 对人类事务中观察到的稳定性所作的陈述，多表述为趋势而非不变规则
senses.example: Economists speak of scientific laws of supply, though the regularities can break.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学家谈供给的科学定律，尽管这些稳定性会失效。
senses.why: Human behaviour changes when people learn the prediction, so social regularities are stated as tendencies and hedged accordingly.
senses.whyCN: 人一旦知道预测就会改变行为，因此社会稳定性被表述为趋势，并相应加上限定。

senses.title: A mathematical law
senses.definition: a named theorem-like regularity, such as the law of large numbers, proved from stated assumptions
senses.definitionCN: 有专名、近似定理的稳定性，如大数定律，由所述前提证明
senses.example: The scientific law of large numbers steadies averages as samples grow.
senses.exampleCN: 大数这条科学定律使平均值随样本增大而稳定。
senses.why: Mathematics supplies regularities that need no experiment, and the word law is borrowed for them by analogy.
senses.whyCN: 数学提供无需实验的稳定性，人们便按类比把定律一词借了过去。

intro.en: Scientific law pairs a Latin-derived adjective with an Old Norse-derived noun. Science comes from scire 'to know'; law comes from Old Norse lag, 'something laid down', and has nothing to do with Latin lex.
intro.cn: scientific law 把拉丁语来源的形容词与古诺尔斯语来源的名词配在一起。science 出自 scire「知道」；law 出自古诺尔斯语 lag「被放下的东西」，与拉丁语 lex 无关。

items.en: Scientia meant knowledge, and scientific is the adjective built on it in modern English.
items.cn: scientia 意为知识，scientific 是 modern English 在它上面构成的形容词。

items.en: Lag meant something laid down or set in place, and the plural lagu named the body of things laid down as custom.
items.cn: lag 意为被放下、被安置的东西，复数 lagu 指作为惯例立下的整套规定。

items.en: Old English borrowed lagu from Norse, and law kept the image of something laid down by authority.
items.cn: 古英语从诺尔斯语借入 lagu，law 保留了「由权威立下之物」的意象。

items.en: Latin lex and its stem leg- give legal, legislate and legitimate; those words are cousins in meaning, not sources of law.
items.cn: 拉丁语 lex 及其词干 leg- 产生 legal、legislate 与 legitimate；这些词只是意思上的近亲，并非 law 的来源。

items.en: Writers on the new physics spoke of laws of nature, borrowing the legal metaphor for regularities found in matter.
items.cn: 新物理学的作者谈「自然规律」，把法律比喻借来描述物质中的稳定性。

items.en: The full phrase settled in the nineteenth century, and the modern contrast between law and theory was fixed in textbooks of the twentieth.
items.cn: 完整说法在十九世纪定型，现代「定律与理论」的对比则在二十世纪教科书中固定下来。

note.en: The first group shares one of the two words; the second group names neighbouring concepts in method.
note.cn: 第一组共享两个词中的一个；第二组是方法上的相邻概念。

entries.definition: A rule laid down by authority, or a regularity in nature.
entries.definitionCN: 由权威立下的规则，或自然中的稳定关系。

entries.definition: Allowed by law; it belongs to the legal side, not the scientific one.
entries.definitionCN: 法律所允许的；属于法律一侧，而非科学一侧。

entries.definition: Following tested method; the adjective half of the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 遵循检验方法的；短语中的形容词一半。

entries.definition: The organized knowledge behind the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词背后的系统知识。

entries.definition: From Latin lex; it looks like a relative of law but comes down another line.
entries.definitionCN: 出自拉丁语 lex；看似与「法律」同族，其实来自另一条线。

entries.definition: Lawful or genuine, from the same Latin legal stem as legal.
entries.definitionCN: 合法或正当的，与「合法的」一词同出拉丁法律词干。

entries.definition: An explanation of why something happens, the partner and not the rival of a law.
entries.definitionCN: 解释事情为何发生的体系，是定律的搭档而非对手。

entries.definition: A general rule that guides reasoning, often broader and less quantitative.
entries.definitionCN: 引导推理的一般规则，通常更宽泛、更少定量。

entries.definition: A testable guess that has not yet earned the name of law.
entries.definitionCN: 尚不足以称为定律的可检验猜测。

entries.definition: A stated regularity or instruction, wider in everyday use than law.
entries.definitionCN: 陈述的稳定性或指示，日常用法比定律更宽。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the two real origins, the legal metaphor and the standard law-theory contrast.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用两个真实来源、法律比喻，以及标准的定律与理论对比。

normal.en: Law came from Norse for something laid down, and a regularity laid down in matter is a law of nature.
normal.cn: law 来自诺尔斯语，指被放下之物；物质中被放下的稳定性就是自然规律。

normal.en: Scientific law is not from Latin lex; legal and legitimate come from that other line.
normal.cn: scientific law 并非出自拉丁语 lex；legal 与 legitimate 才来自那条线。

normal.en: A law says what happens; a theory says why. They answer different questions.
normal.cn: 定律说发生什么，理论说为何发生；两者回答不同问题。

normal.en: Boyle's law, Newton's laws and the conservation of energy are all named regularities.
normal.cn: 玻意耳定律、牛顿定律与能量守恒，都是有专名的稳定性。

normal.en: Biological laws predict ratios, because living systems carry variation.
normal.cn: 生物定律预测比例，因为生命系统带有变异。

abstract.en: A law is a promise nature has kept every time we looked, not a promise it has signed.
abstract.cn: 定律是自然在我们每次观察时都守住的承诺，不是它签署的契约。

abstract.en: The strongest law is the one that forbids something, like a quantity that cannot be lost.
abstract.cn: 最强的定律是禁止某事的定律，比如某个量不能消失。

abstract.en: Calling a regularity a law is a metaphor borrowed from courts, and the metaphor still asks who legislates.
abstract.cn: 把稳定性称作定律是从法庭借来的比喻，而这个比喻仍在追问谁在立法。

examples.en: A scientific law can be stated in one line and tested for centuries.
examples.cn: 一条科学定律能用一行写出，并被检验数百年。

examples.en: The students confused a scientific law with a theory and had to separate them.
examples.cn: 学生们把科学定律与理论混为一谈，后来不得不把它们分开。

examples.en: No scientific law forbids the pattern; it simply has never been seen.
examples.cn: 没有哪条科学定律禁止这种模式，只是从未有人见过。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「赛恩提菲克-罗」——被自然反复遵守的那条规则：科学定律

root: scientific 来自拉丁语 scientia「知识」← scire「知道」；law 来自古诺尔斯语 lag「被放下之物」→ lagu，与拉丁语 lex 无关。「自然规律」的比喻盛行于十七世纪，完整术语在十九世纪定型。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one laid-down regularity: a general statement, a named physical law, the describing half of law and theory, a quantitative law, a conservation law, the philosophical law of nature, a biological regularity, a social tendency and a mathematical law.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟着一条被立下的稳定性：一般陈述、有专名的物理定律、定律与理论中「描述」的那一半、定量定律、守恒定律、哲学上的自然规律、生物稳定性、社会趋势与数学定律。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one short equation on a plaque, surrounded by decades of data tables that all agree with it.
core.cn: 核心意象：牌子上一条简短等式，周围贴满几十年都与它吻合的数据表。

branches.en: THE PATTERN AND THE EQUATION: a regularity stated in words, then in measurable numbers.
branches.cn: 模式与等式：先用文字陈述的稳定性，再用可测数字陈述。

branches.en: THE NAMED AND THE CONSERVED: Newton's laws cited by name, and quantities that cannot be lost.
branches.cn: 具名与守恒：被按名引用的牛顿定律，与不能损失的物理量。

branches.en: THE PARTNER OF THEORY: what happens, set beside why it happens.
branches.cn: 理论的搭档：发生什么，与为何发生并列。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: nature imagined as obeying commands written into matter.
branches.cn: 那个比喻：自然被想象成服从写进物质的命令。

branches.en: THE LOOSER LAWS: ratios in inheritance, tendencies in markets, theorems in mathematics.
branches.cn: 较宽松的定律：遗传中的比例、市场中的趋势、数学中的定理。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin-derived adjective to a Norse-derived noun, and neither half is built from the other.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁语来源的形容词与诺尔斯语来源的名词接在一起，两半都不由对方构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer belongs to scientific alone: scire, sciens and scientia. Law is Norse, and lex is a separate Latin line.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语成分只属于 scientific 这一半：scire、sciens 与 scientia。law 来自诺尔斯语，lex 则是另一条拉丁语线。

items.example: The phrase is a modern pairing of two different origins.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语把两个不同来源的词配在一起。

items.example: It supplies the adjective half.
items.exampleCN: 它提供形容词那一半。

items.example: The noun behind scientific.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词背后的名词。

items.example: The adjective means knowledge-making.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词意为「产生知识的」。

items.example: The image is a thing placed in position.
items.exampleCN: 意象是被安置到位的东西。

items.example: English borrowed the plural as law.
items.exampleCN: 英语借入复数形式作「法律」。

items.example: The legal and scientific senses share one image.
items.exampleCN: 法律义与科学义共享一个意象。

items.example: It gives legal and legitimate, not law.
items.exampleCN: 它产生「合法的」与「正当的」二词，而非「法律」。

items.example: The look-alike that belongs to the other line.
items.exampleCN: 属于另一条线的形近词。

items.example: The partner concept that explains rather than describes.
items.exampleCN: 作搭档的概念，解释而非描述。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb scire (sci-, scitum; to know)
latinEntries.example: The verb underlies scientia, knowledge.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 这个动词是 scientia（知识）的底层。

latinEntries.example: The noun gives the first half of the phrase.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 这个名词提供该短语的前半部分。

latinEntries.example: It builds scientificus, the adjective in the phrase.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它构成该短语中的形容词 scientificus。

latinEntries.example: Latin lex means statute, and its stem leg- gives legal.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 lex 意为成文法，其词干 leg- 给出 legal。

definition_zh: 观察；注意到；作科学观测；评论说；遵守；庆祝（节日或仪式）
definition_en: to watch something carefully, to notice, to make a scientific observation, to remark, or to keep a rule or mark a day
core_image: 山顶观测台上，一个人屏住呼吸把望远镜对准同一颗星，每隔一刻钟记下一次位置
scene: 山顶的观测台上，一个人每隔一刻钟记录一次那颗星的位置，直到云层压过来。Astronomers observe the same star for months to fix its distance.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项：为获取信息而长时间仔细观看；句意为天文学家连续数月观测同一颗星，以确定它的距离。图中可辨识物件：望远镜、记录表、计时器、星图。

pos.zh: 观察；注意到；观测；评论；遵守；庆祝

senses.title: To watch with full attention
senses.definition: to watch someone or something closely over time in order to learn how it behaves
senses.definitionCN: 为弄清某人或某物的行为而长时间仔细观看
senses.example: Astronomers observe the same star for months to fix its distance.
senses.exampleCN: 天文学家连续数月观测同一颗星，以确定它的距离。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to watch over and heed, so sustained attention rather than a glance is the oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 那个拉丁动词意为看守并留心，因此持续注意而非一眼扫过，是最古老的一层。

senses.title: To notice
senses.definition: to see or become aware of something, often without looking for it
senses.definitionCN: 看见或意识到某物，往往并非刻意寻找
senses.example: I observed a crack in the glass before it fell.
senses.exampleCN: 玻璃掉落之前，我就注意到上面有道裂痕。
senses.why: Attention can be caught as well as directed, so the same verb covers the moment something enters the eye.
senses.whyCN: 注意力既能被引导也能被抓住，因此同一个动词也覆盖某物进入视野的那一刻。

senses.title: To measure in a study
senses.definition: to record a phenomenon under controlled conditions as part of scientific work
senses.definitionCN: 作为科研工作的一部分，在受控条件下记录一种现象
senses.example: The team observe the cells every six hours.
senses.exampleCN: 团队每六小时观察一次这些细胞。
senses.why: Measurement begins with watching, and science made the watching formal by giving it conditions and records.
senses.whyCN: 测量始于观看，而科学通过附加条件与记录，把观看变得正式。

senses.title: To remark
senses.definition: to say something as a comment on what has been noticed
senses.definitionCN: 就注意到的事情说一句话作为评论
senses.example: The reviewer observed that the sample was too small.
senses.exampleCN: 评审人评论说样本太小。
senses.why: A remark is often the spoken form of something noticed, so the verb moved from the eye to the mouth.
senses.whyCN: 评论常常是「注意到的东西」的口头形式，这个动词于是从眼睛移到了嘴。

senses.title: To keep a rule
senses.definition: to act in accordance with a law, rule, custom or promise
senses.definitionCN: 依照法律、规则、习俗或承诺行事
senses.example: Drivers must observe the speed limit near the school.
senses.exampleCN: 司机在学校附近必须遵守限速。
senses.why: To observe a rule is to keep watch over yourself, the same inward attention the Latin verb first described.
senses.whyCN: 遵守规则就是看住自己，正是那个拉丁动词最初描述的内在注意。

senses.title: To mark a day or rite
senses.definition: to celebrate or carry out a day, festival or ceremony in the proper way
senses.definitionCN: 以适当方式庆祝某个日子、节日或举行仪式
senses.example: The village observes the harvest festival every autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村子每年秋天都过丰收节。
senses.why: A custom is kept by being performed on its day, so the sense of keeping widened to the act of celebration.
senses.whyCN: 习俗靠在其日子被践行而得以保持，因此「持守」之义扩展到庆祝行为。

senses.title: To keep someone under watch
senses.definition: to watch a person or place secretly, especially as part of an investigation
senses.definitionCN: 暗中监视某人或某地，尤作为调查的一部分
senses.example: Police observe the house from a van across the street.
senses.exampleCN: 警察在街对面的货车里监视那栋房子。
senses.why: The same careful watching turns into surveillance when the watcher does not wish to be seen.
senses.whyCN: 当观看者不愿被看见，同样的仔细观看就变成了监视。

senses.title: To watch without interfering
senses.definition: in research, to study behaviour while taking no part that would change it
senses.definitionCN: 在研究中研究行为，同时不介入以免改变它
senses.example: The psychologist observes the class from the back of the room.
senses.exampleCN: 心理学家在教室后排观察这个班。
senses.why: If the observer changes what is observed, the record is spoiled, so method demands watching with hands off.
senses.whyCN: 观察者若改变了被观察对象，记录就毁了，因此方法要求袖手旁观。

intro.en: Observe comes from Latin observare 'to watch over, heed', built on ob- 'over, before' and servare 'to keep, preserve'. The rule-keeping and celebration senses came through religious usage, and the scientific sense settled in the seventeenth century.
intro.cn: observe 来自拉丁语 observare「看守、留心」，由 ob-「在……之上、在……之前」与 servare「保持、守护」构成。守规与庆祝两义经宗教用法而来，科学观测义则在十七世纪定型。

items.en: Servare meant to keep safe, preserve or watch over, and it stands behind preserve, reserve and conserve.
items.cn: servare 意为保全、守护、看守，preserve、reserve 与 conserve 都出自它。

items.en: The similar-looking servire meant to serve, and it gave servant and service; the two Latin verbs are different words.
items.cn: 形近的 servire 意为服侍，产生了 servant 与 service；这两个拉丁动词是不同的词。

items.en: Ob- plus servare made a verb for watching over something and attending to it, with attention as the core.
items.cn: ob- 加 servare 构成「看守并留心某物」的动词，核心在注意。

items.en: Old French observer carried the word into English in the fourteenth century, first in the sense of keeping a rule.
items.cn: 古法语 observer 在十四世纪把这个词带入英语，最初意为遵守规则。

items.en: Observing the Sabbath and observing a fast fixed the senses of keeping a custom and of celebrating its day.
items.cn: 守安息日、守斋期固定了「持守习俗」与「在其日子举行」两种含义。

items.en: Seventeenth-century astronomy made observe a technical word for recorded watching, and observatory and observer followed.
items.cn: 十七世纪的天文学把 observe 变成指「有记录观看」的技术词，天文台与观察者二词随之而来。

note.en: The first group shares the keeping root or looks close; the second group names ways of watching.
note.cn: 第一组共享「守护」词根或形近；第二组是各种「看」的方式。

entries.definition: The act or result of watching and recording.
entries.definitionCN: 观看并记录的行为或结果。

entries.definition: The person who watches, including the mere onlooker.
entries.definitionCN: 进行观看的人，也包括单纯旁观者。

entries.definition: Quick to notice details; also careful in keeping rules.
entries.definitionCN: 善于察觉细节的；也指守规谨慎的。

entries.definition: The keeping of a rule or rite, not the act of looking.
entries.definitionCN: 对规则或仪式的遵行，而非观看动作。

entries.definition: A building fitted for watching the sky.
entries.definitionCN: 为观测天空而建的场所。

entries.definition: To keep safe from harm, from the same keeping verb with a different prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 使免受损害，同一守护动词加不同前缀。

entries.definition: Work done for others, from servire 'to serve', not from servare.
entries.definitionCN: 为他人所做的工作，出自表示「服侍」的拉丁动词，而非表示「守护」的拉丁动词。

entries.definition: The everyday word for looking at something over a period, with less formality.
entries.definitionCN: 日常说法，指持续一段时间看某物，正式程度较低。

entries.definition: To become aware of something, without the suggestion of sustained study.
entries.definitionCN: 意识到某物，不含持续研究的意味。

entries.definition: To keep a continuous check, often with instruments.
entries.definitionCN: 持续检查，常借助仪器。

entries.definition: To look over a whole area or group, often to record its state.
entries.definitionCN: 遍览整个区域或群体，常为记录其状态。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the keeping verb, the real family and the fixed phrases of rules, rites and research.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用「守护」动词、真实同族词，以及规则、仪式与研究里的固定搭配。

normal.en: Latin servare meant to keep safe, so observe is literally to keep watch over something.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 servare 意为保全，observe 字面就是看住某物。

normal.en: The family runs observe, observation, observer, observant and observatory.
normal.cn: 同族词有 observe、observation、observer、observant 与 observatory。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the range: observe a rule, observe a holiday, observe that.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出范围：遵守规则、庆祝节日、评论说。

normal.en: Preserve and reserve share the keeping verb, while servant and service come from the serving verb.
normal.cn: preserve 与 reserve 共享「守护」动词，而 servant 与 service 出自「服侍」动词。

normal.en: An observatory is a building named for the watching, not for the stars.
normal.cn: 天文台是因「观看」而得名，而非因星星。

abstract.en: To observe a rule is to watch yourself as closely as you watch others.
abstract.cn: 遵守规则，就是像看别人那样看住自己。

abstract.en: The observer who changes the scene has already lost the thing worth recording.
abstract.cn: 改变场景的观察者，已经失去了值得记录的东西。

abstract.en: Attention is the whole word: watch, keep, and do not blink.
abstract.cn: 整个词就是注意：看着、守着、别眨眼。

examples.en: She observed the birds from the hide without making a sound.
examples.cn: 她藏在小棚里观察鸟，没有发出一点声音。

examples.en: Every driver must observe the signs at the crossing.
examples.cn: 每位司机在路口都必须遵守标志。

examples.en: The committee observed a minute of silence for the victims.
examples.cn: 委员会为遇难者默哀一分钟。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「欧布泽夫」——守在旁边盯住不放，看到什么就记下来：观察

root: 拉丁语 servare「保全、守护」→ observare「看守、留心」（ob- 加 servare）；经古法语 observer 进入英语。守规与庆祝义经宗教用法而来，科学观测义在十七世纪定型。注意与 servire「服侍」并非同词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one pair of watching eyes: sustained attention, a sudden notice, a measured record, a spoken remark, a rule kept, a festival marked, a house watched in secret, and a class studied without interference.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一双观看的眼睛：持续注意、忽然察觉、有记录的测量、口头评论、被遵守的规则、被举行的节日、被暗中监视的房子，以及不干预地研究的课堂。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: on a hilltop a watcher holds a telescope on one star and writes its position every quarter hour.
core.cn: 核心意象：山顶的观测者用望远镜对准一颗星，每刻钟记下它的位置。

branches.en: THE EYES: watching for a long time, and catching something in passing.
branches.cn: 那双眼：长时间的看，与路过时捕捉到什么。

branches.en: THE RECORD: cells counted every six hours, a class watched from the back without interference.
branches.cn: 记录：每六小时数一次细胞，在教室后排不干预地观察一个班。

branches.en: THE MOUTH: a note spoken aloud after the eyes have done their work.
branches.cn: 嘴：眼睛做完活之后，说出口的一句评论。

branches.en: THE KEPT RULE: attention turned inward, so that the driver watches himself.
branches.cn: 被守的规则：注意转向内部，司机看住自己。

branches.en: THE MARKED DAY AND THE SECRET WATCH: a rite performed on its date, a house watched from a van.
branches.cn: 被举行的日子与暗中监视：在正日子举行的仪式，与从货车里盯住的房子。

intro.en: Observe is a Latin verb of keeping watch, and its family split off from the separate verb meaning to serve.
intro.cn: observe 是一个表示看守的拉丁动词，其词族与另一个意为服侍的动词分道而行。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is servare, ob-, observare and the noun observatio.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语成分是 servare、ob-、observare 与名词 observatio。

items.example: The verb keeps the image of a guard at a post.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词保留着岗哨看守的意象。

items.example: It also gives preserve, reserve and conserve.
items.exampleCN: 它也是「保存」「保留」与「保护」三词的来源。

items.example: It gives servant and service, and is not the root here.
items.exampleCN: 它产生「仆人」与「服务」两词，不是这里的词根。

items.example: It adds the idea of watching over something.
items.exampleCN: 它加上「看住某物」的意思。

items.example: The compound is the direct source of the English verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词是英语动词的直接来源。

items.example: The noun names both the act and its record.
items.exampleCN: 名词兼指行为与其记录。

items.example: The agent noun includes the mere onlooker.
items.exampleCN: 施事名词包括单纯旁观者。

items.example: The adjective also means careful in keeping rules.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词也指守规谨慎的。

items.meaning: the keeping of a rule or rite
items.example: It names practice, not perception.
items.exampleCN: 它命名实践，而非感知。

items.example: The suffix names a place of work.
items.exampleCN: 词尾命名工作场所。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb servare (serv-, servatum; to keep)
latinEntries.example: Latin servare means to keep or preserve.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 servare 意为保持、守护。

latinEntries.example: Latin ob- appears in obicere, to throw against.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 ob- 见于 obicere（扔向对面）。

latinEntries.example: Latin observare means to watch over, to heed.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 observare 意为看守、留意。

latinEntries.example: Latin observatio means a watching or a noting.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 observatio 意为观看、记录。

definition_zh: 观察者；观测人员；旁观者；列席观察员
definition_en: a person who watches or records something, especially for research, or an onlooker who takes no part in an event
core_image: 教室最后一排坐着一个人，只在本子上记录，从不举手，也不打断任何事
scene: 培训教室里，一位列席者坐在最后一排，只在本子上记录，从不打断讲课。The observer sat at the back and wrote down how often the teacher paused.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项：只观看与记录、不参与其中的人；句意为这位观察者坐在后排，记下老师停顿的次数。图中可辨识物件：后排座位、记录本、秒表、讲台。

pos.zh: 观察者；观测员；旁观者；列席观察员（可数）

senses.title: A watcher who takes no part
senses.definition: a person who watches an event without joining in or changing it
senses.definitionCN: 观看事件、但不参与也不改变它的人
senses.example: The observer sat at the back and wrote down how often the teacher paused.
senses.exampleCN: 这位观察者坐在后排，记下老师停顿的次数。
senses.why: The word is built from the verb of watching plus the agent ending, so the person is defined by attention rather than action.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由表示观看的动词加施事词尾构成，因此这个人是被「注意」而非「行动」定义的。

senses.title: The recorder in a study
senses.definition: a researcher who watches and records behaviour or readings as part of a study
senses.definitionCN: 作为研究的一部分，观看并记录行为或读数的人
senses.example: A second observer checked the timings independently.
senses.exampleCN: 第二位观察者独立核对了计时。
senses.why: Two people watching the same session can compare notes, which is how a study shows that its records are reliable.
senses.whyCN: 两个人看同一场活动可以互相比对记录，研究正是以此证明记录可靠。

senses.title: The watcher in quantum theory
senses.definition: in quantum mechanics, the agent whose measurement fixes one of the possible outcomes
senses.definitionCN: 在量子力学中，其测量使某个可能结果确定下来的角色
senses.example: In quantum theory the observer cannot be left out of the account.
senses.exampleCN: 在量子理论里，观察者无法被排除在描述之外。
senses.why: If a measurement changes the state it measures, the watcher becomes part of the system, and the word carries that problem.
senses.whyCN: 如果测量改变了被测量的状态，观看者就成了系统的一部分，这个词正承担着这一难题。

senses.title: A seat without a vote
senses.definition: a representative allowed to attend and speak at a body but not to vote
senses.definitionCN: 获准出席并发言、但没有表决权的代表
senses.example: The body granted the agency observer status.
senses.exampleCN: 该机构给了这个组织观察员地位。
senses.why: An organisation that watches but does not decide needs a name between member and guest, and this is it.
senses.whyCN: 只看不决定的组织需要一个介于成员与客人之间的身份，这个词正好补上。

senses.title: The monitor at an election
senses.definition: a person sent to watch that a vote is conducted fairly and to report on it
senses.definitionCN: 被派去监督投票是否公正并提交报告的人
senses.example: An observer from each party stood at every ballot box.
senses.exampleCN: 每个投票箱旁都站着一名各党派的观察员。
senses.why: A watcher with a mandate to report turns looking into a safeguard, so the word gains a public function.
senses.whyCN: 负有报告职责的观看者把「看」变成一种保障，这个词于是有了公共职能。

senses.title: The researcher who joins in
senses.definition: in anthropology, a researcher who lives among the people studied while still recording
senses.definitionCN: 在人类学中与被研究者共同生活、同时坚持记录的研究者
senses.example: The observer joined the factory shift to understand the work.
senses.exampleCN: 这位观察者加入工厂班次，以理解那份工作。
senses.why: Some behaviour only appears to insiders, so the method accepts participation while trying to keep the record honest.
senses.whyCN: 有些行为只对内部人显现，因此这种方法允许参与，同时设法保持记录诚实。

senses.title: The impartial witness
senses.definition: a person present who can report what happened without a stake in the outcome
senses.definitionCN: 在场且与结果无利害关系、能陈述发生了什么的人
senses.example: To a neutral observer the mistake was obvious.
senses.exampleCN: 在中立的观察者看来，那个错误一目了然。
senses.why: Someone with no stake can be trusted to say what a participant cannot, and the word supplies that position.
senses.whyCN: 没有利害关系的人能说出参与者说不出口的话，这个词提供了这一位置。

senses.title: The officer at a ceasefire line
senses.definition: a soldier or official deployed to watch a truce or a disputed border and report violations
senses.definitionCN: 被派去监督停火或争议边界、并报告违规行为的军人或官员
senses.example: Military observers reported two breaches before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 军事观察员报告黎明前有两起违约。
senses.why: Where two sides will not share a patrol, a third party watches, and the watching is the whole job.
senses.whyCN: 双方不愿共同巡逻时，就由第三方来看，而「看」本身就是全部工作。

senses.title: A perceptive commentator
senses.definition: a person known for noticing and describing what others miss, often in public writing
senses.definitionCN: 以察觉并描述他人忽略之处著称的人，常见于公共写作
senses.example: She is a sharp observer of how committees really decide.
senses.exampleCN: 她是一位敏锐的观察者，看得出委员会真正如何决定。
senses.why: Long practice in watching produces someone whose remarks are trusted, and the plain word for watcher becomes praise.
senses.whyCN: 长期观看的练习造就一个其评论可信的人，于是「观看者」这个朴素词成了赞誉。

intro.en: Observer is observe plus the agent ending -er, with Latin observator behind it. The science sense is early modern, and the quantum sense is a twentieth-century extension of it.
intro.cn: observer 是 observe 加施事词尾 -er 构成，背后有拉丁语 observator。科学观测义属近代早期，量子力学义则是二十世纪对它的延伸。

items.en: Observare meant to watch over and heed, from ob- 'over' and servare 'to keep'.
items.cn: observare 意为看守并留心，由 ob-「在……之上」与 servare「保持」构成。

items.en: Late Latin observator named the person who watched or kept a rule, a model for the English agent noun.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 observator 指观看或守规的人，为英语的施事名词提供了样板。

items.en: The English agent ending came from Old English -ere, itself borrowed from Latin -arius, so the two halves meet again.
items.cn: 英语施事词尾来自古英语 -ere，而 -ere 又借自拉丁语 -arius，两半在英语里重新汇合。

items.en: Observer entered English in the sixteenth century, at first for a person who keeps a rule or a custom.
items.cn: observer 在十六世纪进入英语，最初指遵守规则或习俗的人。

items.en: Seventeenth-century astronomy and natural history gave the word its recording sense, with instruments and notebooks.
items.cn: 十七世纪的天文学与博物学给了它「用仪器与记录本观看」的含义。

items.en: The twentieth century added the observer in quantum measurement and the observer sent to watch elections and ceasefires.
items.cn: 二十世纪又加上量子测量中的观察者，以及被派去监督选举与停火的观察员。

note.en: The first group shares the watching root; the second group names related onlooker roles.
note.cn: 第一组共享「观看」词根；第二组是相关的旁观角色。

entries.definition: The verb of watching, keeping and remarking.
entries.definitionCN: 表示观看、遵守与评论的动词。

entries.definition: The act or the recorded result of watching.
entries.definitionCN: 观看的行为，或被记录下来的结果。

entries.definition: Quick to notice; also careful about rules.
entries.definitionCN: 察觉敏锐的；也指守规谨慎的。

entries.definition: A building equipped for watching the sky.
entries.definitionCN: 装备起来观测天空的建筑。

entries.definition: The keeping of a rite or rule, not the person who watches.
entries.definitionCN: 对仪式或规则的遵行，不是观看的人。

entries.definition: Someone who watches an event without taking part; no scientific weight.
entries.definitionCN: 观看事件而不参与的人；没有科研分量。

entries.definition: A person who saw an event and can testify to it.
entries.definitionCN: 看见事件并能作证的人。

entries.definition: A person or device that keeps a continuous check.
entries.definitionCN: 持续进行检查的人或装置。

entries.definition: A member of an audience, there to be entertained.
entries.definitionCN: 观众之一，为观赏而来。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Latin watcher, the real family and the fixed titles of research and missions.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用拉丁语中的观看者、真实同族词，以及科研与派驻任务里的固定头衔。

normal.en: Observer is the verb of watching plus the person ending, and Latin already had a watcher noun.
normal.cn: observer 是观看动词加表示人的词尾，拉丁语里本就有「观看者」这一名词。

normal.en: The family runs observe, observation, observer, observant and observatory.
normal.cn: 同族词有 observe、observation、observer、observant 与 observatory。

normal.en: Research has a second observer check the timings, so the record can be trusted.
normal.cn: 研究中让第二位观察者核对计时，记录才可信。

normal.en: Elections and ceasefires both send observers, because a report needs a witness.
normal.cn: 选举与停火都派观察员，因为报告需要见证者。

normal.en: The observer effect names the trouble that watching can change what is watched.
normal.cn: 观察者效应命名「观看可能改变被观看之物」这一麻烦。

abstract.en: An observer is paid to be unnoticed, and noticed only in the report.
abstract.cn: 观察者的本分是不被注意，只在报告里被注意。

abstract.en: The best observer knows which detail would change the conclusion.
abstract.cn: 最好的观察者知道哪个细节会改变结论。

abstract.en: Watching without a stake is the quietest kind of power.
abstract.cn: 无利害关系的观看，是最安静的一种权力。

examples.en: Each observer recorded the same session on a separate sheet.
examples.cn: 每位观察者用各自的表格记录同一场活动。

examples.en: The observer noted that the queue moved faster after noon.
examples.cn: 观察者注意到中午之后队伍移动更快。

examples.en: An observer may speak at the meeting but may not vote.
examples.cn: 观察员可以在会上发言，但没有表决权。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「欧布泽弗」——守在旁边只看不插手的那个人：观察者

root: observe（拉丁语 observare「看守、留心」）+ 施事词尾 -er（古英语 -ere，借自拉丁语 -arius）；拉丁语本有 observator。科学义见于十七世纪，量子与政治观察员义为二十世纪延伸。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one silent watcher: the non-participant, the study recorder, the quantum measurer, the seat without a vote, the election monitor, the participant researcher, the impartial witness, the ceasefire officer and the perceptive commentator.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟着一个沉默的观看者：不参与者、研究记录者、量子测量者、无表决权席位、选举监督者、参与式研究者、公正见证者、停火军官与眼光锐利的评论者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure in the last row writes in a notebook and never raises a hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：最后一排的人在本子上记录，从不举手。

branches.en: THE ONLOOKER: present without a part, and trusted because there is no stake.
branches.cn: 旁观者：在场而不参与，因无利害而被信任。

branches.en: THE RESEARCH WATCHER: one of two recorders, or a researcher who lives among the studied.
branches.cn: 研究中的观看者：两名记录者之一，或与被研究者共同生活的研究者。

branches.en: THE MEASURER: the watcher whose act of watching enters the system being described.
branches.cn: 测量者：其观看动作进入了被描述系统的观看者。

branches.en: THE MANDATED WATCHER: a seat without a vote, a monitor at a ballot box, an officer on a truce line.
branches.cn: 受命观看者：无表决权的席位、投票箱旁的监督者、停火线上的军官。

branches.en: THE REMARKER: long watching turned into trusted comment.
branches.cn: 评论者：长期观看变成可信的评论。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is observare, servare and observator, with -or and -arius as agent endings.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语成分是 observare、servare 与 observator，施事词尾有 -or 与 -arius。

items.example: The person noun is built on the verb, not on a Latin noun.

items.meaning: a watcher; a keeper of rules

items.example: It builds observator, creator and narrator.

items.example: English prefers this ending for everyday agents.

items.example: The noun names the activity, not the person.

items.example: The adjective describes the habit the person has.

items.example: The place noun extends the family to buildings.

definition_zh: 测量；量出；尺寸；措施；分寸；程度；节拍；格律
definition_en: to find the size or amount of something; a step taken to deal with a problem; a standard or a degree of something
core_image: 一把卷尺贴住桌沿，读出的数字被写进料单，旁边压着一张应对步骤的便签
scene: 木工把卷尺贴住桌沿，读出长度，再把数字写在料单上。Carpenters measure every board twice before the saw is switched on.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项：测定某物的尺寸或数量；句意为木工在开锯之前把每块板量两遍。图中可辨识物件：卷尺、桌沿、料单、铅笔。

pos.zh: 尺寸；量度；措施；分寸；（音乐的）小节；格律

senses.title: To find a size or amount
senses.definition: to find the size, length, weight or amount of something by using a tool or a standard
senses.definitionCN: 用工具或标准求出某物的尺寸、长度、重量或数量
senses.example: Carpenters measure every board twice before the saw is switched on.
senses.exampleCN: 木工在开锯之前把每块板量两遍。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to measure, and the physical act of comparing against a standard is the oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 那个拉丁动词本意就是测量，拿某物与标准相比较的实体动作是最古老的一层。

senses.title: The number obtained
senses.definition: the size or amount that a measurement produces, often written as a figure with a unit
senses.definitionCN: 测量得出的尺寸或数量，常写成带单位的数字
senses.example: The measure came out at two metres, not one.
senses.exampleCN: 量出来的结果是一点九米，不是一米。
senses.why: A measurement is both the act and its outcome, so the noun carries the number as well as the procedure.
senses.whyCN: 测量既是动作也是结果，因此这个名词既携带数字，也携带过程。

senses.title: A step taken to fix something
senses.titleCN: 为解决问题所采取的步骤
senses.definition: an action or policy adopted to deal with a problem or to reach an aim
senses.definitionCN: 为处理问题或达到目的而采取的行动或政策
senses.example: The city took measures to cut traffic at the school gate.
senses.exampleCN: 市里采取措施减少校门口的交通。
senses.why: A step is a measured amount of action: enough to change the situation, not more, and the metaphor runs from dose to policy.
senses.whyCN: 一个步骤就是定量的行动：足以改变局面，又不过量，这个比喻从剂量一直走到政策。

senses.title: A proposed law
senses.definition: in a legislature, a proposed law put forward for debate and vote
senses.definitionCN: 在立法机构中提交辩论与表决的法律草案
senses.example: The measure passed by three votes.
senses.exampleCN: 这项法案以三票之差通过。
senses.why: A bill is a measured response written into legal form, and American usage kept the word for the draft itself.
senses.whyCN: 法案是把有分寸的应对写成法律形式，美式用法保留了这个词来指草案本身。

senses.title: A standard for comparison
senses.definition: a standard, unit or benchmark by which other things are judged
senses.definitionCN: 用来判断其他事物的标准、单位或基准
senses.example: Test scores are a crude measure of a school.
senses.exampleCN: 考试分数是对学校的一种粗略衡量。
senses.why: To measure anything one needs a fixed unit, and the noun then names any yardstick, including an abstract one.
senses.whyCN: 要测量任何东西都需要固定单位，名词随后指任何标尺，包括抽象的标尺。

senses.title: A degree or extent
senses.definition: the extent to which something is true or present, as in in large measure
senses.definitionCN: 某事物为真或存在的程度，如「在很大程度上」
senses.example: The success was in large measure due to the technicians.
senses.exampleCN: 这次成功在很大程度上要归功于技术人员。
senses.why: An amount can be spoken of without a ruler, so the word extends from physical quantity to degree of influence.
senses.whyCN: 数量可以不用尺子来说，于是这个词从物理量扩展到影响的程度。

senses.title: A limit or moderation
senses.definition: a proper limit in behaviour or feeling, or the absence of one in beyond measure
senses.definitionCN: 行为或情感上应有的限度，或在「无法估量」中表示没有限度
senses.example: His anger went beyond measure.
senses.exampleCN: 他的愤怒到了无法估量的地步。
senses.why: The idea of a fixed amount turns moral: to keep measure is to keep within bounds, and to exceed it is to lose proportion.
senses.whyCN: 固定数量的观念转向道德：守分寸就是守在界限内，越过就是失去比例。

senses.title: A bar in music
senses.definition: a group of beats between two bar lines, the unit of musical time
senses.definitionCN: 两条小节线之间的一组拍子，是音乐时间的基本单位
senses.example: The phrase fits one measure of four beats.
senses.exampleCN: 这个乐句正好占一小节四拍。
senses.why: Music divides time into equal measured spans, so the word for measuring became the name of the span.
senses.whyCN: 音乐把时间分成等长的段，于是表示测量的词成了那一段的名字。

senses.title: The metre of a line
senses.definition: the patterned rhythm of a line of verse, counted in feet
senses.definitionCN: 诗句中有规律的节奏，以音步计数
senses.example: The poem keeps a steady measure through twelve lines.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗十二行都保持稳定的格律。
senses.why: Verse counts syllables the way a ruler counts inches, and the noun for the count became the name of the pattern.
senses.whyCN: 诗句像尺子量英寸那样数音节，表示计数的名词就成了这种模式的名字。

intro.en: Measure comes from Old French mesure, from Latin mensura 'a measuring', built on metiri 'to measure'. The root is generally connected with a very old word for measure that also gave Greek metron and English metre.
intro.cn: measure 来自古法语 mesure，源头是拉丁语 mensura「测量」，由 metiri「测量」构成。这个词根一般认为与一个极古老的「度量」词相关，希腊语 metron 与英语 metre 也出自它。

items.en: Metiri meant to measure or apportion, and it is the verb behind the whole family.
items.cn: metiri 意为测量、按量分配，是整个词族背后的动词。

items.en: Mensura named the act and the result of measuring, and it passed through French as the English noun.
items.cn: mensura 指测量的动作与结果，经法语成为英语名词。

items.en: The old root is generally reconstructed as a word for measure, the same one behind metre and metric; the reconstruction is accepted but the exact shape is source uncertain.
items.cn: 这个古老词根一般被重构为表示「度量」的词，metre 与 metric 也出自它；这一重构被接受，但确切形态来源不确定。

items.en: Old French mesure carried both the physical and the moral senses, and English took the pair together in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 mesure 同时带有物理与道德两层意思，英语在十三世纪把两者一起接收。

items.en: American usage of the eighteenth century applied measure to a proposed law, a use that British English largely dropped.
items.cn: 十八世纪的美式用法把这个词用到法律草案上，英式英语后来大体放弃了这一用法。

items.en: Latin mensura had already named the counted span in rhythm, and English kept measure for a bar and for metrical pattern.
items.cn: 拉丁语 mensura 早已用来指节奏中被数出的段落，英语保留 measure 指小节与格律。

note.en: The first group shares the measuring root; the second group names related actions or quantities.
note.cn: 第一组共享「测量」词根；第二组是相关动作或数量。

entries.definition: The act or the figure produced by measuring.
entries.definitionCN: 测量的动作，或测量得出的数字。

entries.definition: Large or stable enough to be measured.
entries.definitionCN: 大到或稳定到可以被测量的。

entries.definition: Deliberate and restrained, as if each step were weighed.
entries.definitionCN: 审慎而有节制的，仿佛每一步都称过。

entries.definition: The process, or a compound for a tool such as a measuring tape.
entries.definitionCN: 测量过程，或构成卷尺一类工具名。

entries.definition: The mathematics of lengths, areas and volumes; a learned doublet.
entries.definitionCN: 研究长度、面积与体积的数学；学术性的同源词。

entries.definition: To estimate or measure, often with an instrument; also the instrument.
entries.definitionCN: 估计或测量，常借助仪器；也指该仪器。

entries.definition: To express something as a number.
entries.definitionCN: 把某事物表示为数字。

entries.definition: To judge the value or level of something, with less emphasis on units.
entries.definitionCN: 判断某物的价值或水平，对单位的强调较少。

entries.definition: An action taken toward a goal, the everyday word behind the policy sense.
entries.definitionCN: 为达到目标而采取的行动，是政策义背后的日常说法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Latin measuring verb, the real family and the fixed phrases of policy and tools.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用拉丁语测量动词、真实同族词，以及政策与工具里的固定搭配。

normal.en: Latin metiri meant to measure, and mensura gave English the noun through French.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 metiri 意为测量，mensura 经法语给了英语这个名词。

normal.en: The family runs measure, measurement, measurable, measured and measuring.
normal.cn: 同族词有 measure、measurement、measurable、measured 与 measuring。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the range: take measures, safety measures, in large measure, beyond measure.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出范围：采取措施、安全措施、在很大程度上、无法估量地。

normal.en: A tape measure is the tool, and a measure of success is the standard: one word, two kinds of ruler.
normal.cn: 卷尺是工具，衡量成功的标准是标尺：同一个词，两种尺。

normal.en: Music counts beats into a measure, and verse counts feet into a measure.
normal.cn: 音乐把拍子数成小节，诗句把音步数成格律。

abstract.en: To keep measure is to know how much is enough, which is a moral skill before it is a mathematical one.
abstract.cn: 守分寸就是知道多少算够，这先是道德的技能，然后才是数学的。

abstract.en: What can be measured is not always what matters, and what matters is not always measurable.
abstract.cn: 可测量的不总是重要的，重要的也不总是可测量的。

abstract.en: A measure is a decision about what counts, made before any number appears.
abstract.cn: 尺度是在数字出现之前，关于「什么算数」的决定。

examples.en: The nurse measured the wound and wrote the figure in the chart.
examples.cn: 护士量了伤口的大小，把数字写进病历。

examples.en: The council adopted three measures to reduce waste.
examples.cn: 议会通过三项措施减少浪费。

examples.en: Her patience was tested beyond measure that afternoon.
examples.cn: 那天下午，她的耐心受到了无法估量的考验。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「米热」——用尺子一点点比过去，看看到底有多长：测量

root: 拉丁语 metiri「测量」→ mensura「测量、量度」→ 古法语 mesure → 英语 measure。词根一般认为与古希腊语 metron 同源，确切形态属重构，来源不确定；法案、小节与格律义均为后起扩展。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one ruler: the act of measuring, the number it gives, a policy step, a bill, a standard, a degree of influence, a moral limit, a musical bar and a line's metre.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟着同一把尺：测量的动作、量出的数字、政策步骤、法案、比较标准、影响程度、道德限度、音乐小节与诗句格律。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tape is laid along the desk, and the number goes straight onto the cutting list.
core.cn: 核心意象：卷尺贴住桌沿，数字直接写进下料单。

branches.en: THE ACT AND THE FIGURE: laying a tape down, and the number that comes back.
branches.cn: 动作与数字：把尺子贴上去，以及报回来的那个数。

branches.en: THE POLICY DOSE: a step sized to the problem, and the same step written as a bill.
branches.cn: 政策剂量：按问题大小配出的步骤，以及写成法案的同一步骤。

branches.en: THE YARDSTICK: test scores used as a crude ruler for a school.
branches.cn: 标尺：把考试分数当作衡量学校的粗尺。

branches.en: THE DEGREE AND THE LIMIT: influence measured in large part, anger that passes all bounds.
branches.cn: 程度与限度：占很大部分的影响，与越过一切界限的愤怒。

branches.en: THE COUNTED SPAN: four beats between two bar lines, feet counted through a line of verse.
branches.cn: 被数出的段落：两条小节线之间的四拍，与一行诗里数出的音步。

intro.en: Measure is a Latin noun and verb of measuring, and the family keeps both the physical tool and the abstract standard.
intro.cn: measure 是拉丁语中表示测量的名词与动词，其词族同时保留实体工具与抽象标准两面。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is metiri, mensura and the adjective mensurabilis, with French mesure as the carrier into English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语成分是 metiri、mensura 与形容词 mensurabilis，古法语 mesure 则是进入英语的载体。

items.example: The noun carries both the act and the standard.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词同时携带动作与标准。

items.example: The verb is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整个词族的根。

items.example: It named both the act and its result.
items.exampleCN: 它兼指动作与结果。

items.example: It builds nouns of outcome, as in mensura.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示结果的词，如 mensura。

items.example: French added the moral sense of keeping within bounds.
items.exampleCN: 法语加上了守界限的道德含义。

items.meaning: the act or result of measuring
items.example: The English suffix names the process.
items.exampleCN: 英语词尾命名过程。

items.example: The suffix marks possibility.
items.exampleCN: 词尾表示可能。

items.example: The participle turned the noun into a manner.
items.exampleCN: 分词把名词变成了举止。

items.example: The negative suffix marks what cannot be counted.
items.exampleCN: 否定词尾标出无法计数之物。

items.example: The learned doublet stays close to Latin.
items.exampleCN: 这个学术同源词紧贴拉丁语。

latinEntries.structure: Latin deponent verb metiri (met-, mensus; to measure)
latinEntries.example: Latin metiri means to measure or allot.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 metiri 意为测量、分配。

latinEntries.example: Latin mensura means a measuring, and gives English measure.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 mensura 意为测量，并给出英语 measure。

latinEntries.structure: Latin noun suffix -ura (result of an action)
latinEntries.example: Latin -ura builds nouns such as cultura, cultivation.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 -ura 构成 cultura（耕作）这类名词。

latinEntries.example: Latin mensurabilis means measurable.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 mensurabilis 意为可测量的。

definition_zh: 自变量；实验中由研究者主动改变、用来检验其影响的变量
definition_en: the variable that a researcher deliberately changes in an experiment in order to test its effect on an outcome
core_image: 实验台上并排三台培养箱，温度分别设在三个水平，其余条件全部锁死
scene: 实验台上并排摆着三台培养箱，温度分别设成三档，其余条件完全一致。The independent variable in this design is temperature, the one factor the team chooses to change.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项：由研究者主动改变、用来检验其影响的变量；句意为这个设计里的自变量是温度，是团队选择改变的那一个因素。图中可辨识物件：三台培养箱、温度旋钮、封住的湿度阀、标签卡。

collocations.phrase: the independent variable in the design
an independent variable with three levels

collocations.zh: 自变量与因变量（常成对出现）

senses.title: The factor the researcher changes
senses.titleCN: 研究者主动改变的因素
senses.definition: the factor that an experimenter sets at different levels so that its effect on the outcome can be seen
senses.definitionCN: 实验者把它设成不同水平、以便看出它对结果有何影响的因素
senses.example: The independent variable in this design is temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 这个设计里的自变量是温度。
senses.why: If only one factor is moved while the rest are held, any change in the outcome can be credited to that factor, and that factor is independent of the outcome.
senses.whyCN: 若只让一个因素变动、其余固定，结果的变化就能归给它，而它不依赖结果，故称独立。

senses.title: The x of a function
senses.definition: in mathematics, the input of a function, whose value is chosen freely within its domain
senses.definitionCN: 在数学中，函数的输入，其值在定义域内可自由选取
senses.example: In the equation, the independent variable runs along the horizontal axis.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个方程里，自变量沿横轴展开。
senses.why: A function assigns an output to each input, and the input is independent because nothing in the rule fixes it in advance.
senses.whyCN: 函数为每个输入指定输出，输入之所以独立，是因为规则并不预先固定它。

senses.title: The predictor in a model
senses.titleCN: 统计模型中的预测变量
senses.definition: in regression, a variable entered to explain or predict the values of another variable
senses.definitionCN: 在回归分析中，用来解释或预测另一个变量取值的变量
senses.example: The model used age as its only independent variable.
senses.exampleCN: 该模型只把年龄作为自变量。
senses.why: Statistics borrows the experimental word for any variable placed on the explaining side of an equation.
senses.whyCN: 统计学借用实验术语，把方程中处于「解释」一侧的变量都叫作自变量。

senses.title: The input of a simulation
senses.definition: a quantity supplied to a model or simulation whose values are varied to explore outcomes
senses.definitionCN: 提供给模型或模拟、通过改变取值来探索结果的量
senses.example: They varied the independent variable across fifty runs.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在五十次运行中改变这个自变量。
senses.why: A simulation has knobs and dials, and the knob the operator turns is the independent variable of the run.
senses.whyCN: 模拟里有旋钮与表盘，操作者转动的那个旋钮就是这一次运行的自变量。

senses.title: The explanatory factor in social research
senses.titleCN: 社会研究中的解释因素
senses.definition: in social science, a factor such as income or schooling whose association with an outcome is examined
senses.definitionCN: 在社会科学中，收入或受教育程度一类、被考察与某结果有何关联的因素
senses.example: Researchers treated neighbourhood income as the independent variable.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者把社区收入当作自变量。
senses.why: When experiments are impossible, the same word marks the factor that is expected to do the explaining.
senses.whyCN: 当实验无法进行时，同一个词标出被期待承担解释作用的因素。

senses.title: The assigned treatment condition
senses.definition: in a controlled trial, the condition to which participants are assigned, such as drug or placebo
senses.definitionCN: 在对照试验中，参与者被分配到的条件，如药物或安慰剂
senses.example: The independent variable had two levels: drug and placebo.
senses.exampleCN: 自变量有两个水平：药物与安慰剂。
senses.why: Random assignment makes the treatment independent of the people receiving it, which is why the word fits a trial.
senses.whyCN: 随机分配使处理与接受者无关，这正是这个词适用于试验的原因。

senses.title: The factor with set levels
senses.definition: in analysis of variance, a factor whose categories or levels are chosen in advance by the design
senses.definitionCN: 在方差分析中，其类别或水平由设计预先选定的因素
senses.example: The experiment crossed two independent variables, each with three levels.
senses.exampleCN: 实验交叉了两个自变量，每个各有三个水平。
senses.why: A design that crosses factors needs a name for each factor it moves, and this is that name.
senses.whyCN: 交叉因素的实验设计需要一个名字来指每一个被移动的因素，就是这个词。

senses.title: The outside force in economics
senses.definition: in economics, a variable treated as determined outside the model, such as an external price
senses.definitionCN: 在经济学中，被视为由模型之外决定、如外部价格的变量
senses.example: The oil price entered the model as an independent variable.
senses.exampleCN: 油价作为自变量进入模型。
senses.why: An outside price is not explained by the model, so it sits on the independent side of the equation.
senses.whyCN: 外部价格不由模型解释，所以它站在方程的自变量一侧。

senses.title: The column on the horizontal axis
senses.definition: the quantity whose values are read along the horizontal axis when a relation is graphed
senses.definitionCN: 作关系图时，其取值沿横轴读取的量
senses.example: Plotting it as the independent variable makes the trend easy to read.
senses.exampleCN: 把它作为自变量作图，趋势就一目了然。
senses.why: By convention the cause goes left to right and the effect up and down, so the horizontal axis carries the independent variable.
senses.whyCN: 按惯例，原因从左到右，结果从下到上，因此横轴承载自变量。

intro.en: The phrase joins independent, from Latin in- 'not' plus dependere 'to hang from', and variable, from variare 'to change'. The experimental sense belongs to nineteenth- and twentieth-century design, not to Latin.
intro.cn: 这个短语把 independent（拉丁语 in-「不」加 dependere「悬挂于」）与 variable（variare「变化」）组合起来。实验义属于十九、二十世纪的设计方法，并非拉丁语本有。

items.en: The negative prefix in- marks what does not depend, and it is the same element in invisible and inaccurate.
items.cn: 否定前缀 in- 标出「不依赖」，与 invisible、inaccurate 中的同一成分。

items.en: Dependere meant to hang from or be attached to, built from de- 'down' and pendere 'to hang'.
items.cn: dependere 意为悬挂于、依附于，由 de-「向下」与 pendere「悬挂」构成。

items.en: Independent entered English in the seventeenth century, first describing a person or a state free of control.
items.cn: independent 在十七世纪进入英语，最初描述不受控制的人或国家。

items.en: Variare meant to change or make different, from varius 'varied, spotted', the source of variable.
items.cn: variare 意为改变、使不同，出自 varius「杂色的、有斑的」，是 variable 的来源。

items.en: In seventeenth-century algebra a variable was a quantity whose value could change, and the word moved from that use into design.
items.cn: 十七世纪代数中的变量是取值可变的量，这个词从那一用法走进实验设计。

items.en: Experimental design in the later nineteenth and early twentieth centuries fixed the pair independent and dependent variable, and Fisher's methods made it standard.
items.cn: 十九世纪后期至二十世纪初的实验设计固定了「自变量与因变量」这一对说法，费希尔的方法使其成为标准。

note.en: The first group shares one of the two words; the second group names the other factors in the same design.
note.cn: 第一组共享短语中的一个词；第二组是同一设计中的其他因素。

entries.definition: Free of control by something else; the adjective inside the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 不受他物控制的；短语中的形容词。

entries.definition: The state of not being controlled or supported by another.
entries.definitionCN: 不受他人控制或供养的状态。

entries.definition: A quantity that can take different values.
entries.definitionCN: 可取不同值的量。

entries.definition: To change or make different; the verb behind the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 改变或使不同；名词背后的动词。

entries.definition: A different form of the same thing, from the same changing root.
entries.definitionCN: 同一事物的不同形态，同出「变化」词根。

entries.definition: The outcome measured in the experiment; what is expected to change when the independent variable moves.
entries.definitionCN: 实验中测量的结果；预期会随自变量变动而改变的量。

entries.definition: A factor held constant so that it cannot explain the result.
entries.definitionCN: 被保持恒定、因而无法解释结果的因子。

entries.definition: Any influence being studied in a design, whether moved or held.
entries.definitionCN: 设计中正在被研究的任何影响，无论被移动还是被固定。

entries.definition: The statistical word for a variable placed on the explaining side.
entries.definitionCN: 统计用语，指放在解释一侧的变量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the 'not hanging' root, the design image of one knob turning, and the fixed pairing with dependent.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用「不悬挂」的词根、只转一个旋钮的设计意象，以及它与因变量的固定配对。

normal.en: Independent is literally not hanging from anything: the factor's values are set by the experimenter, not by the outcome.
normal.cn: independent 字面是「不悬挂于任何东西」：这个因素的取值由实验者设定，而不由结果决定。

normal.en: The family runs independent, independence, variable, vary and variant.
normal.cn: 同族词有 independent、independence、variable、vary 与 variant。

normal.en: In a design one knob is turned and the rest are locked; that knob is the independent variable.
normal.cn: 设计里只转一个旋钮，其余锁死；那个旋钮就是自变量。

normal.en: On a graph the independent variable runs along the horizontal axis and the outcome goes up the vertical one.
normal.cn: 图上自变量沿横轴展开，结果沿纵轴上升。

normal.en: A trial assigns drug or placebo: the assigned condition is the independent variable, and randomisation keeps it independent of the people.
normal.cn: 试验分配药物或安慰剂：被分配的条件就是自变量，而随机化使它独立于人。

abstract.en: The independent variable is the question you choose to ask; the dependent variable is the answer you are allowed to hear.
abstract.cn: 自变量是你选择提出的问题，因变量是你被允许听到的答案。

abstract.en: Independence here is not freedom but a decision: someone must set the levels.
abstract.cn: 这里的独立不是自由，而是一个决定：总得有人来设定水平。

abstract.en: Move one thing at a time, and the world tells you which thing moved it.
abstract.cn: 一次只动一样东西，世界才会告诉你是哪一样动了它。

examples.en: The team changed only the independent variable between the two runs.
examples.cn: 两次运行之间，团队只改变了自变量。

examples.en: In the graph, time is the independent variable and mass loss is the result.
examples.cn: 图中时间是自变量，质量损失是结果。

examples.en: A trial with two independent variables needs more participants than a simple comparison.
examples.cn: 有两个自变量的试验比简单比较需要更多参与者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「因迪彭登特-维瑞额波」——不靠结果定值、由实验者自己拧的那个旋钮：自变量

root: independent 来自拉丁语 in-「不」+ dependere「悬挂于」；variable 来自 variare「变化」← varius「杂色的」。实验设计术语定型于十九、二十世纪，与费希尔的统计方法密切相关。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one knob the experimenter turns: the manipulated factor, the x of a function, the regression predictor, a simulation input, a social explanatory factor, the assigned treatment, a factor with set levels, an outside economic price, and the horizontal axis.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟着实验者转动的同一个旋钮：被操纵的因素、函数中的 x、回归预测变量、模拟输入、社会解释因素、被分配的处理条件、设有水平的因素、经济中的外部价格，以及横轴。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: three incubators side by side, each set to a different temperature, every other dial sealed.
core.cn: 核心意象：三台培养箱并排，各自设在不同温度，其余旋钮全部封住。

branches.en: THE MANIPULATED CONDITION: temperature set by hand, or drug assigned by randomisation.
branches.cn: 被操纵的条件：手动设定的温度，或随机分配的药物。

branches.en: THE X: the input of a function, and the quantity read along the horizontal axis.
branches.cn: 那个 x：函数的输入，以及沿横轴读取的量。

branches.en: THE EXPLAINER: a regression predictor, or neighbourhood income expected to account for an outcome.
branches.cn: 解释者：回归中的预测变量，或被期待解释结果的社区收入。

branches.en: THE SIMULATION DIAL: the knob turned between runs to explore what the model can do.
branches.cn: 模拟的旋钮：在多次运行之间转动，以探索模型能做什么。

branches.en: THE DESIGN FACTOR: a crossed factor with three levels, or an outside oil price the model does not explain.
branches.cn: 设计因素：带三个水平的交叉因素，或模型不解释的外部油价。

intro.en: The phrase combines a Latin negative adjective with a Latin verb of changing; neither part is a technical coinage, though the pairing is modern.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁语否定形容词与表示变化的拉丁动词组合起来；两部分都不是技术造词，但这个搭配是现代产物。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is in-, dependere, pendere and variare, with varius behind the noun variable.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语成分是 in-、dependere、pendere 与 variare，名词 variable 背后还有 varius。

items.example: The adjective denies dependence rather than claiming freedom.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词否定依附，而非宣称自由。

items.example: It marks the absence of a link.
items.exampleCN: 它标出联系的缺失。

items.example: The image is a weight hanging from a hook.
items.exampleCN: 意象是重物挂在钩上。

items.example: It also lies behind pendant and pendulum.
items.exampleCN: 它也是「吊坠」与「摆锤」两词的来源。

items.example: The noun names a quantity that can take several values.
items.exampleCN: 名词指可取多个值的量。

items.example: The verb is the root of the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是名词的根。

items.example: The adjective describes what is not uniform.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述不齐一的东西。

items.example: It turns the verb into an adjective of possibility.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词变成表示可能的形容词。

items.example: The pair marks which side is moved and which is read.
items.exampleCN: 这一对词标出哪一侧被移动、哪一侧被读取。

items.example: The third term marks what is deliberately not allowed to change.
items.exampleCN: 第三个词标出被刻意不许变动的东西。

latinEntries.structure: Latin negative prefix in-, assimilated before consonants
latinEntries.example: It negates dependens, the participle behind dependent.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它否定 dependens，即 dependent 背后的分词。

latinEntries.example: Latin dependere means to hang down from something.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 dependere 意为从某物上垂下。

latinEntries.example: Latin variare means to change or make varied.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 variare 意为变化、使多样。

latinEntries.example: Latin varius means varied or mottled.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 varius 意为多样的、有斑纹的。

latinEntries.example: Latin -abilis builds adjectives such as mutabilis, changeable.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 -abilis 构成 mutabilis（可变的）这类形容词。

definition_zh: 因变量；实验中随自变量变化而被测量、被解释的结果变量
definition_en: the variable that is measured in an experiment and expected to change in response to the independent variable
core_image: 记录板上只留一列读数，每一行对应一种处理条件，最后一栏写着结果
scene: 记录板上只留一列读数，每一行对应一种处理条件。Plant height is the dependent variable here, recorded after each week of treatment.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项：实验中随自变量改变而被测量的结果变量；句意为株高在这里是因变量，每周处理后记录一次。图中可辨识物件：记录板、单列数字、处理标签、直尺。

collocations.zh: 因变量与自变量（常成对出现）
