senses.title: The outcome that is measured
senses.definition: the factor that an experimenter measures, expected to respond to changes in the independent variable
senses.definitionCN: 实验者测量的因素，预期会随自变量的变化而作出反应
senses.example: Plant height is the dependent variable here, recorded after each week of treatment.
senses.exampleCN: 株高在这里是因变量，每周处理后记录一次。
senses.why: Its value is read only after the treatment is applied, so it hangs on the factor that was moved, and that dependence is the name.
senses.whyCN: 它的值只在处理实施之后才被读出，因此取决于被移动的那个因素，这种「依从」正是名称的由来。

senses.title: The response in statistics
senses.definition: in a statistical model, the quantity whose variation the analysis tries to account for
senses.definitionCN: 在统计模型中，分析试图解释其变异的那个量
senses.example: The response was treated as the dependent variable in every model.
senses.exampleCN: 每个模型都把响应量当作因变量。
senses.why: Statistics asks what explains variation, and the variable being explained sits on the outcome side of the equation.
senses.whyCN: 统计学追问什么解释了变异，而被解释的变量就坐在方程的「结果」一侧。

senses.title: The y of a function
senses.definition: in mathematics, the output of a function, whose value is fixed once the input is chosen
senses.definitionCN: 在数学中，函数的输出，其值在输入选定后即被确定
senses.example: In the equation, the dependent variable changes when the input changes.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个方程里，输入一变，因变量就变。
senses.why: A rule assigns one output to each input, so the output depends on the input by construction.
senses.whyCN: 规则为每个输入指定一个输出，因此输出在构造上就依赖于输入。

senses.title: The outcome in social research
senses.definition: in social science, the measured condition that a study tries to explain, such as a test score or a rate
senses.definitionCN: 在社会科学中，研究试图解释的被测状态，如考试分数或比率
senses.example: The study used the graduation rate as its dependent variable.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究把毕业率作为因变量。
senses.why: When the outcome cannot be manipulated, it is still measured, and the word keeps the experimental image of reading a result.
senses.whyCN: 当结果无法被操纵时，它仍可被测量，这个词保留了「读出结果」的实验意象。

senses.title: The behaviour recorded in psychology
senses.definition: in psychology, the observed response, such as reaction time or a rating, treated as the outcome of a manipulation
senses.definitionCN: 在心理学中，被观察的反应，如反应时或评分，被视为操纵的结果
senses.example: Reaction time was the dependent variable in the attention task.
senses.exampleCN: 注意任务中的因变量是反应时。
senses.why: Behaviour is what the experiment can see, while the mental process is inferred, so the visible response becomes the measured variable.
senses.whyCN: 行为是实验看得见的东西，心理过程只能推断，因此可见的反应成了被测量的变量。

senses.title: The endpoint of a trial
senses.definition: in a clinical trial, the pre-specified outcome used to judge whether a treatment works
senses.definitionCN: 在临床试验中，用来判断治疗是否有效的预先指定结果
senses.example: The trial's dependent variable was the number of symptom-free days.
senses.exampleCN: 这项试验的因变量是无症状天数。
senses.why: A trial must name its outcome before it begins, so the measured endpoint is fixed in the protocol and called the dependent variable.
senses.whyCN: 试验必须在开始前指定结果，因此被测终点写进方案，并被称为因变量。

senses.title: The explained side of a regression
senses.definition: in regression analysis, the variable on the left of the equation, whose values the predictors are used to estimate
senses.definitionCN: 在回归分析中，方程左边的变量，其取值由预测变量来估计
senses.example: Income sat on the left as the dependent variable.
senses.exampleCN: 收入作为因变量放在左边。
senses.why: Regression draws a line from predictors to an outcome, and the outcome is dependent because the line is fitted to it.
senses.whyCN: 回归从预测变量画一条线到结果，结果之所以为因变量，是因为这条线是照着它拟合的。

senses.title: The quantity on the vertical axis
senses.definition: the quantity whose values are read up the vertical axis when a relation is graphed
senses.definitionCN: 作关系图时，其取值沿纵轴向上读取的量
senses.example: With yield as the dependent variable, the trend rises to the right.
senses.exampleCN: 以产量作因变量，趋势向右上升。
senses.why: By convention the effect is placed on the vertical axis, so the graph puts the dependent variable where the eye reads change.
senses.whyCN: 按惯例结果放在纵轴，因此图把因变量放在眼睛读取变化的位置。

senses.title: The outcome an economic model explains
senses.titleCN: 经济模型要解释的结果
senses.definition: in economics, the quantity a model seeks to account for, such as consumption responding to income
senses.definitionCN: 在经济学中，模型试图解释的量，如随收入变化的消费
senses.example: Consumption is the dependent variable, with income on the other side.
senses.exampleCN: 消费是因变量，收入在另一侧。
senses.why: A model is written to explain one quantity by others, and that quantity is dependent on the explanatory side.
senses.whyCN: 模型是为了用其他量解释某一个量，那个量就依赖于解释的一侧。

intro.en: Dependent variable joins dependent, from Latin dependere 'to hang from', to variable, from variare 'to change'. The pair with independent variable belongs to modern mathematics and experimental design.
intro.cn: dependent variable 把 dependent（拉丁语 dependere「悬挂于」）与 variable（variare「变化」）组合起来。它与自变量成对使用，属于现代数学与实验设计。

items.en: Dependere meant to hang from or be attached to, from de- 'down' and pendere 'to hang'.
items.cn: dependere 意为悬挂于、依附于，由 de-「向下」与 pendere「悬挂」构成。

items.en: Dependent entered English through French in the fifteenth century, meaning reliant on another for support.
items.cn: dependent 经法语在十五世纪进入英语，意为依靠他者供养。

items.en: Variare meant to change, from varius 'varied', and it gave the noun variable.
items.cn: variare 意为改变，出自 varius「杂色的」，由此产生名词 variable。

items.en: In the mathematics of functions, the input was called independent and the output dependent; the labels became standard in nineteenth-century algebra.
items.cn: 在函数数学中，输入被称为自变量，输出被称为因变量；这对标签在十九世纪代数中成为标准。

items.en: Laboratory and agricultural design in the later nineteenth and early twentieth centuries applied the pair to treatments and measured responses.
items.cn: 十九世纪后期至二十世纪初的实验室与农业设计，把这组词用到处理与测得反应上。

items.en: Regression, psychology and clinical trials each adopted the term for their own outcome, and the protocol fixed it in advance.
items.cn: 回归、心理学与临床试验各自采用这一术语指自己的结果，而试验方案会预先把它固定下来。

note.en: The first group shares one of the two words; the second group names the other factors of a design, with the differences spelled out.
note.cn: 第一组共享短语中的一个词；第二组是设计中的其他因素，并写明差别。

entries.definition: Reliant on something else; the adjective inside the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 依靠他物的；短语中的形容词。

entries.definition: The state of relying on another for support or value.
entries.definitionCN: 在供养或取值上依靠他者的状态。

entries.definition: A quantity that can take different values.
entries.definitionCN: 可取不同值的量。

entries.definition: To change; the verb behind the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 变化；名词背后的动词。

entries.definition: The factor that is deliberately changed, the cause side of the pair.
entries.definitionCN: 被刻意改变的因素，这一对中的原因一侧。

entries.definition: A factor held constant so it cannot explain the outcome; unlike the dependent variable, it is not measured as a result.
entries.definitionCN: 被保持恒定、因而无法解释结果的因子；与因变量不同，它不作为结果被测量。

entries.definition: The result itself, in ordinary language, without the statistical frame.
entries.definitionCN: 日常语言中的结果本身，不带统计框架。

entries.definition: What a system or subject does after a stimulus; the statistical word for the measured side.
entries.definitionCN: 系统或受试者在刺激之后的反应；统计中用来指被测的一侧。

entries.definition: The pre-declared measure of success in a trial, the clinical name for the dependent variable.
entries.definitionCN: 试验中预先声明的成功量度，是因变量的临床名称。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the hanging root, the x-and-y image, and the fixed contrast with the independent variable.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用「悬挂」词根、x 与 y 的意象，以及它与自变量的固定对照。

normal.en: Dependent is literally hanging from something: the measured outcome hangs on the factor that was changed.
normal.cn: dependent 字面是悬挂在某物上：被测结果挂在被改变的因素上。

normal.en: The family runs depend, dependent, dependence, variable, vary and variant.
normal.cn: 同族词有 depend、dependent、dependence、variable、vary 与 variant。

normal.en: In a graph the independent variable runs across and the dependent variable rises up the side.
normal.cn: 图上自变量横着走，因变量沿侧边上升。

normal.en: A trial declares its dependent variable, such as symptom-free days, before the first patient is enrolled.
normal.cn: 试验在第一位患者入组前就声明因变量，例如无症状天数。

normal.en: The pair is fixed: one factor is moved, the other is measured, and neither is held still.
normal.cn: 这一对是固定的：一个因素被移动，另一个被测量，两个都不被固定。

abstract.en: The dependent variable is the answer the experiment is allowed to give, and it must be chosen before the question is asked.
abstract.cn: 因变量是实验被允许给出的答案，而且必须在提问之前选好。

abstract.en: An outcome that nobody defined in advance can always be explained afterwards.
abstract.cn: 事先没有定义的结果，事后总能找到解释。

abstract.en: To depend is not weakness here; it is the mark of having been measured.
abstract.cn: 在这里，依赖不是软弱，而是「被测量过」的标志。

examples.en: The dependent variable was recorded at the same hour each day.
examples.cn: 因变量每天在同一时刻记录。

examples.en: A trial must state its dependent variable in the protocol.
examples.cn: 试验必须在方案中写明因变量。

examples.en: If the dependent variable is vague, the analysis cannot be repeated.
examples.cn: 如果因变量含糊，分析就无法重复。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「迪彭登特-维瑞额波」——挂在处理条件后面、等着被读出的那个结果：因变量

root: dependent 来自拉丁语 dependere「悬挂于」（de- 向下 + pendere 悬挂），经法语进入英语；variable 来自 variare「变化」。因变量与自变量成对，是十九世纪函数数学与实验设计的产物。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one measured outcome: the experimental response, the statistical response, the y of a function, a social outcome, a recorded behaviour, a trial endpoint, the left side of a regression, the vertical axis and an explained economic quantity.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟着同一个被测量的结果：实验反应、统计响应、函数中的 y、社会结果、被记录的行为、试验终点、回归左侧、纵轴，以及被解释的经济量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a board holds a single column of readings, one row per treatment, and the last row is the result.
core.cn: 核心意象：记录板上只有一列读数，每种处理一行，最后一行就是结果。

branches.en: THE MEASURED OUTCOME: weekly height, or symptom-free days declared before a trial begins.
branches.cn: 被测结果：每周的株高，或试验开始前就声明的无症状天数。

branches.en: THE RESPONSE SIDE: the variation a model explains, the quantity on the left of a regression.
branches.cn: 响应一侧：模型所解释的变异，回归方程左边的量。

branches.en: THE Y: the output fixed once the input is chosen, and the quantity rising up the vertical axis.
branches.cn: 那个 y：输入选定后被固定的输出，以及沿纵轴上升的量。

branches.en: THE EXPLAINED FACT: graduation rates in social research, consumption responding to income.
branches.cn: 被解释的事实：社会研究中的毕业率，随收入变化的消费。

branches.en: THE VISIBLE BEHAVIOUR: reaction time standing in for a mental process that cannot be seen.
branches.cn: 可见的行为：以反应时代表看不见的心理过程。

intro.en: The phrase pairs a Latin adjective of hanging with a Latin noun of change; the hyphen-free two-word unit is a modern technical name.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁语「悬挂」形容词与「变化」名词配在一起；这个不带连字符的两词单位是现代技术名称。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is dependere, pendere, variare and varius, with -abilis in the noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语成分是 dependere、pendere、variare 与 varius，名词中还有 -abilis。

items.example: The adjective describes a value that follows another.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述随另一量而定的值。

items.example: It marks the point from which something hangs.
items.exampleCN: 它标出悬挂的起点。

items.example: It also gives pendant and pendulum.
items.exampleCN: 它也是「吊坠」与「摆锤」两词的来源。

items.example: The verb joins physical hanging to logical reliance.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把物理悬挂与逻辑依赖连在一起。

items.example: The noun names a measurable quantity.
items.exampleCN: 名词指可测量的量。

items.example: The verb is the root of the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是名词的根。

items.example: It describes what is not uniform.
items.exampleCN: 它描述不齐一之物。

items.example: It builds the adjective that became the noun.
items.exampleCN: 它构成后来变作名词的形容词。

items.example: The pair splits moving from measuring.
items.exampleCN: 这一对把「移动」与「测量」分开。

items.example: The third term marks what must not move.
items.exampleCN: 第三个词标出不许变动的东西。

latinEntries.example: The compound gives English depend and dependent.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 这个复合词给出英语 depend 与 dependent。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb pendere (pend-, pensum; to hang)
latinEntries.example: Latin pendere means to hang, and gives pendant and suspend.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 pendere 意为悬挂，并给出 pendant 与 suspend。

latinEntries.example: It is the verb behind variable and variation.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它是 variable 与 variation 背后的动词。

latinEntries.example: The adjective supplies the idea of changeability.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 这个形容词提供「可变」这层意思。

latinEntries.example: It forms variabilis, the Latin adjective behind variable.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它构成 variabilis，即 variable 背后的拉丁形容词。

definition_zh: 控制变量；实验中刻意保持不变、以排除干扰的因素；对照条件
definition_en: a factor that is deliberately held constant, or a variable used to check the effect of another so that it cannot explain the result
core_image: 一整排旋钮被胶带封住，标签上写明设定值，谁都不许再动
scene: 实验开始前，技术员把湿度、光照与营养液的旋钮都封住，只在记录本上写明设定值。Room humidity is the control variable, held at the same level for every trial.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项：被刻意保持恒定、以排除干扰的因素；句意为室内湿度就是控制变量，每次试验都保持在同一水平。图中可辨识物件：封住的旋钮、胶带、设定值标签、记录本。

pos.zh: 控制变量；受控因素；对照条件（可数）

collocations.phrase: a control variable in the design

collocations.zh: 控制变量与自变量（常成对出现）

senses.title: The factor held constant
senses.definition: a factor that is fixed at one value throughout an experiment so that it cannot account for a change in the outcome
senses.definitionCN: 在整个实验中固定在一个取值、因而无法解释结果变化的因素
senses.example: Room humidity is the control variable, held at the same level for every trial.
senses.exampleCN: 室内湿度就是控制变量，每次试验都保持在同一水平。
senses.why: If a factor is allowed to drift, no one can tell whether the treatment or the drift produced the result, so it is pinned and called controlled.
senses.whyCN: 若允许某因素漂移，就分不清是处理还是漂移造成了结果，因此把它钉住，称为受控。

senses.title: The baseline for comparison
senses.definition: the condition against which a treated condition is judged, often a group given no treatment
senses.definitionCN: 用来判断处理条件的参照条件，常指未接受处理的组
senses.example: For the baseline arm the control variable was the absence of the drug.
senses.exampleCN: 基准组的控制变量就是不给药物这一条件。
senses.why: A result means little without a baseline, and the baseline is the control against which the change is read.
senses.whyCN: 没有基准的结果说明不了什么，而基准就是用来读取变化的那项对照。

senses.title: A confounder shut out
senses.definition: a factor known to affect the outcome that is neutralised by design, such as time of day or temperature
senses.definitionCN: 已知会影响结果、并通过设计被中和的因素，如一天中的时刻或温度
senses.example: Time of day was a control variable, because temperature rises with it.
senses.exampleCN: 一天中的时刻是控制变量，因为温度随它升高。
senses.why: A factor that moves with both treatment and outcome can fake a link, so the design removes its freedom to vary.
senses.whyCN: 同时随处理与结果变化的因素会伪造出联系，因此设计拿走它变化的自由。

senses.title: A covariate adjusted in analysis
senses.titleCN: 分析中加以调整的协变量
senses.definition: a variable measured and adjusted for statistically so that its influence on the outcome is removed
senses.definitionCN: 被测量并在统计上加以调整、以去除其对结果影响的自变量
senses.example: Age was entered as a control variable in the regression.
senses.exampleCN: 年龄作为控制变量进入回归。
senses.why: When a factor cannot be held fixed in the field, it can still be measured and subtracted, and analysis calls that controlling.
senses.whyCN: 某因素在野外无法固定时，仍可测量并扣除，分析工作把这一步称为控制。

senses.title: A parameter fixed in a model
senses.definition: a quantity in a model or simulation set to one value so that other effects can be examined
senses.definitionCN: 在模型或模拟中设定为某一固定值、以便考察其他效应的量
senses.example: In the simulation, gravity was a control variable set to the local value.
senses.exampleCN: 模拟中重力是控制变量，设为当地数值。
senses.why: A model with every input moving at once cannot be read, so some inputs are frozen and called controls.
senses.whyCN: 所有输入同时变化的模型读不出结果，因此有一部分输入被冻结，称为控制量。

senses.title: A loop counter in a program
senses.titleCN: 程序中的循环控制变量
senses.definition: in computing, the variable whose value decides whether a loop continues or stops
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机中，其取值决定循环继续还是停止的变量
senses.example: The loop's control variable starts at zero and rises by one.
senses.exampleCN: 循环的控制变量从零开始，每次加一。
senses.why: A repeated block of code needs one number to count its turns, and that number controls the repetition.
senses.whyCN: 重复执行的代码需要用一个数来数圈数，这个数控制重复。

senses.title: A parameter held in mathematics
senses.definition: in mathematics, a quantity treated as fixed while other variables change, so that a family of cases can be compared
senses.definitionCN: 在数学中，视作固定而让其他变量变化的量，以便比较一族情形
senses.example: Treating the radius as a control variable isolates the effect of height.
senses.exampleCN: 把半径当作控制变量，就能单独看出高度的作用。
senses.why: A quantity held fixed while others move turns a family of cases into a comparison, so it is treated as a control.
senses.whyCN: 让一个量固定、其余量变化，就把一族情形变成了可比较的实验，因此它被当作控制量。

senses.title: A standardised field condition
senses.titleCN: 野外研究中标准化的条件
senses.definition: in field research, a condition such as plot size or sampling hour kept identical across sites
senses.definitionCN: 在野外研究中，样地大小或采样时刻一类在各样点保持一致的安排
senses.example: Plot size was the control variable across all twelve sites.
senses.exampleCN: 十二个样点的控制变量都是样地面积。
senses.why: Sites differ in many ways, so researchers standardise one condition at a time and name it as controlled.
senses.whyCN: 样点在许多方面不同，研究者便逐项统一条件，并称之为受控。

senses.title: The negative comparison
senses.definition: a comparison condition in which the active element is removed, used to show that the effect is not an artefact
senses.definitionCN: 去掉有效成分的比较条件，用来表明效应并非假象
senses.example: A sham treatment served as the control variable in the device trial.
senses.exampleCN: 器械试验中，模拟处理充当控制变量。
senses.why: A device can produce an effect by being touched, so removing the active part tests whether the effect belongs to it.
senses.whyCN: 器械仅靠被触碰就可能产生效应，因此去掉有效部分，检验效应是否真属于它。

intro.en: Control variable joins control, from Medieval Latin contrarotulus 'a check roll', to variable, from variare. Control first meant checking a record against a copy, and only later came to mean command.
intro.cn: control variable 把 control（中世纪拉丁语 contrarotulus「核对用的卷册」）与 variable（variare「变化」）组合。control 最初意为拿副本核对账册，后来才转为「指挥、控制」。

items.en: Contrarotulus was a roll kept to check another roll, built from contra 'against' and rotulus 'a little roll'.
items.cn: contrarotulus 是用于核对另一卷册的副本卷，由 contra「对着」与 rotulus「小卷」构成。

items.en: Old French contrerole named the copy of a roll used to verify accounts, and English borrowed it in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 contrerole 指用来核对账目的副本卷，英语在十六世纪借入。

items.en: English control first meant to verify accounts by a duplicate, which is why the word still implies a standard held alongside the thing tested.
items.cn: 英语 control 最初意为用副本核对账目，因此这个词至今暗含「在旁边持一标准」的意思。

items.en: The sense of command or restraint grew from checking, and by the nineteenth century control meant power over a process.
items.cn: 指挥与约束之义从核对生长出来，到十九世纪 control 已指对过程的支配。

items.en: Nineteenth-century experimenters adopted control for the comparison condition, and the phrase control variable fixed the idea of a factor held still.
items.cn: 十九世纪实验者用 control 指比较条件，而 control variable 这一说法固定了「被保持不动的因素」之意。

items.en: The twentieth century added statistical adjustment for covariates and the loop control variable of programming, both keeping the idea of a quantity that governs or is governed.
items.cn: 二十世纪又加上对协变量的统计调整与编程中的循环控制变量，两者都保留「支配或被支配的量」这一意象。

note.en: The first group shares one of the two words; the second group names the other factors, with the experimental difference stated.
note.cn: 第一组共享短语中的一个词；第二组是其他因素，并写明实验中的差别。

entries.definition: To check, restrain or direct; the verb inside the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 核对、约束或指挥；短语中的动词。

entries.definition: Deliberately kept fixed or compared, as in a controlled trial.
entries.definitionCN: 被刻意固定或作比较的，如对照试验。

entries.definition: A person or device that regulates a process.
entries.definitionCN: 调节某个过程的人或装置。

entries.definition: A quantity that can take different values.
entries.definitionCN: 可取不同值的量。

entries.definition: The factor the researcher changes; a control variable is instead held still.
entries.definitionCN: 研究者主动改变的因素；控制变量则被保持不动。

entries.definition: The outcome that is measured; it is allowed to change.
entries.definitionCN: 被测量的结果；它被允许变化。

entries.definition: The comparison treatment given to a baseline group, a design element rather than a measured factor.
entries.definitionCN: 给基准组的那种比较处理，属于设计安排，而非被测因素。

entries.definition: A factor that corrupts a comparison if it is left free to vary.
entries.definitionCN: 若任其变化就会污染比较的因素。

entries.definition: A variable measured alongside the outcome and adjusted for in analysis.
entries.definitionCN: 与结果同时测量、并在分析中加以调整的变量。

entries.definition: A quantity fixed for a given model or case, the mathematical cousin of a control variable.
entries.definitionCN: 在给定模型或情形中固定的量，与控制变量在数学上相近。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the check-roll origin, the taped knobs, and the fixed contrast with the other two variables.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用「核对卷册」的词源、被封住的旋钮，以及它与另外两个变量的固定对照。

normal.en: Control came from a duplicate roll kept to check accounts, so to control a factor is to keep a standard beside it.
normal.cn: control 来自用来核对账目的副本卷，因此控制一个因素就是把它旁边的标准守住。

normal.en: The family runs control, controlled, controller, variable and vary.
normal.cn: 同族词有 control、controlled、controller、variable 与 vary。

normal.en: Three roles are fixed: the independent variable is moved, the dependent one is measured, the control one is held still.
normal.cn: 三个角色是固定的：自变量被移动，因变量被测量，控制变量被保持不动。

normal.en: Field studies standardise plot size or sampling hour and call it the control variable.
normal.cn: 野外研究统一了样地面积或采样时刻，并称之为控制变量。

normal.en: In a program the loop counter is a control variable: its value decides whether the loop runs again.
normal.cn: 程序里的循环计数器也是控制变量：它的值决定循环是否再跑。

abstract.en: A control variable is a promise not to let the world cheat on your behalf.
abstract.cn: 控制变量是一个承诺：不让世界替你作弊。

abstract.en: What is held still cannot explain the change, and that is exactly why it is held.
abstract.cn: 被固定住的东西无法解释变化，这正是它被固定的原因。

abstract.en: Control began as double-checking, and science still uses it to check itself.
abstract.cn: control 起初意为双重核对，科学至今仍用它来核对自身。

examples.en: The control variable was fixed at the level recorded on the first day.
examples.cn: 控制变量固定在第一天的记录水平。

examples.en: Researchers adjusted for age as a control variable before comparing the groups.
examples.cn: 研究者先把年龄作为控制变量加以调整，再比较两组。

examples.en: A loop needs a control variable that ends the repetition.
examples.cn: 循环需要一个能终止重复的控制变量。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「肯戳-维瑞额波」——被胶带封死、谁都不许动的那颗旋钮：控制变量

root: control 来自中世纪拉丁语 contrarotulus「核对用的副本卷」（contra 对着 + rotulus 小卷），经法语进入英语，先指核对账目，后指支配；variable 来自 variare「变化」。实验对照义见于十九世纪，统计与编程义见于二十世纪。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one sealed knob: the factor held constant, the baseline condition, a shut-out confounder, an adjusted covariate, a fixed model parameter, a loop counter, a mathematical parameter, a standardised field condition and a negative comparison.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟着同一个被封住的旋钮：被保持恒定的因素、基准条件、被隔离的混淆因素、被调整的协变量、固定的模型参数、循环计数器、数学参数、标准化的野外条件，以及反向对照。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of dials wrapped in tape, each label stating the value that no one may change.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排旋钮被胶带缠住，每张标签写明谁都不许改的数值。

branches.en: THE PINNED CONDITION: humidity sealed in the lab, plot size standardised across twelve sites.
branches.cn: 被钉住的条件：实验室里封住的湿度，十二个样点统一的样地面积。

branches.en: THE BASELINE: a briefing without the drug, against which the treated group is read.
branches.cn: 基准：不给药物的说明，用来读取处理组的变化。

branches.en: THE CONFOUNDER AND THE COVARIATE: removed by design in the lab, subtracted by statistics in the field.
branches.cn: 混淆因素与协变量：实验室里用设计移除，野外用统计划除。

branches.en: THE FROZEN NUMBER: gravity set in a simulation, the radius held while height varies.
branches.cn: 被冻结的数：模拟中设定的重力，以及高度变化时保持不动的半径。

branches.en: THE GOVERNING VARIABLE AND THE SHAM: a counter that ends a loop, a device trial with the active part removed.
branches.cn: 起支配作用的变量与假处理：终止循环的计数器，以及去掉有效部分的器械试验。

intro.en: Control variable joins a medieval checking noun to a Latin noun of change; the compound is modern technical English.
intro.cn: control variable 把中世纪表示核对的词与拉丁语表示变化的名词接在一起，是现代的英语技术复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is contrarotulus, contra, rotulus, variare and varius.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语成分是 contrarotulus、contra、rotulus、variare 与 varius。

items.example: The oldest sense is checking, not commanding.
items.exampleCN: 最古老的意思是核对，不是指挥。

items.example: It was a duplicate kept for verification.
items.exampleCN: 它是为核对而保留的副本。

items.example: It marks the copy set against the original.
items.exampleCN: 它标出对着原件的那份副本。

items.example: It also gives the English word roll.
items.exampleCN: 它也是英语中「卷册」一词的来源。

items.example: The participle marks a condition deliberately set.
items.exampleCN: 分词标出被刻意设定的条件。

items.example: The agent noun applies to people and devices.
items.exampleCN: 施事名词可用于人，也可用于装置。

items.example: The noun names a measurable quantity.
items.exampleCN: 名词指可测量的量。

items.example: The verb is the root of the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是名词的根。

items.example: It describes what is not uniform.
items.exampleCN: 它描述不齐一之物。

items.example: A factor that spoils a comparison if left free.
items.exampleCN: 任其自由就会毁掉比较的因素。

latinEntries.example: Medieval Latin contrarotulus was a check roll kept against a record.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 中世纪拉丁语 contrarotulus 指与正本对照的副本卷。

latinEntries.example: Latin contra means against, as in contra naturam.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 contra 意为对着、相反，如 contra naturam（逆自然）。

latinEntries.structure: Latin diminutive of rota (wheel); a little roll
latinEntries.example: Latin rotulus means a little roll, and gives English roll.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 rotulus 意为小卷，并给出英语 roll。

latinEntries.example: Latin variare means to change, and supplies variable.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 variare 意为变化，提供 variable 的词干。

latinEntries.example: Latin varius means varied, the state a variable measures.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 varius 意为多样的，正是变量所测量的状态。
